chapters.title: Chapter 1023
paragraphs: Huff, huff.
Footsteps climbed the steep mountain slope without a word, while clouds of white breath billowed here and there.
The Great Snow Mountain was as cold as midwinter all year round, and the air was thin. It spared no one—not even those who had come to defend this land.
If anything, these conditions might be harder on our side.
“Cough. Haa...”
Was it the altitude?
Or was Namho’s body simply getting old?
He kept coughing and struggling to catch his breath. I was about to give an order when someone reached his side ahead of me.
“Steady your breathing. Relax.”
Tap.
A hand pressed his Mingmen acupoint as a calm voice spoke. Faint qi stirred around Namho.
Whoosh.

The pallor creeping across his face eased, and his complexion regained some color. With the internal energy sent through the Mingmen acupoint, Namho looked as if nothing had happened and went back to grumbling as usual.
“Damn it. Getting old’s a crime. Anyway, thanks for the help...”
His words trailed off.
Namho had just turned to thank him when his voice faltered despite himself. Standing behind him, Sama Pyo asked with an impassive face,
“What is it? Is something wrong?”
Namho’s surprise lasted only an instant. The old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent recovered quickly.
“Hm? No, nothing’s wrong. Thought I saw something move over there.”
“Over there?”
As Sama Pyo turned to look where Namho was pointing, a small shadow sprang out from behind a dry tree and darted across the snow.
“A mountain hare. No need to worry.”
“Is that so? Well, it’s not like they could’ve snuck all the way up here. Getting old just gives you more to worry about.”
Namho replied nonchalantly, then looked at me and smacked his lips.
“Getting this winded from a little climb? I must be getting old. If I were just ten years younger—no more, no less—I’d be leading the charge. Wouldn’t you say?”
The more someone knew, the easier it was for their reaction to give them away. Namho had hidden his well enough, though. I answered evenly.
“Have you gone senile? You wouldn’t be leading the charge even if you were thirty years younger.”
I wasn’t just saying that to help us move past the moment. All around us, people were panting as they climbed the Great Snow Mountain.
Can’t be helped. We chose quantity over quality.
Gansu Province was vast, but it was still only one province. We’d managed to gather a staggering thirty thousand people by taking in all manner of riffraff.

There were boys whose upper lips had only just begun to darken, and Third Rate swordsmen who’d spent their whole lives in back alleys before growing old. Everywhere I looked, I saw people who might never have had their lives threatened—let alone killed anyone.
In the vast sea of Murim, they were small fry. Prey for the other predators.
I didn’t look down on them. I had neither the right nor the inclination. I’d been weak once myself. Even now, there were people who would consider me weak.
What worried me was that we had to face Dark Heaven’s forces with an army whose numbers had been inflated without adding much strength.
And besides...
More than half of them are from the unorthodox faction.
Someone once said it didn’t matter whether a cat was white or black, as long as it caught mice. I agreed. History had already proved the point.

The Great Faction War had been the decisive turning point that united Murim under one banner. And during the Great Cataclysm in the modern era, even the infamous Mexican drug cartels had joined the government forces to fight the monsters.
An outside enemy could turn yesterday’s foe into today’s ally.
But right now, what mattered was who had put bells on all those black cats—and what he truly intended.
The Black Night King, Sima Gong.
The biggest, strongest black cat to survive the Great Faction War. Another Alliance Leader, ruling the unorthodox Murim of today.

If he already had other plans, the crushing defeat at Dunhuang and the fall of the Kongtong Sect might be nothing more than steps in a course set long ago. At the end of it, a new Heaven called Dark Heaven would be waiting for us all.
I have to stop that. No matter what it takes.
I muttered the words inwardly and glanced behind me.
Sama Pyo, walking along in silence, caught my brief look and gave me a small nod.
He looked no different from usual. Yet just then, it felt as if a huge boulder were pressing down on one corner of my chest.
Rustle.
Dozens of jang away, the bare trees shivered all at once. A group emerged among them, hundreds of silver arrowheads glinting between the branches.
My brief alarm eased at a shout.
“Lower your bows! They’re our brothers from Gansu Murim!”
Not everyone relaxed.
“Stand by! No one lowers their guard until I give the order!”
The voice boomed. Its owner wore rough armor and had pulled his helmet low over his face. He was heavily armed.
One thought flashed through my mind.
The military.
Step, step.
Despite his heavy armor, he moved with easy grace. He covered the dozen or so jang between us at a measured pace. Sima Gong, who was leading our group, opened his mouth.
Or rather, he tried to.
The man passed Sima Gong as smoothly as water flowing downstream, fixed his gaze on me, and asked,
“May I ask your name, sir?”
“Have you no manners? Do you even know who this man is, to demand an answer from him?”
Naturally, I wasn’t the one who said that.
Before I could speak, Hyuk Mujin stepped forward, putting on airs as he raised the silver tablet in his hand—wait. When had he taken that?

“If I may introduce him, he is the Third Young Master of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, the hegemon of Shanxi Province; a Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who protects the Great Nation’s imperial family; and one personally appointed by His August Majesty the Emperor...”
“Hong Pyo, Deputy Thousand Captain of the Gansu Regional Military Commission!”
A roar swallowed Hyuk Mujin’s voice. The knees of the man, who had stood like an iron tower, bent.
Thud.
With a heavy sound, the man—Hong Pyo—knelt on one knee and gave me a crisp military salute.
“I pay my respects to the Marquis of Shangshan!”
“We pay our respects to the Marquis of Shangshan!”
Hundreds of voices rang across the cold snowfield. Only then did the soldiers lower their bows and weapons. They knelt with Hong Pyo and bowed low.
Hyuk Mujin began to tremble.
“Nngh. Ugh. Ahhh.”
“...What’s that weird noise?”
“Captain. I think I’m gonna burst.”
Burst, my ass. You lunatic.
I sighed and shook my head. Then I caught Sima Gong watching us with a peculiar look, and I smacked my lips.
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Go ahead. Let it all out.”
Hyuk Mujin’s face turned stern.
“What do you mean, let it out? It’s just a figure of speech.”
“Don’t say embarrassing things like that in front of your subordinates. You need to maintain your dignity as a marquis. Otherwise, you’ll look vulgar.”
I really wanted to kill him.
Hong Pyo, the man with the lengthy title of Deputy Thousand Captain of the Gansu Regional Military Commission, was built like a bear.
To put it kindly, he was steadfast. To put it less kindly, he was so inflexible he didn’t know when to back down.
In a word...
An unlucky Jeong Hogun, maybe.
Thinking of Thousand Captain Jeong Hogun, whom we’d had no choice but to leave behind because we were in such a hurry, Hong Pyo reminded me of him, yet was unmistakably different.
And the biggest reason I could make such a firm judgment about Hong Pyo’s character, whom I’d only met today, was probably his attitude toward Sima Gong.
“So you’re the Deputy Thousand Captain everyone’s been talking about. They say no one in the world is more meticulous than you when it comes to carrying out official business.”
Sima Gong had already been ignored once, but he addressed Hong Pyo with a gentle smile. Hong Pyo stared at him blankly for a moment, then spoke.
“Identity tablet.”
“Pardon?”
“Present your identity tablet. I’ll verify who you are, as procedure requires.”
“...You’re asking me for my identity tablet?”
Hong Pyo nodded without hesitation.
“Yes.”
“Do you not know who I am?”

“I saw you once from a distance at the City Lord’s sixtieth-birthday banquet the year before last. I asked my superior, the Regional Military Commissioner, and he told me you were the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate.”
“I see. Then you know.”

“What does that have to do with anything? That was then. This is now. My duty is to guard this stretch of roughly three hundred jang and verify the identity of anyone passing through. Nothing more. The Marquis of Shangshan has already gone through the procedure.”
Hong Pyo frowned at Sima Gong as though he were looking at a particularly strange man.
“Don’t make me ask again. I can overlook you speaking so casually to me, since you’re clearly older. But if you keep refusing, old man, you won’t like what happens.”
The air seemed to freeze, and not just because we were on the snow-covered Great Snow Mountain.
Who was Sima Gong?

He was the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, a man with enormous influence over Gansu Murim. With his standing and power, he could sit at the City Lord’s table as an equal. He had strong ties to both Murim and the government.
Hong Pyo had demanded that man’s identity tablet and called him an old man.
That alone was enough to stun everyone. Then Hong Pyo went a step further.
Swish.
“I told you. I won’t ask twice.”
He drew the iron baton from his waist. Sima Gong and everyone around him fell silent.
“Ha! Hahahaha! Yes! That’s exactly right!”
Jeok Cheongang’s laughter rang out. Holding his stomach, he guffawed as he looked at Hong Pyo.
“A man ought to carry out the duty he’s been given. Now, what was your name?”
Hong Pyo answered Jeok Cheongang’s friendly question.
“Identity tablet.”
“Have yours ready too. You’re next, old man.”
“And your travel pass. That bright red hair of yours looks suspicious from root to tip.”
Silence threatened to suffocate us all. Hyuk Mujin trembled and whispered so quietly I could barely hear him.
“Captain. I really think I’m gonna burst.”
But before I could answer, a sound echoed like a distant call from beyond the white ridge stretching far away.
Boom. Ba-boom. Booooom!
An urgent drumbeat.
The sound of the war drums shook the snow-covered mountain range.

chapters.title: Chapter 1024
paragraphs: For martial artists who lived on the edge of death, hearing was an invaluable sense.
Sound carried a great deal of meaning.

When you were facing an enemy, the whisper of a sleeve brushing past could only mean they were launching a sneak attack. And you could read someone’s state of mind from the pitch and tremor of their voice.
To a martial artist, sound was information.
And the drumbeats rolling in from far away at that very moment were no exception.
Thump. Thump-thump. Thuuump!
There was no proper rhythm, and each beat rang out at a different volume.

An image came to the middle-aged man’s mind: somewhere in the snow-covered mountains, a drummer was pounding away with all his might, looking as if half his soul had already left his body. He scratched the back of his neck.
“Did we come on a little too strong with the greeting?”
Low laughter rippled through the group at his words.
By now, they weren’t the only ones who knew that the hundred scouts from the Great Snow Mountain they had encountered nearby two hours earlier were dead.
“Can you blame them? The people they shared meals with came back as corpses overnight.”
“Those horses came back with heads dangling all over them. Looks like everyone’s scared out of their wits already, and this is only the beginning.”
“Still, we mustn’t let our guard down. We don’t know exactly how powerful the Fire King, that old monster, is...”
Boom!
A deafening whoosh swallowed the rest of the old man’s words.
Before he could finish speaking, an immense force slammed into his chest. He shot backward like a cannonball, righted himself in midair, and tried to land.
“Ugh, bleurgh!”
Blood spilled from his lips. He lost his balance and staggered.
Unable to withstand his internal injuries, he dropped to one knee. The other two elders, who had been laughing along moments ago, stared at the middle-aged man, their faces stiff.
Having felled a Supreme Peak master with a single move, the middle-aged man glanced from his hand to the fallen elder and back, looking perfectly unconcerned.
“Well, I put too much into that. Elder Three, are you all right?”
Elder Three knelt there coughing up blood. He answered between gasps.
“I’m... I’m fine.”
“I didn’t mean for it to come to that... More importantly, what do you think?”
“What... do you mean?”
The middle-aged man smiled at him.
“I’m asking how I compare to the Fire King, that old man.”

“What, you think I don’t stand a chance? Well, you don’t know much about the Fire King either, so I suppose it’s hard to answer. You said you’d only seen him once, from a distance, a long time ago. Wasn’t that right?”
He looked over the three elders in turn, smacked his lips, and muttered, “Shouldn’t have asked. You ran off like rats, so how would you know?”
Could there be a greater insult to martial artists, who were said to be made of pride and confidence instead of flesh and blood?
Yet the three old men—the Three Elders of Tianshan—could only tremble in silence.
Were they trying to suppress the rage welling up inside them?
No.
How could they suppress something that wasn’t there?
There was no anger toward the middle-aged man in their aging bodies or hearts. What bound them like chains was fear.

He’d lashed out with a killing blow without hesitation over a single word that displeased him. His expression and tone made it seem as though he were looking at ants he could crush underfoot at any moment.
The middle-aged man before them had both the strength and the right to act that way.
“Please forgive us!”
“I-It’s because we’re lacking.”
“This foolish old man misspoke. How could the Fire King possibly be a match for the Demon Lord?”
The three fiends of Tianshan, who had once drenched the Central Plains in blood beneath the Demonic Cult’s banner, scrambled to prostrate themselves.
If they didn’t, they felt the middle-aged man—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—might kill them on the spot.
He looked down at them with an unmistakable sneer.
Pathetic fools. Did we really try to conquer the world with men like these?
His scorn wasn’t limited to the Three Elders of Tianshan. It was directed at the man he had once followed, the man who had been everything to him.
You were bound to fail, Cult Leader. You were only human, yet you compared yourself to Heaven.
The Heavenly Demon.
Remembering the man who had inherited that title through the generations and ruled as the king and Heaven of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord let out a hollow laugh.
Looking back now, it was laughable. He had placed his faith and loyalty in a man of that caliber.
That he had dreamed of a Demonic Path ruling the world—a feat no Heavenly Demon had achieved in a thousand years.
But things were different now.
Failure had brought him enlightenment, and he had accepted a new Heaven.
A new Heaven called the Lord of Heaven.
His true master.

The Blood-Sword Demon Lord firmly believed that the enemies drawing nearer on the Great Snow Mountain would soon serve the Lord of Heaven alongside him. Even if they refused, resisted with all their might, and chose death in the end, the outcome would be the same.
In the end, they’ll seek shelter in that person’s shadow.
Laughing softly, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord turned to look behind him.
Crunch. Crunch.
Tens of thousands of troops were marching toward the Great Snow Mountain, crushing the frost-covered plants underfoot.
At their head were seven strange figures dressed in black as pitch, and, in stark contrast, several dozen people dressed in white.
“You seem worried, so I’ll tell you one thing.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord spoke without warning, then continued slowly, addressing the Three Elders of Tianshan.
“Someone like the Fire King could never stop us.”
This wasn’t confidence. It was certainty.
Certainty in the strength they had kept hidden even when they crossed Jade Gate Pass and trampled Dunhuang, defended by the Zhongnan Sect, in a single sweep.

The Three Elders of Tianshan had an inkling of it too. Even they, fiends who had once dominated their age, sensed something ominous about those figures. Whoever they were, they were no ordinary people.
But...
What exactly are they?
He hasn’t told us their names or titles. How can he be so certain?
There’s nothing we can do. We just have to follow him.
They swallowed their questions. They didn’t dare meet his eyes.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord clicked his tongue at their bowed heads, then gave his first order on the Great Snow Mountain.
“Send them a messenger.”
“A messenger?”
“We’ve already given them a greeting. We might as well show them the mercy of offering a chance to surrender. And...”
The Three Elders waited, but he left the sentence unfinished. A faint smile crossed his face.
There’s someone I’d very much like to see, too.
He didn’t mean the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang—an old enemy who had fought on a different battlefield for a different goal.
Before the fighting truly began, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord wanted to meet not the old monster from Mount Jiuhua, but his Disciple.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
For some reason, the young colossus of the orthodox Murim had drawn the attention of his master—the Lord of Heaven—in a way the Demon Lord couldn’t understand.
From the moment he received the excessive order not to kill Taekyung even if they met, his thoughts had been fixed on him.
Let’s see if he’s worthy of that attention.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes gleamed.
A hundred.
Not one of the Great Snow Mountain’s hundred scouts had been spared.
They had set out four hours earlier to check the enemy’s movements. Now they had returned together—as heads dangling from the saddles of their horses.
“J-Junior Sister...”
“No. No!”
Cries like screams rose all around us.
Those who had lost people close to them in the scouting party poured out their grief and rage. Even the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who were used to gruesome sights, clenched their teeth.
“This...”
Someone’s lips trembled, unable to finish the thought.
But in a situation like this, someone had to keep a cool head. I examined the severed heads, then exchanged a look with Jeok Cheongang.
“You saw it?”
“Yes. Each was cut with a single stroke. And the wounds are all alike.”
“So that means...”
“One person did it. That sword technique is fearsome. I’ve seen few like it in all my years.”
Death left its mark. The cuts that had severed the scouts’ heads were so uniform and sharp they looked as though they’d been measured with a ruler.
If even Jeok Cheongang judged it that way, then it had to be a master at least comparable to one of the Ten Kings—or someone even stronger—who had slaughtered them all.
“And this...”
Jeok Cheongang stopped and frowned.
“Damn it, I can’t place it. I’m sure I’ve seen a wound like this somewhere before...”
He seemed to be searching his memory, but I quietly shook my head.
The enemy’s identity wasn’t what mattered right now.
What mattered was the horrifying number of enemies approaching in the distance, raising a vast cloud of dust.
I couldn’t make out their exact numbers yet, but even just counting those pouring down the hill toward us, there were a staggering twenty thousand.
They were still several hundred jang away. Even so, the aura and killing intent pouring from that enormous army sent the birds of the harsh Great Snow Mountain beating their wings in frantic flight.
“Damn it. It was real. What I saw was real. Those fiends made it all the way here.”
Ma Junggeol, chief of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang, had been dragged here as something of a hostage. He chewed his lip as he muttered.
In his trembling hand was a telescope—or, as they called it in Murim, a ten-li scope.
“Madness. The Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, just like I’d heard. We’re finished. It’s all over...”
“Shut your mouth, unless you want to be the first one finished.”
That was enough to silence Ma Junggeol. Hyuk Mujin snatched the scope from his hand and whispered to me.
“Captain. What do you plan to do now?”
I answered evenly.
“You know what we have to do.”

sentences.text: For martial artists who lived on the edge of death, hearing was an invaluable sense.
Sound carried a great deal of meaning.
When you were facing an enemy, the whisper of a sleeve brushing past could only mean they were launching a sneak attack.
And you could read someone’s state of mind from the pitch and tremor of their voice.
To a martial artist, sound was information.
And the drumbeats rolling in from far away at that very moment were no exception.
Thump.
Thump-thump.
Thuuump!
There was no proper rhythm, and each beat rang out at a different volume.
An image came to the middle-aged man’s mind: somewhere in the snow-covered mountains, a drummer was pounding away with all his might, looking as if half his soul had already left his body.
He scratched the back of his neck.
“Did we come on a little too strong with the greeting?”
Low laughter rippled through the group at his words.
By now, they weren’t the only ones who knew that the hundred scouts from the Great Snow Mountain they had encountered nearby two hours earlier were dead.
“Can you blame them?
The people they shared meals with came back as corpses overnight.”
“Those horses came back with heads dangling all over them.
Looks like everyone’s scared out of their wits already, and this is only the beginning.”
“Still, we mustn’t let our guard down.
We don’t know exactly how powerful the Fire King, that old monster, is...”
Boom!
A deafening whoosh swallowed the rest of the old man’s words.
Before he could finish speaking, an immense force slammed into his chest.
He shot backward like a cannonball, righted himself in midair, and tried to land.
“Ugh, bleurgh!”
Blood spilled from his lips.
He lost his balance and staggered.
Unable to withstand his internal injuries, he dropped to one knee.
The other two elders, who had been laughing along moments ago, stared at the middle-aged man, their faces stiff.
Having felled a Supreme Peak master with a single move, the middle-aged man glanced from his hand to the fallen elder and back, looking perfectly unconcerned.
“Well, I put too much into that.
Elder Three, are you all right?”
Elder Three knelt there coughing up blood.
He answered between gasps.
I’m fine.”
“I didn’t mean for it to come to that...
More importantly, what do you think?”
“What... do you mean?”
The middle-aged man smiled at him.
“I’m asking how I compare to the Fire King, that old man.”
“What, you think I don’t stand a chance?
Well, you don’t know much about the Fire King either, so I suppose it’s hard to answer.
You said you’d only seen him once, from a distance, a long time ago.
Wasn’t that right?”
He looked over the three elders in turn, smacked his lips, and muttered, “Shouldn’t have asked.
You ran off like rats, so how would you know?”
Could there be a greater insult to martial artists, who were said to be made of pride and confidence instead of flesh and blood?
Yet the three old men—the Three Elders of Tianshan—could only tremble in silence.
Were they trying to suppress the rage welling up inside them?
No.
How could they suppress something that wasn’t there?
There was no anger toward the middle-aged man in their aging bodies or hearts.
What bound them like chains was fear.
He’d lashed out with a killing blow without hesitation over a single word that displeased him.
His expression and tone made it seem as though he were looking at ants he could crush underfoot at any moment.
The middle-aged man before them had both the strength and the right to act that way.
“Please forgive us!”
“I-It’s because we’re lacking.”
“This foolish old man misspoke.
How could the Fire King possibly be a match for the Demon Lord?”
The three fiends of Tianshan, who had once drenched the Central Plains in blood beneath the Demonic Cult’s banner, scrambled to prostrate themselves.
If they didn’t, they felt the middle-aged man—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—might kill them on the spot.
He looked down at them with an unmistakable sneer.
Pathetic fools.
Did we really try to conquer the world with men like these?
His scorn wasn’t limited to the Three Elders of Tianshan.
It was directed at the man he had once followed, the man who had been everything to him.
You were bound to fail, Cult Leader.
You were only human, yet you compared yourself to Heaven.
The Heavenly Demon.
Remembering the man who had inherited that title through the generations and ruled as the king and Heaven of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord let out a hollow laugh.
Looking back now, it was laughable.
He had placed his faith and loyalty in a man of that caliber.
That he had dreamed of a Demonic Path ruling the world—a feat no Heavenly Demon had achieved in a thousand years.
But things were different now.
Failure had brought him enlightenment, and he had accepted a new Heaven.
A new Heaven called the Lord of Heaven.
His true master.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord firmly believed that the enemies drawing nearer on the Great Snow Mountain would soon serve the Lord of Heaven alongside him.
Even if they refused, resisted with all their might, and chose death in the end, the outcome would be the same.
In the end, they’ll seek shelter in that person’s shadow.
Laughing softly, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord turned to look behind him.
Crunch.
Crunch.
Tens of thousands of troops were marching toward the Great Snow Mountain, crushing the frost-covered plants underfoot.
At their head were seven strange figures dressed in black as pitch, and, in stark contrast, several dozen people dressed in white.
“You seem worried, so I’ll tell you one thing.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord spoke without warning, then continued slowly, addressing the Three Elders of Tianshan.
“Someone like the Fire King could never stop us.”
This wasn’t confidence.
It was certainty.
Certainty in the strength they had kept hidden even when they crossed Jade Gate Pass and trampled Dunhuang, defended by the Zhongnan Sect, in a single sweep.
The Three Elders of Tianshan had an inkling of it too.
Even they, fiends who had once dominated their age, sensed something ominous about those figures.
Whoever they were, they were no ordinary people.
But...
What exactly are they?
He hasn’t told us their names or titles.
How can he be so certain?
There’s nothing we can do.
We just have to follow him.
They swallowed their questions.
They didn’t dare meet his eyes.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord clicked his tongue at their bowed heads, then gave his first order on the Great Snow Mountain.
“Send them a messenger.”
“A messenger?”
“We’ve already given them a greeting.
We might as well show them the mercy of offering a chance to surrender.
And...”
The Three Elders waited, but he left the sentence unfinished.
A faint smile crossed his face.
There’s someone I’d very much like to see, too.
He didn’t mean the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang—an old enemy who had fought on a different battlefield for a different goal.
Before the fighting truly began, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord wanted to meet not the old monster from Mount Jiuhua, but his Disciple.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
For some reason, the young colossus of the orthodox Murim had drawn the attention of his master—the Lord of Heaven—in a way the Demon Lord couldn’t understand.
From the moment he received the excessive order not to kill Taekyung even if they met, his thoughts had been fixed on him.
Let’s see if he’s worthy of that attention.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes gleamed.
A hundred.
Not one of the Great Snow Mountain’s hundred scouts had been spared.
They had set out four hours earlier to check the enemy’s movements.
Now they had returned together—as heads dangling from the saddles of their horses.
“J-Junior Sister...”
“No.
No!”
Cries like screams rose all around us.
Those who had lost people close to them in the scouting party poured out their grief and rage.
Even the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who were used to gruesome sights, clenched their teeth.
“This...”
Someone’s lips trembled, unable to finish the thought.
But in a situation like this, someone had to keep a cool head.
I examined the severed heads, then exchanged a look with Jeok Cheongang.
“You saw it?”
“Yes.
Each was cut with a single stroke.
And the wounds are all alike.”
“So that means...”
“One person did it.
That sword technique is fearsome.
I’ve seen few like it in all my years.”
Death left its mark.
The cuts that had severed the scouts’ heads were so uniform and sharp they looked as though they’d been measured with a ruler.
If even Jeok Cheongang judged it that way, then it had to be a master at least comparable to one of the Ten Kings—or someone even stronger—who had slaughtered them all.

Jeok Cheongang stopped and frowned.
“Damn it, I can’t place it.
I’m sure I’ve seen a wound like this somewhere before...”
He seemed to be searching his memory, but I quietly shook my head.
The enemy’s identity wasn’t what mattered right now.
What mattered was the horrifying number of enemies approaching in the distance, raising a vast cloud of dust.

They were still several hundred jang away.

What I saw was real.
Those fiends made it all the way here.”
Ma Junggeol, chief of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang, had been dragged here as something of a hostage.
He chewed his lip as he muttered.
In his trembling hand was a telescope—or, as they called it in Murim, a ten-li scope.

The Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, just like I’d heard.
We’re finished.
It’s all over...”
“Shut your mouth, unless you want to be the first one finished.”
That was enough to silence Ma Junggeol.

chapters.title: Chapter 1025
paragraphs: There were only a dozen or so of them, yet three things made them stand out even among tens of thousands of enemies.
First, the white banner held high enough to pierce the sky.
Second, a massive black horse charging fiercely, its jet-black mane flying in stark contrast to that banner.
And third, the three old men at the front of the group.
Who are those old men?
They were too far away for even my Qi Sense to make them out. Still, I could instinctively feel that their auras were anything but ordinary.
I narrowed my eyes. By then, the group had reached the foot of the mountain, and a deep voice boomed from among them.
“You dogs of the Murim Alliance, listen!”
Backed by profound internal energy, the voice carried across the mountain range.
The old man who’d shouted had a blood-soaked shirt, though I couldn’t tell why. Jeok Cheongang looked at me and blinked.
“Goodness, how strange. I think this old man just heard a bizarre hallucination.”
“I doubt it.”
“What? Then that madman really did tell us to prostrate ourselves? And to no one else but this old man?”
“He didn’t single you out quite like that, but you do belong to the Murim Alliance at the moment.”
“I do. For now.”
“He called us dogs of the Murim Alliance, so that includes you. For now.”
“So this old man heard him correctly.”
Jeok Cheongang thought for a moment, then went on.

“Let me ask you something. When a pack of worthless mutts crawls out of nowhere and insults a Master as exalted as the heavens, how should his one and only Disciple—no, someone more or less like a Disciple—respond?”
If you’re a Disciple, you’re a Disciple. What was this “more or less like one” business?
He was still stubbornly keeping up the act. I clicked my tongue and answered with action rather than words.
Whoosh. Clack.
“H-Huh?”
Leaving the martial artist who’d suddenly been left empty-handed staring in confusion, I drew back the spear I’d borrowed from him as far as I could.
“Borrowed” wouldn’t be the right word.
I wouldn’t be able to give it back.
Swish.
My waist bent like a bow. My muscles contracted, my joints relaxed, and the movements flowed together as one.
At the far end of the direction the spearhead pointed, the group carrying the white banner continued shouting.
“If you throw down your weapons and surrender at once—!”
Whoosh!
The spear left my hand and tore through the air.
It outran even the fierce whistle of its own passage, becoming a streak of light. It reached its target in an instant.
Boom!
Bright red blood burst into the air.

The black horse, its body blown apart before it could even whinny, crumpled like a rotten tree trunk. The old man who’d been loudly spouting the most ridiculous nonsense dropped lightly to the ground.
A Supreme Peak master.
I’d suspected as much when he’d used enough internal energy to send his voice across the rugged mountain range. The old man was more than worthy of being called a superhuman.
Even at that distance, he’d evaded a spear carrying tremendous force and speed without much difficulty.
And he wasn’t the only one in the group with that level of skill.
“That’s quite a rough welcome, child.”
“Launching a preemptive attack on someone carrying a white banner? Has the code of the martial world you’ve been going on about fallen to the ground?”
The voices were low but clear.
Through the countless bare branches, the other two old men stared straight at me.
“So it’s you. That young brat we’ve heard about.”
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung, is that right?”
I put internal energy behind my answer.
“Nope.”
“Kidding. It is.”
The two old men, who’d greeted me like they knew me, looked at each other in bewilderment. So did the one whose horse I’d just taken out with a spear.
There were probably two reasons.
First, this young brat had started talking nonsense right off the bat. Maybe he’d eaten something bad.
Second, whatever that brat had been eating, he’d clearly had plenty of it. The internal energy behind his nonsense was immense.
I had no intention of explaining to those senile old men how much EXP I’d eaten by now.
I was simply curious why, after using their overwhelming forces to crush even Dunhuang, they were urging us to surrender.
First, though, I needed to know who these mutts were.
“I’ve told you who I am, so we might as well exchange names. There’s that code of the martial world you mentioned.”
The old man in the middle, his face covered in pockmarks, answered readily.
“You’ve got no manners for a brat still wet behind the ears. Fine. We’re called the Three Elders of Tianshan.”
My eyes widened.
“The Three Elders of Tianshan...!”
The second old man, fat and potbellied, nodded as if he’d expected that reaction.
“So you have heard of us.”
“Good heavens. You’re the Three Elders of Tianshan?”
At my exclamation, the third old man—clearly the lowest-ranking of the three, with a crown like a heaping bowl of rice—gave a short laugh.
“You must have heard the tales about us that have been passed down since before the Great Faction War. Are you finally ready to talk properly?”
I kept my surprised expression.
“No.”
“Don’t do something you’ll regret. Even now, you can—what?”
“I said no. I’ve never even heard that title before today. And cut the ‘Elder’ stuff.”
“What?”
“I figured if I acted surprised, you’d start blabbing on your own. Oh, have you ever heard of the Three Elders of Tianshan?”
I turned to the living Murim encyclopedia, Jeok Wiki. Before long, he answered.
“I’ve long heard that three stray dogs wander around Tianshan.”
“Ah-ha.”
“Dogs by nature, it seems. During the Great Faction War, they sided with the Demonic Cult and raised all kinds of hell in the Central Plains. This old man was itching to teach them a lesson.”
“And?”
“And what? If this old man had made up his mind, why do you think those bastards are still breathing?”
“You never met them on the battlefield.”
“Born sons of bitches, but they had good noses. They ran so damn fast I never even caught sight of their shadows.”
“Oh.”
I drew my conclusion from our brief conversation and muttered as if to myself.
With enough internal energy behind it for everyone to hear, of course.
“They were weak as shit.”
The air around us trembled.
But unlike the enemy at the foot of the mountain, whose rage was boiling hot despite being invisible, the allies lined up along the ridge reacted differently.
Who were the Three Elders of Tianshan?
Fiends from a bygone era. Supreme Peak masters who’d made their mark during the Great Faction War and struck fear into everyone.
And yet Jeok Cheongang and I looked down at them and called them nothing but a bunch of dogs. Weaklings.
Those outrageous insults and absurd antics were enough to fill our allies with both astonishment and relief.
Exactly what I was going for.
With a fierce battle ahead, I’d provoked the enemy with a few words and raised our allies’ morale at the same time.
It wouldn’t overturn our disadvantage in an instant, but momentum mattered more than anything.
Of course...
If the Lord of Heaven is here, momentum won’t mean a damn thing.
The new Heaven of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples.
Evil itself, possessed of power so immense I couldn’t begin to guess its limits.
The corner of my mouth had curled up for all to see, but the thought of that absolute being—someone I’d never once met—left a heaviness in my chest.
If someone can send the Three Elders of Tianshan as mere messengers, who the hell is leading them?
As though he’d read my mind, the pockmarked old man—apparently the eldest of the three—glared up at us, his eyes blazing, and spoke.
“There’s no need for more talk. The Demon Lord wishes to see you.”
“...What?”
The Demon Lord?
I frowned and exchanged glances with Jeok Cheongang and the other leaders.
As everyone here knew, all those who could be called Demon Lords were dead.
The three Demon Lords of the East, West, and North, and even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, who had finally met her end at the Nanman Beast Palace.
But there’s another Demon Lord left?
Had these bastards come up with something tacky and ridiculous, like the East-West Demon Lord or the Northwest Demon Empress?
Then someone came to mind.
Could it be the Blood Lord?
Had he filled the vacancy left by a coworker who’d been marked dead on the job?
Before the leaders could begin whispering about the enemy commander’s identity, another shout rang out from the foot of the mountain.
“The Demon Lord says your safety will be guaranteed if you accept this offer!”
Dark Heaven was guaranteeing our safety?
That was obviously complete bullshit.
The leaders laughed at the ridiculous claim, and so did I.
Then, at a gesture from the Three Elders, one of the Dark Heaven martial artists following them took something from his saddle and handed it over.
Whoosh. Thud.
It flew high and landed halfway up the mountain. Our allies carried it straight to the leaders. Before I opened the large, blood-soaked bundle, I knew what was inside.
No—we all did.
Thump. Thump-thump.
Dozens of severed heads rolled down with heavy thuds. Groans rose from all around us. Among them, Sima Gong recognized a familiar face and murmured,
“The Kongtong Sword Dragon.”
I’d never seen him, but I’d heard the title.
A direct Disciple of the Kongtong Sect Leader and one of the greatest young prodigies in the Central Plains, known as one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
And the very man said to have escaped Dunhuang alive with his Master, the Sect Leader.
“T-the two Perfected Ones who served as Elders are here, too.”
“The Guardian Court Chief has also met his end. How could this have happened...?”
Those already believed dead were among the heads. So were people we’d been told had survived.
The core leadership of the Kongtong Sect had come back to us as severed heads.
“Then could it be...”
I couldn’t finish. Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord shook his head gravely.
“Fortunately, it seems the Sect Leader escaped their grasp. Though I don’t know if we should call that fortunate.”
The fighting at Dunhuang hadn’t been the end.
There had been a relentless pursuit, and a horrific slaughter.
And now, for some reason, a new Demon Lord we’d never heard of wanted to see us. He’d even sent the Three Elders of Tianshan to back his demand with a threat.
“A shame you’re so far away. If you were closer, I could see your faces properly.”
The three old men, furious only moments ago, went on with a cackling laugh.
“You don’t think this is all, do you? Hm?”
Jeok Cheongang spoke in a low voice.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
Perhaps some old fear had surfaced. The Three Elders of Tianshan flinched at Jeok Cheongang’s presence, but soon answered, putting even more force into their voices.
“A thousand. We still have another thousand prisoners.”
“If you accept the offer you made earlier, we’re willing to return some of them.”
My mouth went dry. My stomach twisted as I asked,
“And if we refuse?”
The three sons of bitches laughed aloud.
“Want to find out?”
Damn it.
That all but decided my answer.

With a fierce battle ahead, I’d provoked the enemy with a few words and raised our allies’ morale at the same time.
It wouldn’t overturn our disadvantage in an instant, but momentum mattered more than anything.
Of course...
If the Lord of Heaven is here, momentum won’t mean a damn thing.
The new Heaven of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples.
Evil itself, possessed of power so immense I couldn’t begin to guess its limits.
The corner of my mouth had curled up for all to see, but the thought of that absolute being—someone I’d never once met—left a heaviness in my chest.
If someone can send the Three Elders of Tianshan as mere messengers, who the hell is leading them?
As though he’d read my mind, the pockmarked old man—apparently the eldest of the three—glared up at us, his eyes blazing, and spoke.
“There’s no need for more talk.
The Demon Lord wishes to see you.”
“...What?”
The Demon Lord?
I frowned and exchanged glances with Jeok Cheongang and the other leaders.
As everyone here knew, all those who could be called Demon Lords were dead.
The three Demon Lords of the East, West, and North, and even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, who had finally met her end at the Nanman Beast Palace.
But there’s another Demon Lord left?
Had these bastards come up with something tacky and ridiculous, like the East-West Demon Lord or the Northwest Demon Empress?
Then someone came to mind.
Could it be the Blood Lord?
Had he filled the vacancy left by a coworker who’d been marked dead on the job?
Before the leaders could begin whispering about the enemy commander’s identity, another shout rang out from the foot of the mountain.
“The Demon Lord says your safety will be guaranteed if you accept this offer!”
Dark Heaven was guaranteeing our safety?
That was obviously complete bullshit.
The leaders laughed at the ridiculous claim, and so did I.
Then, at a gesture from the Three Elders, one of the Dark Heaven martial artists following them took something from his saddle and handed it over.
Whoosh.
Thud.
It flew high and landed halfway up the mountain.
Our allies carried it straight to the leaders.
Before I opened the large, blood-soaked bundle, I knew what was inside.
No—we all did.
Thump.
Thump-thump.
Dozens of severed heads rolled down with heavy thuds.
Groans rose from all around us.
Among them, Sima Gong recognized a familiar face and murmured,
“The Kongtong Sword Dragon.”
I’d never seen him, but I’d heard the title.
A direct Disciple of the Kongtong Sect Leader and one of the greatest young prodigies in the Central Plains, known as one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
And the very man said to have escaped Dunhuang alive with his Master, the Sect Leader.
“T-the two Perfected Ones who served as Elders are here, too.”
“The Guardian Court Chief has also met his end.
How could this have happened...?”
Those already believed dead were among the heads.
So were people we’d been told had survived.
The core leadership of the Kongtong Sect had come back to us as severed heads.
“Then could it be...”
I couldn’t finish.
Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord shook his head gravely.
“Fortunately, it seems the Sect Leader escaped their grasp.
Though I don’t know if we should call that fortunate.”
The fighting at Dunhuang hadn’t been the end.
There had been a relentless pursuit, and a horrific slaughter.
And now, for some reason, a new Demon Lord we’d never heard of wanted to see us.
He’d even sent the Three Elders of Tianshan to back his demand with a threat.
“A shame you’re so far away.
If you were closer, I could see your faces properly.”
The three old men, furious only moments ago, went on with a cackling laugh.
“You don’t think this is all, do you?
Hm?”
Jeok Cheongang spoke in a low voice.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
Perhaps some old fear had surfaced.
The Three Elders of Tianshan flinched at Jeok Cheongang’s presence, but soon answered, putting even more force into their voices.
“A thousand.
We still have another thousand prisoners.”
“If you accept the offer you made earlier, we’re willing to return some of them.”
My mouth went dry.
My stomach twisted as I asked,
“And if we refuse?”
The three sons of bitches laughed aloud.
“Want to find out?”
Damn it.
That all but decided my answer.

chapters.title: Chapter 1026
paragraphs: Their offer was simple.
First, we would meet halfway in half an hour, unarmed.
Second, no more than three people could attend.
And third...
One of those three had to be the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
I was watching the Three Elders of Tianshan ride away, going over the terms I’d just heard, when Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“You’re staying behind.”
His voice was firm. He looked at me, his face set, and continued.
“Not this time.”
I shrugged.
“That’s not quite what I was going to say, but close enough.”
“What are you talking about?”
“I was about to say something similar. I think I have to go this time.”
There was no other choice.
A thousand people.
The bastards had wagered a thousand lives without hesitation. This wasn’t some empty bluff to lure us down from the Great Snow Mountain.
Even now, a long line of prisoners, looking battered and miserable, was appearing on the distant hillside, bound together.
They had to be people captured at Dunhuang, or people who’d fled only to be hunted down.
“You see them, right?”
Jeok Cheongang didn’t answer. I went on.
“Not ten. Not a hundred. A thousand. We don’t have a choice.”
Before leaving, those three bastard dogs who’d spent their lives as outlaws had delivered a stern warning, as if they were judges handing down a sentence.
If we broke even one of their conditions, they would kill every last prisoner.
And I didn’t want those people sentenced to death.
“Honestly, I’m pretty damn scared too, but what can you do? I don’t know how much longer I’ll live, but... if I don’t want to spend the rest of it losing sleep, I have to go.”
Half joke, half serious.
When will the nightmares stop?
I pushed the thought aside and made myself smile. Jeok Cheongang, who had been silent for a long while, finally sighed.
“You foolish brat.”
“Hey, what’s that for? You should be cursing those bastards, not me. Shameless pricks. They won big, then went and chased everyone down too.”
“Don’t pretend to be cheerful. It doesn’t suit you.”
“Is it that obvious?”
“You’re more shameless than anyone under heaven, yet you’ve never been any good at lying.”
“...I guess not.”
“Even if there were only ten prisoners instead of ten thousand or a thousand, you’d go. That’s the kind of person you are, as far as this old man knows.”
Would I?
I didn’t know. It was hard to be certain about something that hadn’t happened.
But... yeah. I probably would.
And I thought Jeok Cheongang was that kind of person, too.
“You’re going, right? Even if I try to stop you?”
“Were you planning to?”
“No.”
I grew serious.
“If things go wrong, we could be dead in a flash. I need you beside me, Old Master.”
Only then did Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh.
“So we die together?”
“Why put it like that? I mean we live together.”
“Isn’t that the same thing?”
“Of course not. One word can make all the difference. How could you say that? Keep it up and you’ll hurt my feelings. Can’t you feel my trust, hope, and love for you?”
“You never run out of words when you start wagging that tongue. But...”
His amusement faded, and his voice dropped.
“Do you think those men share that trust you’re talking about?”
Instead of answering, I looked where he was looking.
The men in question—the leaders—had finished their deliberations and were approaching from some distance away.
Squish. Squish.
Dozens of feet crossed ground turned to mud by snow and rain.
At their head was one man.
The Black Night King, Sima Gong.
“Have you made up your mind?”
For a moment, I stared at Sima Gong as he got straight to the point.
Then I answered.
“I made up my mind a while ago. And so did the old—my Master here.”
“You understand how dangerous this could be?”
“Of course.”
“Be careful. If they can draw in a major piece with just a thousand prisoners, it will be the best possible outcome for them.”
He was right about that.
As much as I hated to say it, Jeok Cheongang and I had to be Dark Heaven’s highest-priority targets. After all the damage we’d done, they must have wanted nothing more than to tear us apart.
But...
Just a thousand, huh.
No matter how you looked at it...
How could you talk so lightly about the immense weight of so many lives?
And how much did the outcome Dark Heaven wanted resemble the picture you were trying to paint? How sincere was that warning to be careful?
I swallowed the words circling the tip of my tongue. Then four characters suddenly came to mind, and I blurted them out.
“A large group doesn’t die easily.”
“A large group doesn’t die easily... I see. If you and Senior Jeok go, you should be able to return safely even if it’s a trap.”
Sima Gong murmured the old Go proverb to himself, then nodded.
“I understand what you and Senior Jeok have decided.”
We’d given them our answer. Now it was time to hear theirs.
“Then who’s the third person?”
Three people could attend. Jeok Cheongang and I were settled, leaving one place open.
What happened next was more or less what I’d expected.
“I’ll go. As Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, I’m willing to—”
“No. I’ll go.”
The two spoke almost at once.
Like a couple of middle-aged men arguing over who got to pay the bill at a bar, Sima Gong and the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord each tried to stop the other.
“We don’t know what danger awaits us. Sect Leader, you should remain here.”
“Then all the more reason for me to go. By that reasoning, I’m better suited to it than Sect Leader Sima.”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had a point. Choosing him for the last place was the sensible decision.

Sima Gong wasn’t merely the leader of a sect. He was the beginning and end of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, the heart of the Gansu Murim world. If something happened to him, the Black Dragon Demon Gate—no, the entire Gansu force, which made up more than half our army—would be thrown into disarray.

The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, on the other hand, had two Senior Brothers who could take his place as head of the Zhongnan Sect. Whatever their faults as people, the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword had enough influence within the sect.
Given the danger and the importance of the positions they held, sending the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord was the lower-risk choice.
Of course...
Only if you’re sure the person left behind is an ally you can trust completely.
It might be the sensible decision, but if common sense ruled the world, why would we be here?
Sometimes the world changed because of a tiny handful of madmen. For better or worse.
And one of those madmen might seize control of our rear while Jeok Cheongang, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, and I are gone.
But I couldn’t argue against the decision on the strength of a suspicion I couldn’t prove. Nor did we have time.
We’re running out of it.
More than half of the promised half hour had already passed.
I quietly met Jeok Cheongang’s eyes and knew we were thinking the same thing.
If those are the choices...

The two of us should go alone. Sima Gong was someone we couldn’t fully trust whether he came with us or stayed behind. That made it all the more important for the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord to remain here.
I was about to tell everyone.
Or rather, I would have—if someone no one expected hadn’t spoken first.
Step.
“Forgive me for speaking out of turn, but may I ask you both to yield the place to me?”
I saw it clearly: as his son stepped forward, his footsteps ringing unusually loud, his father’s eyes sank into a deep, dark gaze.
“Please give me the last place.”
Sama Pyo repeated himself, his voice clear enough for everyone to hear.
“I’ll go. Myself.”
Why?
Why had it turned out this way?
I didn’t know. For the moment, all that mattered was that I was walking between Jeok Cheongang and Sama Pyo.
But my patience was just a little too thin to keep the questions building inside me to myself.
“Why’d you do it?”
I kept my gaze straight ahead. After a moment, Sama Pyo answered quietly.
“I don’t know what you mean.”
“Why’d you suddenly volunteer? It was pretty much decided.”
“If it had been decided, I wouldn’t be here. Would I?”
I frowned.
“Well...”
“No one wants to walk willingly into a place that might be a death trap. Not even the Sect Leader of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, however highly he values honor.”
Sama Pyo continued evenly.
“And his disciples would do whatever they could to keep their Sect Leader from going. Wouldn’t they, Pavilion Master?”
I couldn’t argue. He wasn’t speculating. He was describing what had happened moments ago.

When Sama Pyo stepped forward at just the right time, the Zhongnan disciples had looked relieved and done everything they could to dissuade their Sect Leader. The leaders of the Gansu Murim forces had taken their chance, too, grabbing at Sima Gong’s sleeves.
If everyone left, who would be in command if something happened?
What would happen to all these people?

Sama Pyo was both the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate and a member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion. He had grounds to dissuade the leaders and the standing to volunteer himself. Perhaps that was why everyone had accepted the young man’s sudden offer without much fuss.
Put in modern terms, the situation had fallen into place rather neatly.
While everyone had been trying to read each other’s faces, waiting to see which leader would be left holding the bag, Sama Pyo had scratched exactly the itch they all had.
Our people already knew trying to stop us wouldn’t do a damn thing.
The other Fire Dragon Pavilion members who were staying behind hadn’t tried to dissuade us either. They’d simply told us to come back safely.
Anyway, everyone had gotten what they wanted.
Well, maybe not everyone.
Sima Gong.
What had gone through his mind when his son stepped forward? Had that look in his eyes been part of a plan, or had Sama Pyo caught him off guard?
And...
What the hell was Sama Pyo thinking?
He still hadn’t answered my question. Instead, he brought up something that seemed to have nothing to do with it.
“By the way, I didn’t know you knew Go.”
“What?”
“You said it earlier, Pavilion Master. ‘A large group doesn’t die easily.’”
Was he changing the subject, or trying to tell me something? I couldn’t tell.
“I don’t know much about Go. I just picked up a few things watching and listening when I was little.”
“When you were little...”
“My dad liked Go.”
“I see. I’ve heard a little about the Strange Hero of Shanxi, your Family Head.”
“I haven’t seen him in a long time, but I still remember him clearly.”
Sima Gong would have no idea who I meant.
In this second world, I’d found brothers who weren’t related to me by blood. I’d made new companions and friends, and met a Master. But I’d only ever had one father.

Whenever he lost a game of online Go, he’d console himself by insisting those Chinese bastards must have used a cheating program. He’d also poured all his money into the stock of a certain major Korean electronics company, chanting that a large group didn’t die easily.
That was Dad.
“Dad, why is the whole computer screen blue?”
“Son, what color is the sky?”
“Red.”
“No, that’s the sunset. The sky is usually blue. My stock’s only blue for a little while too.”
“Really? So it’ll turn red soon?”
“Of course. This stock is a daema.”
“Daema? Isn’t that bad? The stuff that makes you feel good?”

“What on earth are you doing at kindergarten... No. Anyway, not that kind of daema. This means something really big and strong. And something this big and strong doesn’t die easily. In Go, we say a large group doesn’t die easily.”
“Oh.”
“Before long, that line on the screen will shoot right up. High into the sky, red like the sunset.”
“Hmm. Okay. But, Dad.”
“Yeah?”
“Look at Mom’s face. It’s really red!”
“...Honey, when did you get here?”
A quiet laugh escaped me.
I knew I shouldn’t laugh at a time like this, but I couldn’t hide the smile creeping onto my lips.
“It’s nothing. I just... remembered something nice from a long time ago.”
“A nice memory with your father.”
Sama Pyo murmured as if to himself, then smiled along with me.
“I see.”
His smile was dim and bitter, like the clouded sky. The sight of it gave me a strange sense of déjà vu.
Then Jeok Cheongang, who had been walking silently ahead of us, spoke.
“If you two are done laughing and chatting, it’s time to greet our unwelcome guest.”
At that moment, hoofbeats sounded.
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.
With the slow sound of approaching hooves, they finally appeared.
No—not they.
He did.

His smile was dim and bitter, like the clouded sky.
The sight of it gave me a strange sense of déjà vu.
Then Jeok Cheongang, who had been walking silently ahead of us, spoke.
“If you two are done laughing and chatting, it’s time to greet our unwelcome guest.”
At that moment, hoofbeats sounded.
Clip-clop.
Clip-clop.
With the slow sound of approaching hooves, they finally appeared.
No—not they.
He did.

chapters.title: Chapter 1027
paragraphs: Some people stand out.
Like an awl poking through a pocket. Like a reef rising from the middle of the sea. Like a wildflower in the wilderness.
The man approaching now, as leisurely as if he were admiring the scenery, was one of them.
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.
Gray hair swayed to the slow rhythm of his horse’s hooves.
The middle-aged man’s features were ordinary—neither particularly handsome nor ugly—but his pupils were long, vertical slits.
What truly set him apart, though, was the blood-red light in his eyes. Redder than flame, and far more chilling.
“This is the first time we’ve met face-to-face. Good to see you, Senior Jeok.”
A respectful address, delivered with a smile in his voice.
That was when Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened. The middle-aged man had stopped over ten jang away, and Jeok was staring at his reptilian pupils.
“You can’t be...”
“We were both too busy to meet the last time. What a shame. If you’d been there, Goyangcheon would still be alive and well by now. Don’t you think?”
Goyangcheon.
I remembered the name from something Jeok Cheongang had told me.
He had been the Family Head of the Goyang Family, which once wielded power to rival the Five Great Families. Or rather, he had been its last survivor.

After the Demonic Cult wiped out his family, Goyangcheon became a man consumed by revenge. The world called him the Spear King. Near the end of the Great Faction War, that great martial artist was found in an unnamed field.
He had been cut into dozens of pieces, together with the spear he’d treated as an extension of himself all his life.
Not by a hundred men, or a thousand. By one person.
A killer who craved blood more than anyone else in the Demonic Cult.
“The Blood-Sword Demon Lord...”
The name escaped me in a low groan. The middle-aged man—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—broke into a wide smile.
The infirmities of old age are a frightening thing.
Like a thief slipping in under cover of night, they steal your memories one by one.
That was why, during our stay at Mount Jiuhua, I’d deliberately pestered Jeok Cheongang with questions about his past.
I hoped it might slow his illness, even a little. Hold off the curse of time for even fifteen minutes.
As it turned out, the arrangement was pretty good for both of us.

The old man, who’d been living alone with no one to talk to, recovered forgotten memories through our countless conversations. And the young man keeping him company learned all sorts of things from a veteran of the martial world who’d lived for more than a hundred years.
One of those things concerned the killer now smiling at me.
“I’m glad. You know who I am.”
The System I had couldn’t read minds.
But I could feel it instinctively.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord wasn’t just saying he was glad I knew him. He genuinely was.
There was a childlike innocence to his delight.
That feeling was far too pure for a murderer responsible for so much bloodshed. It made him all the more unsettling.
“I used to be a pretty big deal, you know. These friends here were fairly famous themselves, but to the Demonic Cult, they were only useful guests.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord beamed as he spoke. The Three Elders of Tianshan might have taken offense, but they only nodded, their faces stiff.
“Y-you are right a hundred times over. A thousand times.”
“How could we ever presume to compare ourselves to the Demon Lord?”
“Though we are utterly lacking, being allowed to serve the Demon Lord is the honor of a lifetime.”
They were remarkably good at kissing the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s ass on cue. I wanted to ask how many times a day they brushed their teeth, but from their perspective, it made sense.
The weak fall to the strong. Might Makes Right.
Those called demonic martial artists pursued strength more openly than anyone, and the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was a great fiend beyond comparison to the Three Elders of Tianshan.
Of course, by the world’s standards, the Three Elders were great fiends too. Their martial prowess and the infamy they’d earned during the Great Faction War were more than enough to justify the name.
But as Jeok Cheongang had told them to their faces half an hour ago, they were stray dogs by birth.
They were simply far more ferocious than other dogs, with sharper, stronger teeth.

Still, there was no comparing them to the one mad dog who stood out even among that insane cult of fanatics, a group that had stood shoulder to shoulder with the Murim world for more than a thousand years.
Of course, its rabid dog seemed to have a new master now.
“The Demonic Cult? Shouldn’t you call it the Divine Cult?”
At my sudden question, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord smiled. He’d just called the Three Elders guests of the Demonic Cult himself.
“That was a long time ago. You know that already, so why ask?”
“So, now that you’ve changed collars, are they feeding you on time?”
“Well.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord opened his eyes wide in mock surprise and turned to Jeok Cheongang.
“Senior Jeok, how did you teach your Disciple? Even if we’re on different paths, shouldn’t we show each other some courtesy? Like I do.”
Jeok Cheongang answered calmly.
“I taught him better than your parents taught you, so don’t worry.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at him for a moment, then roared with laughter.
“Well, well. You’re just as the rumors say.”
“And you’re worse. I regret not catching you and killing you long ago.”
“I know that fiery temper of yours, Senior. Whenever you appeared on a battlefield, useful men died left and right. The Cult Leader was furious more times than I can count.”
“That must have made things hard for you. Weren’t you the Heavenly Demon’s favorite guard dog, the one he kept closest?”
“Sorry to disappoint you, but I didn’t have much trouble. I just killed as many as were dying.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord went on, laughter still in his voice.
“When Heaven-Poison, that foolish old man, died, the Sect Leader of Hainan wasn’t enough. I had to bring back the Spear King’s head too. But what could I do? I wanted to do it.”
“Heaven-Poison? You mean the Heaven-Poison Demon Lord?”
“Well, was there another Heaven-Poison?”
I knew that title too.

Second only to the Heavenly Demon in the Demonic Cult, the Heaven-Poison Demon Lord had been a wall even Poison King Tang Taesang could not overcome. Tang Taesang, the former Grand Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, was dead now too.
Then one day, the Heaven-Poison Demon Lord encountered disciples of Huashan on a battlefield. He died there.
Someone had unleashed a brilliant purple Sword Force, radiant enough to overwhelm the sunset.

“The Sword Saint—though I suppose I should call him the Alliance Leader now? In any case, I was secretly grateful to Mae Jonghak. That old Heaven-Poison always looked at me strangely. Luckily, he died before it was too late, and things worked out well.”
I watched the Blood-Sword Demon Lord chatter away, plainly delighted with himself. His last remark made me frown.
Things worked out well because he died?
Losing a master meant losing a vital part of your fighting strength. The Heaven-Poison Demon Lord’s death must have been a tremendous blow to the Demonic Cult.
And yet...
“So that’s when you changed collars.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s brow furrowed.
“‘Changed collars’ is a bit much... But think what you like.”
I already knew Dark Heaven had appeared before the Great Faction War ended.
The Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, Baeksang of the Nanman Beast Palace, and even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who’d been the Emperor’s closest confidant...
If you traced things back far enough, Dark Heaven had been taking shape from the very beginning of the Great Faction War.
No. Perhaps...
Dark Heaven might have caused the Great Faction War in the first place.
A chill ran down my spine. I looked at the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
“When did it start?”
“When did what start? I’m not sure what you mean.”
“When you people appeared. When the Lord of Heaven appeared.”
In that instant—
Whoosh!
Wind roared around us, a violent storm of qi.
The snow and frost covering the ground, and the dirt and sand hidden beneath them, flew in every direction before swiftly settling again.
Rustle.
As the debris of nature drifted back down, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at me with a cold, sunken gaze.
“You really have no manners.”
The smile had vanished from his lips. His voice was low.
He sounded calm at first, but cold lava flowed beneath the words.
“How strange. I can understand you to a point, and yet I simply can’t understand you at all. Why would that person go out of their way to...”
He broke off. Then his face opened into a good-natured smile.
“Well, there must be a reason for everything that person does. As always. I only wanted to confirm one thing.”
I didn’t need to ask what.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord slowly raised a hand and continued.

“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. You’re strong. Strong enough that even I’d rather avoid a bloody fight with you. Strong enough that I worry you might commit the blasphemy of defeating that person.”
I could see his eyes on me. Hear his voice.
And I could feel the pure admiration in them.
Along with...
The faint killing intent hidden beneath it.
“Your limitless potential and your sense of justice have moved me. I mean that.”
It happened in an instant.
Jeok Cheongang and I sprang forward. So did Sama Pyo, who had stood silently by until then.
The order and timing of our push off the ground and our charge differed, but the desperation driving us was probably the same.
Crack.
Our toes gouged the earth. Sand crumbled.
Internal energy surged from my dantian into the muscles of my tensed lower body, then exploded.
Boom!
The world slowed. The scenery shifted.
We shot forward, closing the distance of over ten jang.
In that moment, Jeok Cheongang and I were two fierce streaks of flame. Sama Pyo was a silent wind.
And in the slowed flow of time, three walls rose to block the flames and the wind.
“Ha!”
Three voices. One shout.
The Three Elders of Tianshan.
The three fiends of Tianshan unleashed their pent-up fury and energy, wielding a power too great for anyone to dismiss them as mere stray dogs.
A coordinated technique, honed over ages of working together, merged the three walls into one enormous barrier.
Boom!
A single clash shook heaven and earth.
Amid that tremendous roar and the rippling waves of power that filled a time already split into fragments, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s hand, raised toward the sky, finally came down.
Like countless blades waiting on a hillside for a single command.
“Slash!”
Shhk! Thk-thk-thk!
As a thousand or so heads rolled to the ground, my eyes met the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s. The blood in my body went cold.
He was smiling.

chapters.title: Chapter 1028
paragraphs: At that moment, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was smiling.
Pure delight and excitement filled his crescent-shaped eyes. His long, vertically slit pupils trembled with anticipation for what was to come.
More precisely, with anticipation for one young man.
Yes. That’s it. That’s exactly the look.
Watching Jin Taekyung’s eyes widen with shock and fury, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord felt his heart pound.
He had erased a thousand lives with a single gesture, yet he paid them no mind. All his senses were fixed on Jin Taekyung.
He felt not the slightest guilt for the dead, nor the slightest remorse for breaking his promise.
He had been born and raised in the Demonic Cult.

The cruelty he’d possessed since his mother’s womb had blossomed through the demonic martial arts he’d learned from the time he could walk. Even among the twenty-four great fiends who served the Heavenly Demon, no one could match him.
Now, Jin Taekyung was the only thing that interested him.
The Divine Dragon of the Central Plains Murim, a rising star whom his master was watching closely.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord wanted to see everything about that young brat.
He wanted to feel the full extent of the martial prowess unleashed at his fingertips, the emotions pouring out of him, the something special hidden within.
Show me. Hurry!
And just as the Blood-Sword Demon Lord cried out in his heart—
Whooosh!
An immense, unprecedented energy surged up around one man.
“Who should I kill first?”
Jin Taekyung.
At the sight of the cold flames pouring from the young man’s eyes, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s smile deepened.
The Three Elders of Tianshan’s first reaction was suspicion.
Jin Taekyung held a spear that hadn’t been there moments ago.
How?
The promise had come to nothing now, but one of the terms of their meeting had been to come unarmed. Jin Taekyung’s side had honored that condition.
They had all arrived empty-handed, a considerable comfort to the Three Elders of Tianshan.
If they could handle the terrifying old monster called the Fire King, two weaponless young brats shouldn’t be much trouble.
Even if one of them was the renowned Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, the three elders were fiends of a bygone age whose infamy had spread from Tianshan to the Central Plains.
As far as they were concerned, it was a fight they could win.
At least, until a spear appeared in Jin Taekyung’s hand.
Until an immense power, far beyond anything they had expected, enveloped that divine weapon, clearly made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Hummm.
The dazzling white spearhead trembled.
No—the air around it shuddered in tiny ripples.
At the same time, an immense, pure energy surged up and wrapped around the spearhead. It was far too vast to be contained in the body of a young man who had turned twenty only a few years ago.
Ssssss.
What people called Force was no longer a dazzling blue-white.
This is...
The three old men caught their breath without realizing it.
What could they even call this power?
The Force gathered at the spearhead was dark as the deep sea. It burned blue like fire at its fiercest, yet also flashed like a thunderbolt.
It’s different.
The Three Elders of Tianshan felt it instinctively.
That energy was of a different kind, a different order, from the energy they had cultivated all their lives.
But they had no way of knowing what it truly was.
They did not know that the strange familiarity they felt came from the internal energy Jin Taekyung had received from the Heavenly Power Demon.
They did not know that the ominous power born of demonic martial arts had finally become one with the Fire Gate Clan’s hellfire and the Hebei Peng Family’s thunderbolt.
Nor did they know just how immense and keen the power within that dark-blue streak of light was.
The one person who understood all of it better than anyone stood beside Jin Taekyung.
Ah.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, watched Jin Taekyung, his gaze deep and still.
He had suspected as much. He simply hadn’t confirmed it with his own eyes.
The summit of martial mastery.
The young man had reached the highest peak, one that touched the heavens. Age and experience were no longer measures by which to judge him.
He was a great martial artist who had forged a path of his own, one no one else had walked before.
Jeok Cheongang wanted to ask him, in all sincerity:
Do you know how remarkable the realm you’ve reached is?
And he wanted to tell him:
Across the Central Plains Murim, people gave those who reached such a realm a name spoken with the deepest respect.
The Ten Kings.
A vast, boundless sky and three stars.
Beneath them had stood ten giants.
And today, here and now, Jin Taekyung was proving himself the eleventh.
But he was different from those who had fallen to the passage of time or collapsed beneath their enemies’ cold-blue blades, spilling their blood. He was a hero of a new age.
On this battlefield, where a thousand lives had been extinguished, an immense blaze was rising.
How dazzling you are.
A shiver ran down Jeok Cheongang’s spine.
Then he looked at the Three Elders of Tianshan, staring at Jin Taekyung in a daze, and saw the shadow of death slowly falling over them.
“Old Master.”
A quiet call, seething with pain at having failed to prevent so many deaths—and with the fury that pain had bred.
Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“Do as you’ve decided.”
They didn’t know those few, cryptic words were the trust and encouragement of a master to his Disciple, who was willing to risk his life.
Nor did they know that the brief exchange had sealed their fate.
Whoosh!
A sharp gust of wind swept through.
A dark-blue flash—impossible to tell whether it was flame, wave, or thunderbolt—distorted space as it rushed at them, impossibly fast and carrying tremendous force.
Slash!
Goose bumps rose across the First Elder’s body. He twisted aside on instinct, but blood and terrible pain spread along the path of the strike.
“Gah!”
The flash had passed, and that was all.
If he hadn’t glimpsed something indistinct at the last moment, his ghost would already be wandering the Nine Springs.
How? How could this...!
The First Elder gritted his teeth and barely held back the pain and shock. His face stricken, he clutched his deeply slashed chest and staggered backward.
Against such speed and power, retreat would only lead to death. Fortunately, he had two dependable sworn brothers.
“Elder Brother!”
“No!”
The Second and Third Elders cried out and charged. One wielded a saber, the other a sword. Their hands blurred as they swung at the same target.
Jin Taekyung, who had rushed at them with the ghostlike movements of an assassin.
KWAANG!
One spear against a saber and a sword.
The three weapons, carrying several jiazi of internal energy, collided with a terrible roar that shook everything around them.
The earth heaved. The air burst apart.
Amid waves of power more violently turbulent than anything they had ever felt, the two old men saw it clearly:
The cold flames pouring from Jin Taekyung’s eyes. His hand gripping the spear shaft without the slightest tremor, even against two Supreme Peak masters.
And he was holding it with only one hand.
“Wa—”
Before the warning could leave their lips, Jin Taekyung’s palm slammed into the Third Elder’s chest.
Ah.
His vision swam. The Third Elder felt a terrible heat smash through bone and flesh and burrow deep inside him.
Crack.
The sickening sound came a moment later, faint as a distant echo. Blood surged into his mouth. As his body began to crumple, familiar shouts rang in his ears.
“You bastard!”
“Little Brother!”
No mistake. His elder brothers.
The world had called them fiends and bastards, but they had cherished him as if all three had been born of the same mother.
Crunch.
The Third Elder bit his tongue and forced his collapsing body upright.
He couldn’t fall here. He hadn’t survived this long to meet such a pointless end.
Besides...
We have the Demon Lord. We have his power.
The Third Elder was certain.
By now, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord must have stepped in.
He couldn’t see clearly through the haze in his mind, but surely a single command from the Demon Lord could free him from this terrible internal injury and pain.
But...
But why?
Why can’t I feel anything?
Even with his vision blurred, his senses as a Supreme Peak master remained. Yet as the Third Elder staggered and steadied himself, his Qi Sense told him everything was just as it had been.
Even while his two sworn brothers fought Jin Taekyung with all their might, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s presence remained where it had been, more than ten jang away.
“Demon Lord! Demon Lord!”
Crack! Boom!
The roar erupting from the spearhead swallowed the Third Elder’s desperate cry. But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord could not have failed to hear him.
Still, nothing changed.
No—that wasn’t quite true. Something did change.
It was tiny beside the immense energies surging all around them, and all the more stealthy for it.
Whish—thunk!
The Third Elder’s body locked up.
He felt a cold blade pierce his back, with saber qi gathered at its tip. He spun around in a flash and swung his arm.
Whoom—boom!
Compressed air exploded, but his blow struck nothing.

Black clothes as dark as pitch. Calm eyes.
The young man looked barely thirty, yet his voice was so low and composed it was almost hard to believe.

The Third Elder bit his lip hard enough to draw blood.

It was the young brat he had ignored from the beginning—the one who had somehow kept a dagger hidden and now driven it into his back.
With a single surprise attack.

Another flash came from the ample sleeve of his martial robe.
“I brought plenty of daggers.”
Whish!
