Watching the streak of light fly straight toward him, the Third Elder sneered inwardly.
At least, until he realized he couldn’t move. The terrible internal injury Jin Taekyung had dealt him and the dagger lodged in his back held him fast.
What is this...!
Thwack!
The dagger pierced the center of his forehead, and the Third Elder felt the world go dark.
The last thing he heard was Jeok Cheongang, who had watched it all, speaking.
“That’s one. No, two.”
The Third Elder, whose breath had already stopped, didn’t see it.
At the very moment his final breath left his body, the spearhead of White Flame, cloaked in dark-blue Force, sliced through the Second Elder’s throat.
Slash!
Beneath the fountain of blood, the First Elder’s eyes widened in horror. His body trembled.

sentences.text: At that moment, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was smiling.
Pure delight and excitement filled his crescent-shaped eyes.
His long, vertically slit pupils trembled with anticipation for what was to come.
More precisely, with anticipation for one young man.
Yes.
That’s it.
That’s exactly the look.
Watching Jin Taekyung’s eyes widen with shock and fury, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord felt his heart pound.
He had erased a thousand lives with a single gesture, yet he paid them no mind.
All his senses were fixed on Jin Taekyung.
He felt not the slightest guilt for the dead, nor the slightest remorse for breaking his promise.
He had been born and raised in the Demonic Cult.
The cruelty he’d possessed since his mother’s womb had blossomed through the demonic martial arts he’d learned from the time he could walk.
Even among the twenty-four great fiends who served the Heavenly Demon, no one could match him.
Now, Jin Taekyung was the only thing that interested him.
The Divine Dragon of the Central Plains Murim, a rising star whom his master was watching closely.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord wanted to see everything about that young brat.
He wanted to feel the full extent of the martial prowess unleashed at his fingertips, the emotions pouring out of him, the something special hidden within.
Show me.
Hurry!
And just as the Blood-Sword Demon Lord cried out in his heart—
Whooosh!
An immense, unprecedented energy surged up around one man.
“Who should I kill first?”
Jin Taekyung.
At the sight of the cold flames pouring from the young man’s eyes, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s smile deepened.
The Three Elders of Tianshan’s first reaction was suspicion.
Jin Taekyung held a spear that hadn’t been there moments ago.
How?
The promise had come to nothing now, but one of the terms of their meeting had been to come unarmed.
Jin Taekyung’s side had honored that condition.
They had all arrived empty-handed, a considerable comfort to the Three Elders of Tianshan.
If they could handle the terrifying old monster called the Fire King, two weaponless young brats shouldn’t be much trouble.
Even if one of them was the renowned Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, the three elders were fiends of a bygone age whose infamy had spread from Tianshan to the Central Plains.
As far as they were concerned, it was a fight they could win.
At least, until a spear appeared in Jin Taekyung’s hand.
Until an immense power, far beyond anything they had expected, enveloped that divine weapon, clearly made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Hummm.
The dazzling white spearhead trembled.
No—the air around it shuddered in tiny ripples.
At the same time, an immense, pure energy surged up and wrapped around the spearhead.
It was far too vast to be contained in the body of a young man who had turned twenty only a few years ago.
Ssssss.
What people called Force was no longer a dazzling blue-white.
This is...
The three old men caught their breath without realizing it.
What could they even call this power?
The Force gathered at the spearhead was dark as the deep sea.
It burned blue like fire at its fiercest, yet also flashed like a thunderbolt.
It’s different.
The Three Elders of Tianshan felt it instinctively.
That energy was of a different kind, a different order, from the energy they had cultivated all their lives.
But they had no way of knowing what it truly was.
They did not know that the strange familiarity they felt came from the internal energy Jin Taekyung had received from the Heavenly Power Demon.
They did not know that the ominous power born of demonic martial arts had finally become one with the Fire Gate Clan’s hellfire and the Hebei Peng Family’s thunderbolt.
Nor did they know just how immense and keen the power within that dark-blue streak of light was.
The one person who understood all of it better than anyone stood beside Jin Taekyung.
Ah.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, watched Jin Taekyung, his gaze deep and still.
He had suspected as much.
He simply hadn’t confirmed it with his own eyes.
The summit of martial mastery.
The young man had reached the highest peak, one that touched the heavens.
Age and experience were no longer measures by which to judge him.
He was a great martial artist who had forged a path of his own, one no one else had walked before.
Jeok Cheongang wanted to ask him, in all sincerity:
Do you know how remarkable the realm you’ve reached is?
And he wanted to tell him:
Across the Central Plains Murim, people gave those who reached such a realm a name spoken with the deepest respect.
The Ten Kings.
A vast, boundless sky and three stars.
Beneath them had stood ten giants.
And today, here and now, Jin Taekyung was proving himself the eleventh.
But he was different from those who had fallen to the passage of time or collapsed beneath their enemies’ cold-blue blades, spilling their blood.
He was a hero of a new age.
On this battlefield, where a thousand lives had been extinguished, an immense blaze was rising.
How dazzling you are.
A shiver ran down Jeok Cheongang’s spine.
Then he looked at the Three Elders of Tianshan, staring at Jin Taekyung in a daze, and saw the shadow of death slowly falling over them.
“Old Master.”
A quiet call, seething with pain at having failed to prevent so many deaths—and with the fury that pain had bred.
Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“Do as you’ve decided.”
They didn’t know those few, cryptic words were the trust and encouragement of a master to his Disciple, who was willing to risk his life.
Nor did they know that the brief exchange had sealed their fate.
Whoosh!
A sharp gust of wind swept through.
A dark-blue flash—impossible to tell whether it was flame, wave, or thunderbolt—distorted space as it rushed at them, impossibly fast and carrying tremendous force.
Slash!
Goose bumps rose across the First Elder’s body.
He twisted aside on instinct, but blood and terrible pain spread along the path of the strike.
“Gah!”
The flash had passed, and that was all.
If he hadn’t glimpsed something indistinct at the last moment, his ghost would already be wandering the Nine Springs.
How?
How could this...!
The First Elder gritted his teeth and barely held back the pain and shock.
His face stricken, he clutched his deeply slashed chest and staggered backward.
Against such speed and power, retreat would only lead to death.
Fortunately, he had two dependable sworn brothers.

The Second and Third Elders cried out and charged.
One wielded a saber, the other a sword.
Their hands blurred as they swung at the same target.
Jin Taekyung, who had rushed at them with the ghostlike movements of an assassin.
KWAANG!

The three weapons, carrying several jiazi of internal energy, collided with a terrible roar that shook everything around them.
The earth heaved.
The air burst apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 1029
paragraphs: Tap. Patter-patter.
Hot and damp.
Blood that had shot up like a fountain fell onto my head, soaking my scalp.
Someone who was already a headless corpse would never feel it again.
System Defeated Lv. 135 Gungongbo! Acquired a large amount of Fame. Acquired a large amount of EXP.
Splatter!
A moment later, the body lost its balance and collapsed into the pool of blood.
The Second Elder’s head had come off before he could even react. With a bewildered expression, it looked up at his sworn brothers.
Or rather, at the only sworn brother still in this world.
“One down. No—two.”
Jeok Cheongang’s words marked the Third Elder’s end. I turned and saw a silver blade jutting from the back of the man sprawled like a rotten log.
Pssht.
Blood dripped in little spurts with a deflating hiss.
Sama Pyo pulled the dagger from between the dead Third Elder’s brows. When our eyes met, he shrugged.
“Did I do something I shouldn’t have?”
I answered.
“Yeah.”
“If he was yours to deal with, I’m sorry. I thought leaving him alive might cause trouble...”
“That’s not what I mean.”
A question entered Sama Pyo’s eyes. I let out a breath as hot as a ball of fire.
“You shouldn’t have killed him so easily.”
EXP didn’t matter. Neither did whose hand killed him.
He should have suffered more.
He shouldn’t have left this world so easily, in a single instant.
The Second Elder hadn’t. First his collarbone had been torn away, then one arm severed. Only after his Eight Extraordinary Meridians had been ripped to shreds did his head come off.
“Don’t step in again. Not one step.”
My voice sounded strange and desolate, as if it belonged to someone else.
I didn’t even know what I looked like right now.
But Sama Pyo’s and Jeok Cheongang’s grim, hardened expressions—and the First Elder, frozen as if he’d come face-to-face with a fiend—gave me some idea.
“M-monster...”
His body trembled. So did his voice.
In the eyes of the old fiend who had lost the two sworn brothers he’d spent his life with in the blink of an eye, I saw rage he couldn’t hide. And fear, deeper and darker still.
Splosh.
I took a slow step forward.
Maybe it was the blood soaking the ground, but my footfall sounded unusually loud. The First Elder flinched and stumbled backward.
No. He dragged himself back on his rear, bracing himself with both arms.
With both knees shattered, it was the only way he could put even a little distance between us.
“D-don’t come any closer! I said don’t!”
The First Elder flung out his arms with a scream.
Boom!
I turned my head before I even heard the rush of air. The manifested palm force blasted through the space where my head had been a moment earlier.
He was already half-crippled, but the powerful internal energy flowing deep within him still burned like an inextinguishable flame.
Of course...
“Do it again.”
To my eyes, his movements were clumsy beyond words and hopelessly slow. Every move was full of openings.
“Aaaaaah!”
I couldn’t tell whether it was a scream or a battle shout.
Bang! Bang! Boom!
Panicked, the First Elder unleashed palm force after palm force, bursting the compressed air around me.
The force of his attacks whipped my hair about and tore through my collar and skin.
And that was his final struggle.
Grab—crack!
I seized his wrist like lightning and twisted.
It wasn’t a grappling technique built on complex principles, or even a move powered by internal energy.
Just raw Strength and Agility.
That power and speed, far beyond human limits, crushed frail flesh and bone with ease.
His face twisted with terrible pain. A stifled groan escaped him.
But I knew.
If the old fiend before me were the sort to give up after this much, the name Three Elders of Tianshan would have been forgotten long ago.
Whoosh! Crash!
Five fingers curled like hooks flashed down and struck the ground.
One step.
I read his movement and stepped back ahead of him. His hand barely grazed my collar before plunging deep into the earth. I stomped on the back of it.
Crack!
I felt the bones shatter beneath my sole, a thousand geun of weight behind it.
My calm face was reflected in his eyes, wide with pain and terror beyond anything he’d imagined.
“Don’t look at me like that.”
Thud.
I struck him squarely in the jaw. His head snapped to the side, and yellow teeth flew in every direction with the blood.
“When you look at me like that...”
Thud.
One more.
“Right now...”
Thud.
Again.
“It makes me want to kill you.”
Crack!
Sticky blood clung to my fist.
I grabbed the First Elder by the hair. He no longer moved at all. Slowly, I straightened up.
“We’re only just getting started, aren’t we?”
I wasn’t talking to the First Elder.
I was speaking to the monster watching from more than ten jang away, his face flushed—the one who had cut off a thousand heads with a single gesture.
Clap. Clap. Clap.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord applauded slowly, gazing at me with admiration.
“Magnificent. No—beautiful.”
His answer made my blood run cold.
Even with rage consuming me, I hadn’t expected anything like that reaction from him.
“That’s how a Murim warrior ought to fight. Crush your opponent cruelly and completely. That’s a real fight, don’t you think?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord was grinning from ear to ear.
Two of the Three Elders of Tianshan—valuable fighters who served as his own hands and feet—were dead, and the third was crippled. Yet he looked far happier than he had a moment ago.
“Crazy... bastard.”
“Me? Or you?”
“What?”
“Well, isn’t it true?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord blinked at me, then spread his arms and turned in a slow circle.
“Look at me. My clothes are terribly drab, but compared to you, don’t I look positively mild-mannered?”
“Ah, don’t misunderstand. I’m certainly not saying you look unpleasant. If anything, I find this rather familiar... It’s a good sight, in more ways than one.”
At his satisfied smile, I suddenly felt short of breath.
Familiar, he’d said. Pleasing.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, of all people. That old, vicious fiend.
He was talking about me, drenched in blood from head to toe.
About the person I’d been a moment ago, consumed not merely by revenge but by the desire to inflict even greater pain.
“This... What I mean is...”
“Enough.”
A voice I knew all too well cut me off. It was lower than usual.
“That’s enough.”
Jeok Cheongang strode forward, and I suddenly wanted to ask him something.
Who was he speaking to?
Me? Or the Blood-Sword Demon Lord?
Or both of us?
But I didn’t ask. No—I couldn’t.
For a moment, I was too afraid to ask whether I’d looked like a fiend mad with blood and revenge.
And yet, ironically, it was that very fiend who helped me steady my stiffened body and mind.
“To interrupt us at a time like this, Senior. That’s cruel of you. We were having quite a meaningful conversation.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord shook his head. Jeok Cheongang spat onto the ground.
“Fuck off. This old man has never had a junior like you.”
“I know. But I’ve admired you for so long that I can’t help myself. I’ll have to settle for loving you from afar.”
“Do I have to turn you into charcoal while you’re still alive to shut that mouth of yours?”
“Probably. To be honest, I was a little disappointed about that. I thought at least one of those three would end up that way.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gave a showy sigh, then continued.

“You have no idea how excited I was when I heard what happened at Mount Jiuhua all those years ago. A descendant of the Fire Gate Clan I’d only ever heard about! And when I heard those fools who dared lay a hand on you had all been reduced to ash—how satisfying that was.”
“What did you say?”
“Well, isn’t it? Burned alive—imagine the pain they must have felt. What revenge could be more certain or more terrible?”
“Everyone else shuddered and called you a mad old man. Not me. I’ve admired you ever since.”
His eyes shone like the morning star. Jeok Cheongang and I were speechless. Even Sama Pyo, who had been watching everything calmly, seemed at a loss for words.
A fiend.
More than anyone I’d ever met, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord deserved the word. He was a madman.
Now I understood better than ever why “blood” was part of his title.
And to him, the Three Elders of Tianshan were no more than livestock he’d kept close at hand.

“Those idiots, too. During the Great Faction War, the moment a battle started going against them, they couldn’t run fast enough. Today they stepped forward without knowing their place, so they deserved to die... Ah, come to think of it, one’s still alive.”
Wheeze, wheeze.
“D-Demon Lord...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord glanced at the First Elder, who was still drawing shallow breaths, then looked at me.
“I only ask out of concern, but you aren’t thinking of letting him live, are you?”
“Why do you ask?”
“He’s been bothering me for a while. Neither alive nor dead... Better to settle it one way or the other, don’t you think?”
“If you’re going to kill him, do it quickly. If you want a prisoner, have that young fellow beside you take him back. He doesn’t know much, though, so he won’t be much use.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gestured toward Sama Pyo, then smacked his lips.
“Ah, though perhaps there isn’t time for that anymore.”
Boom. Boom. Bwoom.
The war drums were drawing closer, each beat louder and deeper than the last.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord and us.
Behind each side, the aura of countless troops made the air tremble.
Now it begins.
I could feel it.
The bloody battle for the Great Snow Mountain—the great battle we could no longer avoid—had finally begun.
And...
I can end it right here.
I couldn’t tell exactly how strong the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was, but Jeok Cheongang and I should be enough.
Now that the Three Elders of Tianshan, a core part of the enemy’s strength, were gone, the balance of this battle had tipped heavily in our favor.
Surely.
Surely that was how it would go.
Then why...
Why had the Blood-Sword Demon Lord only watched?
Why had he treated three Supreme Peak masters—fighters that valuable—like livestock?
This is...
The moment that thought came to me, my eyes widened.
Whoosh!
Dark clouds had gathered without my noticing. A cold fiercer than the Great Snow Mountain’s own approached, freezing the wind as it came.
And at the center of it all, a company of riders swept toward us like dark mist.
Sssaaaaa.
Not even a pounding of hooves accompanied their ghostlike charge. Watching them, I thought of the otherworldly beings who should never have appeared here, in Murim.
“Death Knights...?”

“It makes me want to kill you.”
Crack!
Sticky blood clung to my fist.
I grabbed the First Elder by the hair.
He no longer moved at all.
Slowly, I straightened up.
“We’re only just getting started, aren’t we?”
I wasn’t talking to the First Elder.
I was speaking to the monster watching from more than ten jang away, his face flushed—the one who had cut off a thousand heads with a single gesture.
Clap.
Clap.
Clap.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord applauded slowly, gazing at me with admiration.
“Magnificent.
No—beautiful.”
His answer made my blood run cold.
Even with rage consuming me, I hadn’t expected anything like that reaction from him.
“That’s how a Murim warrior ought to fight.
Crush your opponent cruelly and completely.
That’s a real fight, don’t you think?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord was grinning from ear to ear.
Two of the Three Elders of Tianshan—valuable fighters who served as his own hands and feet—were dead, and the third was crippled.
Yet he looked far happier than he had a moment ago.
“Crazy... bastard.”
“Me?
Or you?”
“What?”
“Well, isn’t it true?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord blinked at me, then spread his arms and turned in a slow circle.
“Look at me.
My clothes are terribly drab, but compared to you, don’t I look positively mild-mannered?”
“Ah, don’t misunderstand.
I’m certainly not saying you look unpleasant.
If anything, I find this rather familiar...
It’s a good sight, in more ways than one.”
At his satisfied smile, I suddenly felt short of breath.
Familiar, he’d said.
Pleasing.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, of all people.
That old, vicious fiend.
He was talking about me, drenched in blood from head to toe.
About the person I’d been a moment ago, consumed not merely by revenge but by the desire to inflict even greater pain.
“This...
What I mean is...”
“Enough.”
A voice I knew all too well cut me off.
It was lower than usual.
“That’s enough.”
Jeok Cheongang strode forward, and I suddenly wanted to ask him something.
Who was he speaking to?
Me?
Or the Blood-Sword Demon Lord?
Or both of us?
But I didn’t ask.
No—I couldn’t.
For a moment, I was too afraid to ask whether I’d looked like a fiend mad with blood and revenge.
And yet, ironically, it was that very fiend who helped me steady my stiffened body and mind.
“To interrupt us at a time like this, Senior.
That’s cruel of you.
We were having quite a meaningful conversation.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord shook his head.
Jeok Cheongang spat onto the ground.
“Fuck off.
This old man has never had a junior like you.”
“I know.
But I’ve admired you for so long that I can’t help myself.
I’ll have to settle for loving you from afar.”
“Do I have to turn you into charcoal while you’re still alive to shut that mouth of yours?”
“Probably.
To be honest, I was a little disappointed about that.
I thought at least one of those three would end up that way.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gave a showy sigh, then continued.
“You have no idea how excited I was when I heard what happened at Mount Jiuhua all those years ago.
A descendant of the Fire Gate Clan I’d only ever heard about!
And when I heard those fools who dared lay a hand on you had all been reduced to ash—how satisfying that was.”
“What did you say?”
“Well, isn’t it?
Burned alive—imagine the pain they must have felt.
What revenge could be more certain or more terrible?”
“Everyone else shuddered and called you a mad old man.
Not me.
I’ve admired you ever since.”
His eyes shone like the morning star.
Jeok Cheongang and I were speechless.
Even Sama Pyo, who had been watching everything calmly, seemed at a loss for words.
A fiend.
More than anyone I’d ever met, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord deserved the word.
He was a madman.
Now I understood better than ever why “blood” was part of his title.
And to him, the Three Elders of Tianshan were no more than livestock he’d kept close at hand.
“Those idiots, too.
During the Great Faction War, the moment a battle started going against them, they couldn’t run fast enough.
Today they stepped forward without knowing their place, so they deserved to die...
Ah, come to think of it, one’s still alive.”
Wheeze, wheeze.
“D-Demon Lord...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord glanced at the First Elder, who was still drawing shallow breaths, then looked at me.
“I only ask out of concern, but you aren’t thinking of letting him live, are you?”
“Why do you ask?”
“He’s been bothering me for a while.
Neither alive nor dead...
Better to settle it one way or the other, don’t you think?”
“If you’re going to kill him, do it quickly.
If you want a prisoner, have that young fellow beside you take him back.
He doesn’t know much, though, so he won’t be much use.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gestured toward Sama Pyo, then smacked his lips.
“Ah, though perhaps there isn’t time for that anymore.”
Boom.
Boom.
Bwoom.
The war drums were drawing closer, each beat louder and deeper than the last.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord and us.
Behind each side, the aura of countless troops made the air tremble.
Now it begins.
I could feel it.
The bloody battle for the Great Snow Mountain—the great battle we could no longer avoid—had finally begun.
And...
I can end it right here.
I couldn’t tell exactly how strong the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was, but Jeok Cheongang and I should be enough.
Now that the Three Elders of Tianshan, a core part of the enemy’s strength, were gone, the balance of this battle had tipped heavily in our favor.
Surely.
Surely that was how it would go.
Then why...
Why had the Blood-Sword Demon Lord only watched?
Why had he treated three Supreme Peak masters—fighters that valuable—like livestock?
This is...
The moment that thought came to me, my eyes widened.
Whoosh!
Dark clouds had gathered without my noticing.
A cold fiercer than the Great Snow Mountain’s own approached, freezing the wind as it came.
And at the center of it all, a company of riders swept toward us like dark mist.
Sssaaaaa.
Not even a pounding of hooves accompanied their ghostlike charge.
Watching them, I thought of the otherworldly beings who should never have appeared here, in Murim.
“Death Knights...?”

chapters.title: Chapter 1030
paragraphs: The absurd had invaded common sense long ago.
Laws had been broken, truths overturned, and the word death had become cheap.
At least, that was the world one young man had been born and raised in.
Monsters. Hunters.
Monsters and humans killing one another inside the boundaries between dimensions known as Gates.
Mana and magical power.
Miraculous forces that shattered truths Earth had held since ancient times, along with laws discovered by the handful of geniuses who had shaped human history.
And a war that still hadn’t ended.
The young man was part of that world.
A world where Magic tore open the earth, rained down fire and lightning, and defied gravity.
Where Hunters shone with dazzling auras as they faced monsters of grotesque appearance and unimaginable strength—creatures found only in ancient myths, or beyond anything anyone had ever imagined.
Humans were adaptable creatures.
By the time the little child born on the day humanity won its great victory was approaching thirty, the absurdity that had overturned the world in the Great Cataclysm had become the new common sense.
Until another absurdity changed everything.
On a steep hill in the middle of summer, beside the recycling area outside a goshiwon, lay a massive hunk of scrap metal.
No—a VR capsule. An entrance to another world.
That was how a young man with nothing to his name stepped into a new world.
So much awaited him beyond the invisible veil.
Dangers and opportunities unlike any he’d known, and rewards.
He formed bonds with good people, fought countless enemies, and grew because of it.
That was why he wished so desperately for one thing:
That nothing out of the ordinary would happen here.
Perhaps that wish was why he kept downplaying and ignoring the one suspicion that grew stronger with time.
Until this very moment, when he faced the truth he hadn’t wanted to believe.
“Death Knights...?”
The words slipped vacantly from his parted lips.
The young man—Jin Taekyung—lifted his head and stared.
Caught by the word he himself had spoken.
Overwhelmed by the unbelievable sight before him.
Sssaaaaa.
Beneath the dark clouds hanging over the snow-covered mountains, a murky haze spread.

At its center, seven ghost horses soundlessly charged forward, stepping on empty air. On their backs sat seven men dressed not in armor that covered them from head to toe, but in black clothes as dark as pitch.
No. What he sensed was the unmistakably familiar presence of death.
Its essence never changed, whatever form it took.
The deep, cloying aura of death and its stench reached every one of Jin Taekyung’s senses—even his soul.
No mistake.
Jin Taekyung trembled without realizing it.
He’d been right. It was them.
Death Knights.
Knights who had given up their souls and forsaken their rest.
The absurdity of another world was invading common sense once again.
Yet amid the two vast armies advancing toward each other, Jin Taekyung was the only one who recognized it.
“Retreat! Fall back, now—!”
Whoosh!
As he shouted to his allies, Jin Taekyung felt every hair on his body stand on end. He spun around.
He’d made that movement a thousand times—no, more than ten thousand.
Urgent, yet perfectly practiced, it followed the turn of his waist and arms. Dark-blue Force rose like a tidal wave.
KWAANG!
A deafening boom shook the air. Beyond the gray-white sword blade trembling against his spearpoint, a fiend gone mad with blood grinned at Jin Taekyung.
“Why not surrender while you still can?”
“I’ll return those words to you.”
The reply hadn’t come from Jin Taekyung.
Jeok Cheongang had become a streak of light, closing on the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s flank. His palm struck ahead of his quiet voice.
Whooosh.
Flames erupted in a dazzling burst of heat.
Faced with the terrible heat of the Flame Divine Palm, which burned the air and melted ten-thousand-year snow, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord twisted aside without hesitation.
BOOM!
Compressed air exploded. No—it vaporized on the spot.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord narrowly avoided the palm strike and sprang backward. By any measure, it was a successful dodge, but the heat had still scorched his collar and the skin beneath it black.
“Whoops. Well, look at that.”
Burning pain was said to be worse than any other.
Yet even with his skin charred and parts of it melted, a smile remained on the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s lips.
“Just as they said, you’re a fiery one, Senior.”
“You bastard...!”
“Don’t be so angry. I may speak this way, but it stings me too.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord wasn’t trying to provoke him. He meant it.
They had clashed only once, but he knew one thing for certain.
He could never defeat the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, alone.
And even if Jeok Cheongang—a master half a step above him—weren’t there, capturing Jin Taekyung alive rather than killing him would be extremely difficult.
Of course, that was only how things stood for now.
“I should ask your understanding in advance for what’s about to happen, Senior. Yours too, my friend. I’m not entirely fond of doing things this way myself...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had furrowed his brow as if he were troubled, but soon he burst into hearty laughter and continued.
“But what can I do? This, too, is part of proving that person’s greatness.”
At that moment—
Rumble, rumble, rumble!

The vast army of Dark Heaven had already charged to within roughly three hundred thirty yards. More precisely, the seven pairs of riders at the head of the countless fanatics rose into the air, stepping on empty space.
No—they ran.
Screee!
Everyone advancing to meet them saw it clearly.
Tens of thousands of eyes widened. Tightly closed lips parted of their own accord.
Shock. Fear.
Only those two emotions showed in their eyes and on their faces.
What could anyone call such a sight?
Stepping on Empty Air? Traversing the Void?
No word that came to mind could quite explain it.

Several masters on the Murim Alliance’s side were skilled enough in body-lightness techniques to step on empty air. But running through the sky on horseback was something none of them had ever imagined.
One person, however, was different.
They’re coming.
Jin Taekyung tightened his grip on White Flame.
The sight had shocked him more than anyone else on the battlefield, but he also understood what he was seeing more clearly than anyone.
Familiar, yet strange.
Called Death Knights in the modern world, these beings—whatever they might be called in Murim—were closing in at blinding speed.
They’re strong. These aren’t ordinary ones.
Jin Taekyung could tell that more than their appearance had changed.
The closer they came, the stronger their stench and aura of death grew. Both far surpassed anything he knew from ordinary Death Knights.
Right. This is like...
Lei Fei.
Jin Taekyung suddenly remembered another hero whose soul, not so long ago, had been forcibly corrupted by an Arch Lich.
The Death Knight Lord.
Lei Fei had been an S-rank Hunter and a hero. In his corrupted state, he had been the strongest enemy they faced after the Arch Lich itself.
A chosen leader among Death Knights, who had not only retained all his strength from life but grown stronger still.
A Named Monster fully deserving of the title Lord.
Yet each of the seven men in black riding ghost horses at the head of the enemy army gave off an aura no weaker than Lei Fei’s had been.
No. Stronger.
It was already too late to turn back.
Fear was contagious.
His allies’ morale had soared as they watched him defeat the Three Elders of Tianshan in an instant. Now, faced with something they had never seen or heard of, it was fading like a bubble.
He drew our entire army out of the Great Snow Mountain. He used the Three Elders of Tianshan as bait.
Jin Taekyung understood at last.
The Three Elders of Tianshan had been used as bait from the very beginning, for this exact moment.
And the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s plan had worked perfectly.
Even if their allies retreated now, the enemy would reach them all the faster.
Jin Taekyung had only two choices left.
Hold this position so his shaken allies could retreat before they ever crossed weapons with the enemy.
Or...
Risk everything and turn this around.
At his side stood the one person he trusted and could follow more than anyone.
“How many will you take?”
“All eight.”
Jin Taekyung gave a quiet laugh at Jeok Cheongang’s calm answer.
“That’ll be tough at your age.”
“Don’t worry. Ever since I got younger, I’ve had energy to spare.”
“I’m glad that Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng I brought you was worth it.”
“That little thing? Bring me Ten-Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng next time.”
“Have you no shame?”
“Want to open me up and check?”
The Fire Gate Clan’s master and disciple stood like iron towers at the heart of the battlefield, waiting for the enemy.
About a hundred sixty-five yards away, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord watched them, his face flushed with excitement. The vast army behind him surged past its commander and poured toward them.
“They’re swarming like a pack of dogs. Even the unorthodox faction would have to give them that.”
At Jeok Cheongang’s mutter, Sama Pyo let out a dry laugh.
“Yes. I think so too.”
“Come to think of it, there’s an unorthodox brat right here.”
“I can’t deny that.”
“Unorthodox, you say. Is that truly how you see yourself?”
“This hardly seems the time to answer that, but what can I do? I was born, and the whole world called me unorthodox. I suppose that’s my lot.”
About a hundred yards.

The enemy’s shouts shook the air from every direction, making their ears ring. Sama Pyo tightened his grip on the sword and saber that had once belonged to the Three Elders of Tianshan, one in each hand.
“That’s the stupidest thing I’ve heard. Are you an idiot?”
At the quiet voice in his ear, Sama Pyo’s body stiffened.
“What... did you say?”
“I asked if you’re an idiot. You.”
About sixty-five yards.
As the aura of tens of thousands of enemies made the air tremble, Jin Taekyung went on calmly.
“You live the way you were born, let other people decide what to call you, and go along with it? Is that your life?”
“That’s...”

“Just live however the hell you want. Protect what needs protecting. Do something good now and then. What does it matter whether you’re part of the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, or the dark-path figures?”
Sama Pyo’s face went rigid.
His words came so freely. That made them hurt all the more—and made Sama Pyo envy him.
Unlike Sama Pyo, Jin Taekyung had been born into the orthodox faction.
“What do you know about me to say something like that?”
“Of course I don’t know shit. How would I know what kind of life you’ve lived? You’ve never told me.”
“What?”
“But I know what kind of person you are.”
About thirty yards.
Clouds gathered overhead. Darkness fell.
Watching the shadows descend through the empty air, Jin Taekyung tossed out one short sentence.
“We’re here together now.”
“I guess I’m pretty good at judging people. Right, Old Master?”
Jeok Cheongang didn’t answer, and Jin Taekyung didn’t wait for him to.
About a year earlier, the Pavilion Master of the Fire Dragon Pavilion had gladly welcomed the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate when he’d come calling out of the blue.
Now Jin Taekyung swung the spear in his hand.
Whooosh.
A dark-blue tidal wave rose, hot as hellfire and swift as a thunderbolt.
And as Jin Taekyung advanced without hesitation, Sama Pyo suddenly thought he looked dazzling.
KWA-BOOM!

paragraphs: I didn’t wonder if I could do it.
I had to. I had to see it through.
Power came with responsibility, and the weight of that responsibility wouldn’t let me take even one step back.
That was why I was moving forward now.
Whoosh.
I lowered the First Elder, still in my grip, and planted my foot on the ground. In the same instant, I shot forward.
Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step.
The subtle art I’d learned from the greatest assassin of all time flowed through my feet.
My legs felt impossibly light. Wind brushed past me, then vanished without a trace in the heat radiating from someone nearby.
The moment I tightened my grip on the spear shaft—
Swaaash!
The world slowed.
Seven streams of Force fell like lightning from overhead. Jeok Cheongang and I flung out our hands at the same time.
KWA-BOOOOM!
A crash that seemed to split the sky rang out, and time, paused for an instant, surged forward like a raging torrent.
KRRRUNCH!
The ground flipped over from the force of the collision. My feet, light as air only moments ago, were driven back under a pressure of tens of thousands of pounds.
Damn it.
I felt the difference in strength the instant we collided, and my teeth clenched before I could stop them.
I’d expected them to be strong. Not this strong.
Seven.
Not one, not two, not three—but seven Death Knights.
No, the men in black were far too powerful. They hadn’t merely kept all their former strength; they’d grown stronger still.
Even with Jeok Cheongang at my side, their power was too much to withstand.
“Hngh...!”
A muffled breath came from right beside me.
Jeok Cheongang was holding off four enemies alone, proving his title as the Fire King. But this momentary standoff was like a glass bottle on the verge of shattering.
Just as it was now.
SHWING! KRAANG!
The three spears and swords, shrouded in pitch-black Force, met the White Flame’s blade once more. The impact left me gasping, and I felt my knees bend on their own.
They’re strong. The Three Elders of Tianshan don’t even compare.
The Three Elders had certainly been powerful masters. But inheriting the Thunderbolt Saber King’s internal energy and gaining insight weren’t the only reasons I’d been able to defeat them alone.
Sometimes a pack of wolves was more frightening than a single tiger.
The Three Elders had built their infamy as a pack, much like the Qilian Three Fiends, who had followed the Western Heaven Demon Lord and drenched Sichuan in blood.
But the men in black, closing in on me with tremendous strength and momentum even now, were different.
They were tigers.
Unlike the Three Elders of Tianshan, each one could command an entire mountain range—or, at least, they must have been able to in the past.
The worst part was that these tigers had lost their souls, grown even stronger, and now moved as a pack at one man’s command.
“How do they seem, now that you’ve faced them yourself? Impressive, aren’t they? I call them Black Ghosts.”
Behind the seven men in black—the seven Black Ghosts—the enemy’s vast army drew closer with every passing moment. Even over its roar, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s voice rang clear.
So did his aura, growing more intense with each slow step.
“Don’t struggle too hard. It’s a shame about Senior Jeok, but that can’t be helped. You, on the other hand, are a very important prize.”
I couldn’t see his face behind the Black Ghosts, but I could picture it, if only faintly.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord smiling. His eyes bright with excitement at the sea of corpses and blood to come.
“Who knows? If you surrender quietly now, perhaps both master and disciple can survive.”
Grrk. Grrrk!
Under the crushing pressure, I barely managed to force out my voice.
“Fuck... off!”
KWAANG!
I thrust the spear shaft upward. All three of their spears and swords flew into the air at once.
Four jiazi of internal energy and a body far beyond human limits let me throw off the Black Ghosts’ combined attack, strengthened though they were at the cost of their souls. Only for a moment.
But that moment gave me an opening I wouldn’t get again.
SHHK!
I swung with all my strength and cut through them.
More precisely, I cut three huge black horses in half—ghost horses, powerful monsters in their own right.
FWOOOSH!
Instead of the blood any living creature should have had, a dark mist burst out. Jeok Cheongang, who’d been barely holding on, gaped at the unbelievable sight.
“What kind of fucked-up—!”
I’d have liked to explain, but now wasn’t the time.
The Black Ghosts lost their balance as their mounts vanished beneath them. I seized the chance and charged the four facing Jeok Cheongang.
SHK-SHK! KAKAKANG!
I slashed, stabbed, and struck.
They blocked all three lightning-fast attacks without difficulty. Waiting for them, though, was Jeok Cheongang’s palm strike, wreathed in brilliant white flames.
“Die.”
Whoosh—BOOM!
The Flame Divine Palm shot forward without even a sound of rushing air and struck one of the Black Ghosts.
The man took the blow square in the chest and flew back like a cannonball. Jeok Cheongang bared his teeth in a grin.
Or tried to.
“Good. That’s one—”
—Grrr.
The Black Ghost should have died, his whole body scorched black. Instead, he let out a strange groan and straightened up.
“...No, it isn’t.”
Perhaps the Flame Divine Palm’s force still lingered. Jeok Cheongang stared blankly as the Black Ghost staggered to his feet, then blinked at me.
“What the hell are those things?”
KWAANG!
I parried a Black Ghost’s sword and let out a breath before answering.
“Death. Death Knights.”
“Great Hand, Great Hand, Shift-Head? What the hell are you talking about?”
Unfortunately, I couldn’t clear up Jeok Cheongang’s confusion.
Before I could say another word, all the Black Ghosts charged at once, including the one Jeok Cheongang had knocked away.
KWA-BOOOOM!
My ears rang. Pain shot through my wrist, and both my legs sank deep into the ground.
The pressure was terrifying, as if Taishan itself were bearing down on me.
And just as Jeok Cheongang and I were trapped in a forest of steel, a fierce rush of air sounded from somewhere.
Whoosh—CLANG-CLANG!
A Black Ghost’s great saber knocked away a dozen or so throwing knives. I could guess who’d been fool enough to join this fight.
Sama Pyo. You idiot. What the hell are you doing here?
But there was only a hair’s breadth between courage and stupidity.
Sama Pyo was an idiot, but he was brave. He’d distracted only one of them, yet even that gave us a little room to breathe.
“Old Master, now!”
“Damn it!”
Jeok Cheongang spat a curse and shot out his fist like lightning.
KRRRUNCH!
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Flames erupted like an explosion, pushing back the weapons wrapped in black Force, if only for a moment.
The earth-shaking blast rattled everything for hundreds of feet. It also concealed a streak of light racing through the flames.
SHWING! THUNK!
A throwing knife left Sama Pyo’s hand and sank into a Black Ghost’s throat. The blade quivered.
Of course, I knew better than anyone that it wouldn’t be enough to bring him down.
Pshk.
The Black Ghost pulled out the knife as though it were nothing. I took advantage of the brief gap in their encirclement to leap back.
“You asked earlier what a Death Knight was.”
“They’re bastards like that.”
“...Shit. This is a fine mess.”
Jeok Cheongang sighed. Sama Pyo came up beside us, his face calm.
“What monsters.”
“Idiot. You should’ve fallen back earlier. What, did you come all this way for a good view?”
“I already regret it. But what exactly are they? Some kind of jiangshi?”
“Similar, but let’s say they’re a bit worse.”
Jiangshi would be a thousand times better.
If they were a Maoshan Sect specialty, at least the people of this world could call them native creatures.
But these Death Knights—the Black Ghosts—were an invasive species.
They would destroy the ecosystem and shatter every law and bit of common sense.
No. They already had.
How could this happen...?
I swallowed a quiet groan.
How it was possible no longer mattered.
The rules we’d all believed in had already crumbled, and now we had to deal with the wreckage.
That’s right. Not just a handful of us. All of us.
Rumble, rumble.
The ground trembled. The shouts that had shaken everything around us were now at my back, drawing up beside Jeok Cheongang and Sama Pyo.
“Infinite Life Buddha.”
The one approaching with a low invocation was the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.
Beside him stood the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, who had studied under the same master, along with nearly a thousand disciples of the Zhongnan Sect.
And there was another man, his face set hard.
“So it comes to this.”
The Black Night King, Sima Gong.
He commanded countless martial artists from Gansu—numbers in no way inferior to the enemy’s. His somber gaze rested on us.
No. On Sama Pyo.
His lips parted as though he meant to speak, but in the end he said nothing. He looked ahead instead, toward the rulers from beyond the desert, finally facing us on this vast snowfield.
“Enough.”
The Black Ghosts advancing silently toward us stopped as one. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord stepped out among them, an army of tens of thousands at his back.
Thud.
“Good. This is how you should meet me.”
Vrrrrm.
The gray-white blade trembled. Its color hardly suited the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s title, though it had reaped carnage that ranked among the worst of the Great Faction War.
Dark-red Force welled from it, the surges joining and binding together without pause as he leveled the sword at the people in his way.
It was too late for us to turn back. All we could do was press forward with everything we had.
WAAAAAH!
Shouts and killing intent, fear and anger, mingled and swelled.
Amid that violent whirl of emotion, I took a slow step forward.
Crunch.
Cold. Frost broke beneath my toes.
Thump.
My heart beat.
I quickened my steps to match its harsh, rapid rhythm.
Whoosh. SHWAAAAA!
The wind blew. The mild breeze became a raging gale, and I summoned that gale.
No—the whole battlefield did.
WAAAAAH!
Shouts, clouds, wind.
Beyond them, countless blades flashed.
And two vast armies raced across the dazzling white snowfield, colliding at last in its center.
KRRRUNCH!
The white snow turned red.
Through the blood mist as it billowed and spread, through countless screams and deaths, the superhumans shot toward one another.

chapters.title: Chapter 1032
paragraphs: It was like watching two enormous waves swallow each other.

There were a few differences. This was a vast snowy plain, not the sea. The waves were made of countless people and flashing blades, not water. And the spray thrown up by their collision was red as blood.
No—it was blood itself.
KRRRUNCH!
Tens of thousands clashed with tens of thousands.
Like warhorses that had never learned to retreat, the two armies charged straight at each other and tangled together in an instant, weapons flashing in their hands.
CLANG! THUNK!
SHING!
A dense mist of blood spread through the air with the dreadful sound of blades cutting flesh.
And through the snowy plain, already awash with blood and screams, spearheads drove fiercely toward the heart of the battle.
“Infinite Life Buddha...”
Whoooosh.
The hem of a Daoist robe whipped violently, as if caught in a storm, under the force of an overwhelming aura.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had split five enemies apart with a single stroke. Now he brought his sword down at an angle, its blade enlarged by milky-white Force.
Swaaash!
The sheer pressure warped the space around it. A towering blade of Sword Force swept through the enemies clad in black armor.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The ground heaved with a deafening crash, and flesh and bone scattered in every direction.
Yet even after witnessing the grisly sight from point-blank range, the followers who had begun worshiping a new god called the Lord of Heaven didn’t so much as blink.
No—more precisely, they kept advancing, gazing at the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord with hazy eyes as though entranced.
All the while, they murmured their eight-character creed without pause.
“In heaven and on earth.”
“All demons bow in submission...”
CRUNCH!
Their hollow, almost chilling voices ended only when they died.
At least, that was what the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord believed in that moment.
Gurgle.
Blood bubbled in a follower’s slashed throat.
His neck had been cut by the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s sword, yet he went on muttering as the light slowly faded from his eyes.
“Heaven above... gurgle... hea...”
THUNK!
The creed stopped only when the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord drove his sword into the man’s chest. A chill ran down his spine.
They’re no ordinary people.
Of course they weren’t. Even when the Heavenly Demon swept across the Central Plains, the hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path gathered under him had been half-mad fanatics.
But the enemies the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had faced back then had at least known fear.
They, too, had possessed an emotion every human ought to have.
But what in the world...
Then he understood what had felt so familiar.
Fear.
They had no fear.
Though they clearly knew he was a stronger opponent they could never defeat, the followers of Dark Heaven kept surging toward him as though they had been born for this very moment.
Spraying red blood instead of white sea foam.
Screeeee!
The tip of his sword swept toward the enemies closing in from every direction.
The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.

The Zhongnan Sect’s signature sword art, a technique of Supreme Peak mastery, swept through the space around him. Weapons and bodies met its razor-sharp Force and were cut apart like tofu, their pieces scattering across the snow.
SHING! THUD-THUD!
Corpses collapsed amid the sickening sounds of torn flesh.
Yet one enemy, his chest deeply cut along with one arm, didn’t crumple with a groan of pain. He reached out with his one remaining hand.
BOOM!
A sharp whistle split the air, and the hem of the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s robe burst apart.
He narrowly avoided the palm strike and thrust out his hand at blinding speed.
THUNK!
Only after the Zhongnan Sect’s famed Heavenly Vault Finger Qi pierced the man between the brows did he collapse.
But though he had dispatched dozens of enemies in less than a moment, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s face remained rigid.
This is...
There was no doubt. They had no fear, and they could barely feel pain.
He didn’t know whether some secret technique or a drug that clouded the mind was responsible, but this was far beyond the bounds of common sense.
And there were tens of thousands of them.
They felt neither fear nor pain, and each was a skilled martial artist. They were weapons made to sweep across a battlefield.
This is bad. No—this is the worst.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord bit his lip, feeling a fear he hadn’t known since the Great Faction War. Then—
Swoooosh!
Along with a rush of overlapping whistles, an immense force tore into one side of the battlefield.
KWA-BOOOOM!
A sudden crash sent countless scraps of flesh flying in every direction.

The Zhongnan Sect disciples had formed a tight sword formation around the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword. Now the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord watched it shatter in an instant, his eyes wide.
“No!”
“J-Junior Sister!”
Their cries were almost screams.
Stunned by the loss of fellow disciples they had known since childhood, they stared blankly at the enemy who had broken their formation with a single blow.
Two men covered in pitch black from head to toe.
No—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had called them Black Ghosts, and the name suited these unknown beings all too well.
Sssaaaaa.
Black energy rose in threads around their bodies, swallowing the air.
The Zhongnan Sect disciples began to tremble without realizing it. The energy gripped their hearts and locked their limbs.
“Hngh...”
Strained breaths escaped all around.
Everyone was crushed beneath their chilling aura—an overwhelming force known as Fear somewhere far away.
No—almost everyone.
SHWOOF!
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord closed the distance in an instant, more furious than he had ever been.
Dozens of disciples had died in the blink of an eye.
The people he was duty-bound to protect as Sect Leader—the future pillars of the Zhongnan Sect, whom he had watched grow since childhood—had been cut down in an instant.
“How dare you!”
SHWING-SHWING-SHWING!
His sword tip cut through the air, driven by fury. The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, honed to nine-tenths mastery, sent dozens of sword images pouring forth.
Then they vanished without a trace.
Whoooosh! CLANG!
The moment those immense forces collided, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s eyes widened.
His beloved sword, which had cut through the wind, was being knocked aside by an axe blade swinging with the wind, erasing his sword images as it swept through them.
“What is this...!”
GRRRK. KWAANG!
Before the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord could finish his cry of shock, the blade finally gave way to the immense force and was sent flying. It trembled violently.
KRRUNCH!
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord slid back, his foot carving a deep furrow in the ground. He barely steadied himself, pain stabbing through his wrist.
Far worse than the pain was the shock.
“Y-You...”
The words stumbled from his lips.
He stared at the Black Ghost gripping a battle axe as large as a grown man, his eyes so wide they seemed ready to pop out.
No. It can’t be.
He tried to deny it, but there was no denying what stood before him.
The Black Ghost who had stopped the Zhongnan Sect Leader single-handedly had a face he remembered.
He hadn’t recognized it at first. Now he did.
That crude, strangely shaped weapon. Those features, horribly twisted and discolored, yet still faintly recognizable.
“...Black Axe Fiend.”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord murmured the name, stunned.
A great fiend of the Demonic Cult whom he and his master had faced on the battlefield long ago. A Supreme Peak master who had first taught him the fear of death.
And...
“He should have died.”
One of the twenty-four great fiends under the Heavenly Demon, who had met his end right there on that day.
“Then... how?”
It was impossible. It should never have happened.
But the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s questions went unanswered.
A fierce rush of air swept toward him, dragging him back to the present.
Screeeee—CRUNCH!
A neck was severed. Blood sprayed into the air.
A middle-aged first-generation disciple, one marked as a future Elder, lost his head in a single stroke. Gritting his teeth, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord kicked off the ground.
“Senior Brothers!”
His shout carried internal energy. The Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, frozen after belatedly recognizing the Black Axe Fiend, finally moved.
Fwoosh!
Their figures blurred, their movement techniques making their feet as light as feathers.
But the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s heart was heavy as he shot toward the Black Axe Fiend, returned from death as a Black Ghost, and the other Black Ghost beside him, whose aura was no less immense.

Today might be the day.

Screeeee!

sentences.text: It was like watching two enormous waves swallow each other.
There were a few differences.
This was a vast snowy plain, not the sea.
The waves were made of countless people and flashing blades, not water.
And the spray thrown up by their collision was red as blood.
No—it was blood itself.
KRRRUNCH!
Tens of thousands clashed with tens of thousands.
Like warhorses that had never learned to retreat, the two armies charged straight at each other and tangled together in an instant, weapons flashing in their hands.
CLANG!
THUNK!
SHING!
A dense mist of blood spread through the air with the dreadful sound of blades cutting flesh.
And through the snowy plain, already awash with blood and screams, spearheads drove fiercely toward the heart of the battle.
“Infinite Life Buddha...”
Whoooosh.
The hem of a Daoist robe whipped violently, as if caught in a storm, under the force of an overwhelming aura.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had split five enemies apart with a single stroke.
Now he brought his sword down at an angle, its blade enlarged by milky-white Force.
Swaaash!
The sheer pressure warped the space around it.
A towering blade of Sword Force swept through the enemies clad in black armor.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The ground heaved with a deafening crash, and flesh and bone scattered in every direction.
Yet even after witnessing the grisly sight from point-blank range, the followers who had begun worshiping a new god called the Lord of Heaven didn’t so much as blink.
No—more precisely, they kept advancing, gazing at the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord with hazy eyes as though entranced.
All the while, they murmured their eight-character creed without pause.
“In heaven and on earth.”
“All demons bow in submission...”
CRUNCH!
Their hollow, almost chilling voices ended only when they died.
At least, that was what the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord believed in that moment.
Gurgle.
Blood bubbled in a follower’s slashed throat.
His neck had been cut by the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s sword, yet he went on muttering as the light slowly faded from his eyes.
“Heaven above... gurgle... hea...”
THUNK!
The creed stopped only when the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord drove his sword into the man’s chest.
A chill ran down his spine.
They’re no ordinary people.
Of course they weren’t.
Even when the Heavenly Demon swept across the Central Plains, the hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path gathered under him had been half-mad fanatics.
But the enemies the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had faced back then had at least known fear.
They, too, had possessed an emotion every human ought to have.
But what in the world...
Then he understood what had felt so familiar.
Fear.
They had no fear.
Though they clearly knew he was a stronger opponent they could never defeat, the followers of Dark Heaven kept surging toward him as though they had been born for this very moment.
Spraying red blood instead of white sea foam.
Screeeee!
The tip of his sword swept toward the enemies closing in from every direction.
The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.
The Zhongnan Sect’s signature sword art, a technique of Supreme Peak mastery, swept through the space around him.
Weapons and bodies met its razor-sharp Force and were cut apart like tofu, their pieces scattering across the snow.
SHING!
THUD-THUD!
Corpses collapsed amid the sickening sounds of torn flesh.
Yet one enemy, his chest deeply cut along with one arm, didn’t crumple with a groan of pain.
He reached out with his one remaining hand.
BOOM!
A sharp whistle split the air, and the hem of the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s robe burst apart.
He narrowly avoided the palm strike and thrust out his hand at blinding speed.
THUNK!
Only after the Zhongnan Sect’s famed Heavenly Vault Finger Qi pierced the man between the brows did he collapse.
But though he had dispatched dozens of enemies in less than a moment, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s face remained rigid.
This is...
There was no doubt.
They had no fear, and they could barely feel pain.
He didn’t know whether some secret technique or a drug that clouded the mind was responsible, but this was far beyond the bounds of common sense.
And there were tens of thousands of them.
They felt neither fear nor pain, and each was a skilled martial artist.
They were weapons made to sweep across a battlefield.
This is bad.
No—this is the worst.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord bit his lip, feeling a fear he hadn’t known since the Great Faction War.
Then—
Swoooosh!
Along with a rush of overlapping whistles, an immense force tore into one side of the battlefield.
KWA-BOOOOM!
A sudden crash sent countless scraps of flesh flying in every direction.
The Zhongnan Sect disciples had formed a tight sword formation around the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
Now the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord watched it shatter in an instant, his eyes wide.
“No!”
“J-Junior Sister!”
Their cries were almost screams.
Stunned by the loss of fellow disciples they had known since childhood, they stared blankly at the enemy who had broken their formation with a single blow.
Two men covered in pitch black from head to toe.
No—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had called them Black Ghosts, and the name suited these unknown beings all too well.
Sssaaaaa.
Black energy rose in threads around their bodies, swallowing the air.
The Zhongnan Sect disciples began to tremble without realizing it.
The energy gripped their hearts and locked their limbs.
“Hngh...”
Strained breaths escaped all around.
Everyone was crushed beneath their chilling aura—an overwhelming force known as Fear somewhere far away.
No—almost everyone.
SHWOOF!
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord closed the distance in an instant, more furious than he had ever been.
Dozens of disciples had died in the blink of an eye.
The people he was duty-bound to protect as Sect Leader—the future pillars of the Zhongnan Sect, whom he had watched grow since childhood—had been cut down in an instant.
“How dare you!”
SHWING-SHWING-SHWING!
His sword tip cut through the air, driven by fury.
The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, honed to nine-tenths mastery, sent dozens of sword images pouring forth.
Then they vanished without a trace.
Whoooosh!
CLANG!
The moment those immense forces collided, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s eyes widened.
His beloved sword, which had cut through the wind, was being knocked aside by an axe blade swinging with the wind, erasing his sword images as it swept through them.
“What is this...!”
GRRRK.
KWAANG!
Before the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord could finish his cry of shock, the blade finally gave way to the immense force and was sent flying.
It trembled violently.
KRRUNCH!
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord slid back, his foot carving a deep furrow in the ground.
He barely steadied himself, pain stabbing through his wrist.
Far worse than the pain was the shock.
“Y-You...”
The words stumbled from his lips.
He stared at the Black Ghost gripping a battle axe as large as a grown man, his eyes so wide they seemed ready to pop out.
No.
It can’t be.
He tried to deny it, but there was no denying what stood before him.
The Black Ghost who had stopped the Zhongnan Sect Leader single-handedly had a face he remembered.
He hadn’t recognized it at first.
Now he did.
That crude, strangely shaped weapon.
Those features, horribly twisted and discolored, yet still faintly recognizable.
“...Black Axe Fiend.”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord murmured the name, stunned.
A great fiend of the Demonic Cult whom he and his master had faced on the battlefield long ago.
A Supreme Peak master who had first taught him the fear of death.
And...
“He should have died.”
One of the twenty-four great fiends under the Heavenly Demon, who had met his end right there on that day.
“Then... how?”
It was impossible.
It should never have happened.
But the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s questions went unanswered.
A fierce rush of air swept toward him, dragging him back to the present.
Screeeee—CRUNCH!
A neck was severed.
Blood sprayed into the air.
A middle-aged first-generation disciple, one marked as a future Elder, lost his head in a single stroke.
Gritting his teeth, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord kicked off the ground.
“Senior Brothers!”
His shout carried internal energy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1033
paragraphs: Every martial art contains at least dozens of movements, each with its own principles.
But no matter what martial art you’ve learned, there are ultimately only two ways to deal with an enemy’s attack.
Block it, or dodge it.
And in that moment, I chose the latter.
KWA-BOOOOM! KRRRUNCH!
A flash came hurtling in with a fierce whistle and slammed into the ground.
The earth buckled as if an earthquake had struck, and a tremendous shock wave swept through the area.
At least a dozen enemies were caught in its wake and vanished without a trace. I’d escaped with only a few scratches from flying bits of rock, yet a chill ran down my spine.
Fast. And powerful.
It was hard to believe a javelin thrown from so far away could move that fast and hit that hard.
Dodging had hardly been a choice. I’d had no other option.
If I’d met it with a counterattack, that alone would have cost me a considerable amount of strength.
Jeok Cheongang, standing beside me, knew it too.
“I suspected as much, but those bastards certainly don’t have ordinary internal energy.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered in a low voice and clenched his fist.
Following his gaze, I saw four ghost horses approaching, each carrying a rider as they stepped through the air.
“Four, huh? How many passed us by earlier?”
The Great Snow Mountain region might not be as vast as the Qilian Mountains, but it was still enormous.

The frost-covered land at the foot of the mountain was broad enough for a battle like this, with countless enemies and allies tangled together. Jeok Cheongang and I had punched through the enemy lines ahead of everyone else like a single awl, but we couldn’t stop them all.
Besides, the surest way to win a battle was to cut off the head, not the body.
“If I saw right, two.”
I recalled the distant crash and tremor that had reached me before the javelin came flying.
Judging by their direction and distance...
“I think those two headed toward the Zhongnan Sect.”

The Zhongnan Sect numbered only a thousand among our thirty thousand, but every one of them was an elite disciple of the main sect, not a lay affiliate. With three Supreme Peak masters among them, they were a formidable force.
If the enemy wanted to secure victory, stopping them would be crucial.
“Then that makes five, counting the ones who’ve just appeared.”
We’d already let two slip past, and now four more had shown up.
But as far as we knew, there were seven of these monsters called Death Knights—or Black Ghosts—in all.
I adjusted my grip on White Flame and murmured, “One’s unaccounted for.”
“Then the last one...”
“Either guarding the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, or headed toward the Gansu martial artists led by Sima Gong. If it isn’t the latter...”
I let my voice trail off, but Jeok Cheongang already knew about Sima Gong’s suspicious behavior. He needed no further explanation.
“Then Sima Gong, that damned unorthodox bastard, has thrown in his lot with Dark Heaven.”
Exactly.
A Black Ghost not going after Sima Gong’s forces wouldn’t prove it on its own. But there was no denying it would make betrayal far more likely.
If I were the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, I wouldn’t bother sending a Black Ghost to Sima Gong if he was already an ally.
Especially...
With forces like these.
I watched the Black Ghosts draw closer, radiating a terrifying aura.
Armed with a saber, a sword, a spear, and a chain sickle, they sprang over the heads of the advancing enemy soldiers and shot toward us.
Each was a Supreme Peak master powerful enough to shake an entire city. They felt neither pain nor emotion, and their ability to recover was beyond human.
No—they were monsters through and through. Strange beings the likes of which no one in Murim had ever encountered.
“Old Master.”
“Nothing more to say.”
KRRUNCH!
Jeok Cheongang smashed the head of an enemy charging at him with soulless eyes in a single punch. Then he went on.
“I don’t know what kind of monsters those things are, but we’ll just keep killing them until they’re dead.”
The instant those quiet words left his lips—
Pop.
We kicked off the ground together and shot forward, striking with all our strength.
I swept out White Flame’s spearhead, dark-blue Force surging around it. Jeok Cheongang thrust out a palm wreathed in pure white flames.
FWOOOOSH!
A brilliant flash enveloped everything within a radius of a dozen or so jang. The waves of fanatics flooding in from every direction parted.
No—they evaporated.
KWAANG! KRRRUNCH!
The ground shook with a crash that sounded as if the sky itself had split.
Bodies charred in an instant by the Flame Divine Palm’s terrible heat crumpled lifelessly. Others, cut apart along with their weapons by my spear, flew away in pieces.
They had been stripped of pain and emotion, but death came equally to the hundred or so enemies who lost their lives in that moment.
And through the gap in the battlefield, blanketed in death in an instant—
Ssshh...
Four Black Ghosts rushed toward Jeok Cheongang and me, shrouded in an aura of death like dim night fog.
SHWING!
The wind split around the blades sweeping toward us with terrifying force.
Each took a direction—north, south, east, west—and struck. Their attacks meshed like finely crafted gears, leaving not the slightest opening.
But...
There is one. I’m sure of it.
I took a long step forward to meet the saber blade and spearhead streaking toward me, their outlines blurred by speed.
Straight toward those two chilling flashes aimed at my neck.
Fear of death chilled my spine, but I held fast to my conviction.
“What are you doing—!”
And just as Jeok Cheongang’s urgent shout rang out—
Pshk!
The two weapons grazed either side of my neck, leaving the faintest cuts. Forgetting even that moment’s pain, I smiled.
Just as I thought.
I hadn’t dodged their attacks.
In the life-or-death moment just now, the two Black Ghosts had forced their weapons to twist and change course.
Why?
Simple.
They weren’t allowed to kill me.
Their commander on this battlefield—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—had given them that order.
The Three Elders of Tianshan couldn’t have done that.
No, that wasn’t right.
They wouldn’t have done it.
Unlike the Black Ghosts, they still had their emotions and reason. Their own lives would have mattered a hundred, a thousand times more to them than carrying out an order.
They would have known that making even this tiny mistake to capture me would lead straight to their deaths.
Just like now.
SHWOOOSH!
I didn’t miss the opening that had been invisible until they exposed it themselves.
THUD!
A Black Ghost went rigid as a statue.
White Flame’s spearhead pierced its throat, and the four jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi I’d sent through it erupted.
KABOOOM!
Flames exploded.
Before the headless Black Ghost could fall from its saddle, another belatedly realized its comrade was in danger. It twisted the saber that had passed beside my neck and swung.
SHNK!
Hot. The force of the wind alone sliced into my shoulder, sending blood gushing from the wound.
But when you lose something, you gain something too.
KRRUNCH.
A touch so cold it sent a shiver through me.
With my free hand, I seized the wrist encased in jet-black armor and twisted it without hesitation, as though wringing it dry.
CRACK. KRRUNCH.
Flesh and bone crushed with a sickening, wet sound.
The Black Ghosts had grown stronger through death and rebirth. I had surpassed human limits by surviving countless brushes with death.
So they weren’t the only monsters here.
KRRRUNCH!
I ripped off its wrist, the weapon still gripped in its hand, and drove my fist into the Black Ghost as it stood frozen.
KWAANG!
The body went flying, trailing a foul, burnt stench as its black armor shattered.
But I knew.
I knew what kind of monsters they were, and how tenacious and dreadful the cursed life they’d been given could be.
Step.
Leaving Jeok Cheongang to fight the other two Black Ghosts, I walked toward the ones already staggering to their feet.
“Fine. Let’s find out.”
Ssshh...
Dusky mist rose around their bodies, regenerating the arm I’d torn away, the flesh and bone melted and crumbled by flames—even the missing neck.
“Which of us is the bigger monster?”
SHWOOOOSH—SHNK!
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Fire blazed around the dazzling white spearhead. The strike flashed through the mist like lightning, becoming a dark-blue wave that cleaved through them.
“Magnificent. Absolutely magnificent!”
Like a child given a toy he loved on his birthday, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord watched the battlefield spread before him, his face flushed with excitement.
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!

From the high hill to the snowy plain in the distance, a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords danced across hundreds of jang. Those gleaming blades, forged and tempered again and again for a single purpose, were finally doing their work.
THUD!
“AAAGH!”
Amid the shouts and screams pouring in from every direction, crimson blood sprayed over everyone’s heads like a fountain.
Dozens of lives vanished with one breath in. With one breath out, their places were filled.
Even now, death followed death without end across the horrific battlefield. It was enough to stir the nostalgia of someone who’d spent so many years confined to the lands beyond the desert.
“This is it. This is what I wanted...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord murmured as if half in a daze. His eyes had grown hazy and moist.
How he’d missed it.
How he’d longed for it.

In the distant past, he’d led a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path across the land at the side of the one called the Heavenly Demon. But those memories weren’t especially pleasant for the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Even then, he’d been nothing more than a hunting dog mad for blood, and the Heavenly Demon had given him little authority to command.
Now things were different.
His new master had given the Blood-Sword Demon Lord power over the lives and deaths of tens of thousands.
All he’d been given was one simple condition: under no circumstances was he to kill Jin Taekyung.
To show me such absolute trust...
The seven Black Ghosts he’d been given were proof enough.
And besides...
With them there, we cannot lose this battle. Not under any circumstances.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked away from the battlefield toward the white-robed figures under heavy guard not far away.
They were no less formidable than the Black Ghosts. Perhaps they would prove an even greater force.
