In the life-or-death moment just now, the two Black Ghosts had forced their weapons to twist and change course.
Why?
Simple.
They weren’t allowed to kill me.
Their commander on this battlefield—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—had given them that order.
The Three Elders of Tianshan couldn’t have done that.
No, that wasn’t right.
They wouldn’t have done it.
Unlike the Black Ghosts, they still had their emotions and reason.
Their own lives would have mattered a hundred, a thousand times more to them than carrying out an order.
They would have known that making even this tiny mistake to capture me would lead straight to their deaths.
Just like now.
SHWOOOSH!
I didn’t miss the opening that had been invisible until they exposed it themselves.
THUD!
A Black Ghost went rigid as a statue.
White Flame’s spearhead pierced its throat, and the four jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi I’d sent through it erupted.
KABOOOM!
Flames exploded.
Before the headless Black Ghost could fall from its saddle, another belatedly realized its comrade was in danger.
It twisted the saber that had passed beside my neck and swung.
SHNK!
Hot.
The force of the wind alone sliced into my shoulder, sending blood gushing from the wound.
But when you lose something, you gain something too.
KRRUNCH.
A touch so cold it sent a shiver through me.
With my free hand, I seized the wrist encased in jet-black armor and twisted it without hesitation, as though wringing it dry.
CRACK.
KRRUNCH.
Flesh and bone crushed with a sickening, wet sound.
The Black Ghosts had grown stronger through death and rebirth.
I had surpassed human limits by surviving countless brushes with death.
So they weren’t the only monsters here.
KRRRUNCH!
I ripped off its wrist, the weapon still gripped in its hand, and drove my fist into the Black Ghost as it stood frozen.
KWAANG!
The body went flying, trailing a foul, burnt stench as its black armor shattered.
But I knew.
I knew what kind of monsters they were, and how tenacious and dreadful the cursed life they’d been given could be.
Step.
Leaving Jeok Cheongang to fight the other two Black Ghosts, I walked toward the ones already staggering to their feet.
“Fine.
Let’s find out.”
Ssshh...
Dusky mist rose around their bodies, regenerating the arm I’d torn away, the flesh and bone melted and crumbled by flames—even the missing neck.
“Which of us is the bigger monster?”
SHWOOOOSH—SHNK!
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Fire blazed around the dazzling white spearhead.
The strike flashed through the mist like lightning, becoming a dark-blue wave that cleaved through them.
“Magnificent.
Absolutely magnificent!”
Like a child given a toy he loved on his birthday, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord watched the battlefield spread before him, his face flushed with excitement.
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
From the high hill to the snowy plain in the distance, a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords danced across hundreds of jang.
Those gleaming blades, forged and tempered again and again for a single purpose, were finally doing their work.
THUD!
“AAAGH!”
Amid the shouts and screams pouring in from every direction, crimson blood sprayed over everyone’s heads like a fountain.
Dozens of lives vanished with one breath in.
With one breath out, their places were filled.
Even now, death followed death without end across the horrific battlefield.
It was enough to stir the nostalgia of someone who’d spent so many years confined to the lands beyond the desert.
“This is it.
This is what I wanted...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord murmured as if half in a daze.
His eyes had grown hazy and moist.
How he’d missed it.
How he’d longed for it.
In the distant past, he’d led a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path across the land at the side of the one called the Heavenly Demon.
But those memories weren’t especially pleasant for the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Even then, he’d been nothing more than a hunting dog mad for blood, and the Heavenly Demon had given him little authority to command.
Now things were different.
His new master had given the Blood-Sword Demon Lord power over the lives and deaths of tens of thousands.
All he’d been given was one simple condition: under no circumstances was he to kill Jin Taekyung.
To show me such absolute trust...
The seven Black Ghosts he’d been given were proof enough.
And besides...
With them there, we cannot lose this battle.
Not under any circumstances.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked away from the battlefield toward the white-robed figures under heavy guard not far away.
They were no less formidable than the Black Ghosts.
Perhaps they would prove an even greater force.

chapters.title: Chapter 1034
paragraphs: Dressed from head to toe in white so pure it looked almost unnatural, they stood out among Dark Heaven’s pitch-black ranks.
Their sleeves were so long and full they dragged on the ground. Veils hid most of their faces.
Wrapped without a gap in what looked less like clothing than great swaths of silk, they watched the battlefield in silence. Even the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was unaccustomed to the sight of them.
No—in a way, they made him uncomfortable.
Unlike the Black Ghosts—former comrades who had shared meals with him before becoming mindless killing machines—the white-robed figures answered not to him, but to “that person.”
If that were all, it might have been easier to bear.
A moment ago, his eyes had been bright as he watched blood spread across the battlefield. Now displeasure flickered through them.
Such a magnificent battlefield right before me, and I have to stand here watching.
It was more than displeasure. He was beginning to feel downright offended.
His gaze swept over the twenty white-robed figures and stopped on one of them. He remembered the quiet voice that had halted him when he had eagerly moved to the front fifteen minutes earlier.
“Demon Lord, please be patient a little longer. The time is not yet ripe.”
Had anyone said that to him during the Great Faction War, he would have torn open the fool’s mouth and ripped out his tongue.
But fifty years was a long time. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had grown a little more mature.
More precisely, fear and reverence for his new master, the Lord of Heaven, had stayed his feet and checked his murderous impulse.
Damn it.
There was a simple reason the slender figure he was glaring at had survived daring to interfere with him.
If not for that person...

She led the white-robed figures and had served the Lord of Heaven even more closely than he had. Born killer though he was, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord could hardly use a mere slight as grounds to strike her down.
That did not mean he could swallow his irritation.
“They’re holding up rather well. If I’d stepped in sooner, the battle would have swung decisively in our favor by now.”
His gaze and voice made the mockery plain. Neither the figure he had singled out nor anyone around her replied.
Their silence stoked the anger he had been struggling to contain.
“Strange, isn’t it? You stepped in without a care when you shouldn’t have. Now you’re acting like you’ve swallowed your tongue.”
His snake-like pupils narrowed further, still fixed on her.
“Or does that mean you’d like to stay silent forever?”
At the sound of his low voice, the figure finally parted her lips.
“What answer do you want from me, Demon Lord?”
Her reply was calm, without a hint of a tremor. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s brow twitched.
“I command this army. I came here to carry out that person’s will.”
“I know. I was there, too.”
“And yet you, a mere woman, dare to give me orders?”
“I gave no order. I only tried to dissuade you.”
Beneath the white silk veil, her cherry-red lips moved again.
“And that is what that person wishes, too.”
At the unexpected reply, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s face went rigid.
“What... did you say?”
“I said that is what that person wishes.”
“That person—the great Lord of Heaven—doesn’t want me to step in? What is that supposed to...”
He trailed off in disbelief. The woman gave a small shake of her head, and the pure-white veil swayed. Its embroidered pattern was beautiful, yet somehow uncanny.
“You misunderstand. That person simply wishes you to come to no harm, if possible.”
“Harm? Me, of all people?”
For a moment, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord doubted his ears.
It was an unbearably humiliating thing to hear—as a martial artist, and as a subordinate who had devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving someone.
He commanded more than thirty thousand demonic soldiers, the Three Elders of Tianshan—three hunting dogs who had admittedly outlived their usefulness—and seven Black Ghosts besides.
And that was not all.
He hadn’t yet revealed the full extent of his strength, but the Blood-Sword Demon Lord himself had reached the realm of supreme mastery, making him one of the greatest masters alive.
The enemy, by contrast, fell short in every respect: in the number of Supreme Peak masters who could turn a battle, in the quality of their soldiers, and in sheer momentum.
The scales were tipped already. They had been tipping even before the battle began, and they were still tipping now.
So why was that woman spouting such nonsense? Why cast a boulder into his heart and crack his certainty that he had his master’s complete trust?
“Will you stake your life on what you just said?”
His eyes and voice had gone cold. The woman’s answer barely changed.
“That person’s care for you is as vast as the sea. Please, try to understand his wishes.”
It was as good as an admission.
A faint smile touched the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s lips.
“That person cares for me. Yes, I should understand.”
The smile on his face didn’t look like a smile at all. The woman’s voice turned urgent.
“As you know, four Demon Lords and Demon Empresses have already met their ends. That person needs at least one more loyal servant to carry out his great cause...”
“Enough. All you mean to say is that I shouldn’t act rashly.”
“...Demon Lord, that is not—”
“Enough. Hold your tongue. I understand that person’s wishes perfectly well now.”
He spoke evenly, but the thoughts left behind by the storm in his mind were anything but calm.
You are watching me yourself, and this is all you think I’m capable of?
Crack.
The joints of his clenched hand popped. His fist had gone white, and his nails began to dig into his skin.
I have served you with all I have. I followed you more faithfully than anyone.

He remembered the day he first met the Lord of Heaven. The trembling born of unimaginable fear and reverence, the shock that had made him think his heart might stop—he remembered it as clearly as if it had happened yesterday.
Though I was not given the post I wanted, I have lived these fifty years and more solely to serve your great cause.
The Great Faction War.
When the Heavenly Demon met his end at the Martial God’s hands near the close of that long war, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had not been shaken in the slightest.
Of course he hadn’t. The Heavenly Demon he had known was only human.
The ambition that had once seemed so grand, the martial might that had forced the young Blood-Sword Demon Lord to his knees—both had lost their luster after he met the Lord of Heaven.
He had felt no sorrow. He had been glad to find a master truly worthy of his service.
Glad until five other great fiends took seats above him in the newly risen Dark Heaven.
Even then, I simply obeyed you.
He’d understood without a word.

The Western Heaven Demon Lord had outranked him in the Demonic Cult, so his position was justified. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord and the North Heaven Demon Lord were daggers planted deep in the Central Plains; the importance of their roles warranted high standing.
He could understand the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and the Blood Lord as well.
Discontent had taken root in his heart, but their positions were his master’s will.
But...
Now, before it’s too late, you should have trusted me at least a little.

The four Demon Lords and Demon Empress the Lord of Heaven had trusted so deeply had all met their ends. They had failed their missions spectacularly, then left this world before anyone could even call them to account.
At last, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s turn had come.
Together with the Blood Lord, who had stubbornly survived, he had finally become one of the Lord of Heaven’s two arms. Whether he was the right or the left hardly mattered.
His master’s trust and the opportunity he had been given—that was all he had wanted.
That was all.
But what was there to worry about so much?
None of the dead Demon Lords or the Demon Empress had led an army like his. None had commanded seven Black Ghosts and tens of thousands of soldiers.
He had every condition for victory that they had lacked. Yet his master still did not trust him fully.
He could hear that distrust in the words of the woman dressed in snow-white robes.
“Did you trust me so little?”
The lament meant to remain in his heart slipped between his lips.
KWA-BOOOOM!

A pillar of fire shot skyward with a roar that seemed to split the heavens. Even from dozens of jang away, where the Blood-Sword Demon Lord stood, it was unmistakable. It could be seen from anywhere on the battlefield—immense, raging, and merciless.
GRRRRRR!
A violent tremor traveled through the ground.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had turned at the sudden wave of power even before the roar reached him. He took in the scene and murmured to his absent master once more.
“If you’d trusted me just a little more, this battle might already have been over.”
“Demon Lord...!”
“What? Am I not allowed even this much of a complaint?”
He answered the woman’s urgent cry without looking back. His eyes were on the haze rising in the distance—or rather, on the two figures streaking through the terrible heat that had produced it.
KRAK, BOOM!
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
Each punch and palm strike burst the murky black fog apart. As the fog gathered to repair the damage, dark-blue Force slashed through it from every direction.
SHHK—KWA-BOOOOM!
Four Black Ghosts staggered again and again. Dark energy welled from the severed ends of their limbs like blood of another color. They looked unmistakably like humans on the verge of death.
No—the Blood-Sword Demon Lord knew it instinctively.
Eternal death was finally coming for them, too.
Goooooong.
Space suddenly began to distort. Great Force surged around the white spearhead, rising and rolling in waves.
Like...
A dragon.
And at the moment the Blood-Sword Demon Lord muttered those words to himself, the spear, now one with its master, fell toward the Black Ghosts like a bolt of lightning.
SHWAAASH!
Heavenly Strike.
The distant flash swept through a radius of dozens of jang, bathing everything in light and shaking the ground. In its wake, nothing remained.
Not the four Black Ghosts. Not the followers who had kept charging at the master and his disciple without pause.
Only one thing remained: the resolve of a born killer determined to prove himself to his master.
SHING.
A sharp sound brushed the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s ear.

chapters.title: Chapter 1035
paragraphs: Ding. Ding. Ding.
Clear chimes rang in my ears. At the same moment, System notifications confirmed the results of my actions, and new vitality welled up from deep within me.

System Defeated Lv. 152 Go Gwangryung! Defeated Lv. 150 Jeok Hwanyang! Defeated Lv. 155 Pung Sogwi! Defeated Lv. 160 Hwang Dokso! Acquired a massive amount of EXP and Fame! Level Up! The effects of leveling up have restored all energy, cured all status conditions, and healed some injuries!
Shaaah.
Was this what it felt like to wash yourself from head to toe in a cool mountain stream on a sweltering summer day?
I took a deep breath as the exhaustion of that brief but fierce fight melted away all at once.
Whew.
But it wasn’t a sigh of relief at having taken down four Black Ghosts.
It was only a breath to steady myself while I waited for the one person still standing—the one we had to defeat to win this battle.
“Old Master.”
“Yeah.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded at my brief call.
“He’s coming.”
At that moment—
Clack, clack, clack.
The Dark Heaven followers had never seemed to grow fewer, no matter how many we killed. Even after the Black Ghosts fell, those fanatics had kept closing in around us. Now they stopped in unison.
Then they opened a path with grave, orderly movements.
A path for just one person.
Step. Step.
“My apologies. I’m later than I intended.”
His footsteps and calm voice carried clearly, even from a distance.
I shrugged at the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Thump.
I kicked the remains of what had been called Black Ghosts—now scattered into dozens of large and small fragments.
“If you’re sorry, go kill yourself.”
“That would be difficult.”
“Figured. Anyway, I’m fine. I was playing with your friends.”
“Friends? If you mean the trash lying there, you’re mistaken.”
“Trash?”

“Every one of them was pathetic. During the Great Faction War, they either ran wild like reckless brats who didn’t know their place and got themselves killed, or failed to recognize the true Heaven and raised their swords against it.”
That gave me an idea of what the Black Ghosts—the Death Knights who had appeared here today—had been in life.
“They were Demonic Cult fiends. You used to eat from the same pot.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord nodded readily.
“Once. A very long time ago.”
I’d suspected as much.
Everything that came into being had a cause. To make Death Knights this powerful, you obviously needed people of comparable stature to make them from.
“No wonder. Even their names sound like they belonged to a bunch of lowlife bastards.”
“Their names?”
“Go Gwangryung, Jeok Hwanyang, Pung Sogwi, Hwang Dokso... No one with a normal head comes up with names like those. Right?”
The names came out without a moment’s hesitation. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked at me in surprise.
“How strange. How do you know their names?”
“What, weren’t they famous? Just hearing their names puts me in a shitty mood. I can practically tell what kind of lives they led.”
“There was a time when everyone in the Central Plains knew of them. By their sobriquets, that is. But...”

The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked between Jeok Cheongang and me before adding, “A martial artist is known by their martial arts and sobriquet, not their name. Even back then, very few knew those men’s real names. Even with someone who’s spent many years gaining experience at your side, you couldn’t have learned those names.”
He sounded certain.
And for good reason. Xinjiang, once the Demonic Cult’s stronghold and now Dark Heaven’s home, had always been that kind of place.
A Land of Ruin where no one could set foot without permission.
A religious state beyond the desert, whose veil even the Hidden Shadow Pavilion had managed to lift only a little, after long and meticulous preparation.
But I was different.
I could read information no one else knew, even if it was only in fragments.
As long as the subject was in front of me.
And as long as the gap between our strength and abilities wasn’t too great.
Shaaah!
At that moment, a blue circle I couldn’t see swallowed up the space around us in a flash of light, responding to my will.
Qi Sense, now nine-tenths mastered, reached out from me and washed an area more than fifty jang in radius in blue.
Ding. Ding-ding-ding.
Countless System windows appeared over the heads of the hundreds—no, thousands—of enemies within Qi Sense’s range.
But my gaze stayed fixed on one person.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had stopped walking the instant Qi Sense activated.
System Lv. 170 Chuk Banghyeol
I could clearly make out the Level window above his head from more than twenty jang away.
I could see his furrowed brow and puzzled expression, too.
“What in the world did you just—”
Qi Sense wasn’t a term exclusive to me. Martial artists who had reached a certain realm routinely gauged and read their own qi and that of others.
But Qi Sense as part of the System felt different from theirs.
“What did you do?”
His voice had dropped. The warmth had gone from his tone.
I grinned at him.
“Our Banghyeol sure has a lot of questions. Is it because you’re still in your prime?”
“Oh, was that name a secret too? Why do you fiends have so much to hide?”
Jeok Cheongang had experienced my Qi Sense when we first met in Shanxi Province. He clicked his tongue and joined in.
“You may not know this, but that thing feels pretty damn unpleasant. The first time, even I thought some bizarre dark art had been used on me.”
“But he’s a fiend. Shouldn’t dark arts feel familiar to him?”
“Well...”
Jeok Cheongang studied the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s rigid face before answering.
“Maybe he’s embarrassed. Even from what little I’ve heard, it’s not a very good name. Banghyeol? That’s supposed to be a person’s name? Sounds like a fart.”
“Come on. Even if you’re old enough to have shoved your years up your ass, you can’t make fun of him for that. That man’s probably almost a hundred himself.”
“You wait till you’re old. Sometimes you feel strange for no reason. Who knows? Maybe he sits under the moon every night with tears in his eyes.”
“Oh.”
The idea that a notorious great fiend had finally entered menopause was pretty interesting. But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s next words wiped the look from my face.
“You’re right, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
“What?”
“Didn’t you just say it yourself? That dark arts ought to be familiar to him.”
He gazed down at his hands, as though trying to recall the sensation my Qi Sense had left behind.
“I see. It’s a little different from what I know, but it does feel familiar.”
My eyes widened before I could stop them.
Different, but familiar.
The meaning of those few words was becoming clearer. So was the source of the unease rising within me.
“At first, I was surprised. Now I finally understand why that person watched you so closely.”
Step. Step. Splash.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord crossed the dry, frozen ground and stepped into a pool of blood.
Plip.
Blood splashed with his roughened stride.
A powerful energy covered the slowly rising blade, thicker and more viscous than the blood itself.
“But this time, that person was wrong. I should have handled this myself from the start. There was never any need to stop me or worry about me.”
Wooooong.
I felt something change around the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Not because the wind had stopped and the air was trembling.
Not because the sword in his grip was roaring as it poured out immense Force.
Beep.
System Lv. 175 Chuk Banghyeol
It had changed.
The qi he gave off. The number in his Level window.
This is...
I knew instinctively.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord hadn’t simply been concealing his strength through Returning to Simplicity.
He definitely, definitely wasn’t this strong before.
We had clashed once before the battle began in earnest. Jeok Cheongang and I had fought at full strength, and so had the Blood-Sword Demon Lord. The result had been clear: he was at a disadvantage.
So why?
Beep.
System Lv. 178 Chuk Banghyeol
How?
Beep.
System Lv. 180 Chuk Banghyeol
How was the Blood-Sword Demon Lord growing stronger even now, as he slowly approached us?
“What in the world... What dark art are you using?”
There was no way a master wouldn’t feel what his Disciple felt.
Jeok Cheongang’s question cast light on the unease that had been swelling inside me.
Dark arts.
A dark, devious technique, just as the words themselves meant.
Those who used them had strayed from the straight and righteous path into demonic, heterodox arts. And those who dwelled deepest in that abyss belonged to what people called—
The Demonic Path.
People who rejected life as humans and chose the path of demons.
Then what should the dark arts wielded by beings so full of incomprehensible mysteries be called?
How had those beings known as Black Ghosts come into existence, and appeared here?
“What?”
“It’s not dark arts.”
The words slipped from my lips in a dazed murmur.
Jeok Cheongang’s repeated questions grew distant, like echoes. For a moment, I even forgot the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s presence, growing stronger with every step he took toward us.
As if entranced, I looked at the white-robed figures.
Until now, his presence had obscured them. They were only a tiny part of this vast battlefield, where the fighting still raged.
No. Like the Black Ghosts, they possessed power that should not exist in this world.
“Magic.”
And the moment that familiar, unbelievable word slipped from my lips—
“Power of the Wind Ghost.”
A chant rang out clearly from far away.
“Dwell within him.”
The spell, imbued with intent, manifested in the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s body.

sentences.text: Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
Clear chimes rang in my ears.
At the same moment, System notifications confirmed the results of my actions, and new vitality welled up from deep within me.
System Defeated Lv.
152 Go Gwangryung!
Defeated Lv.
150 Jeok Hwanyang!
Defeated Lv.
155 Pung Sogwi!
Defeated Lv.
160 Hwang Dokso!
Acquired a massive amount of EXP and Fame!
Level Up!
The effects of leveling up have restored all energy, cured all status conditions, and healed some injuries!
Shaaah.
Was this what it felt like to wash yourself from head to toe in a cool mountain stream on a sweltering summer day?
I took a deep breath as the exhaustion of that brief but fierce fight melted away all at once.
Whew.
But it wasn’t a sigh of relief at having taken down four Black Ghosts.
It was only a breath to steady myself while I waited for the one person still standing—the one we had to defeat to win this battle.
“Old Master.”
“Yeah.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded at my brief call.
“He’s coming.”
At that moment—
Clack, clack, clack.
The Dark Heaven followers had never seemed to grow fewer, no matter how many we killed.
Even after the Black Ghosts fell, those fanatics had kept closing in around us.
Now they stopped in unison.
Then they opened a path with grave, orderly movements.
A path for just one person.
Step.
Step.
“My apologies.
I’m later than I intended.”
His footsteps and calm voice carried clearly, even from a distance.
I shrugged at the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Thump.
I kicked the remains of what had been called Black Ghosts—now scattered into dozens of large and small fragments.
“If you’re sorry, go kill yourself.”
“That would be difficult.”
“Figured.
Anyway, I’m fine.
I was playing with your friends.”
“Friends?
If you mean the trash lying there, you’re mistaken.”
“Trash?”
“Every one of them was pathetic.

During the Great Faction War, they either ran wild like reckless brats who didn’t know their place and got themselves killed, or failed to recognize the true Heaven and raised their swords against it.”
That gave me an idea of what the Black Ghosts—the Death Knights who had appeared here today—had been in life.
“They were Demonic Cult fiends.
You used to eat from the same pot.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord nodded readily.
“Once.
A very long time ago.”
I’d suspected as much.
Everything that came into being had a cause.
To make Death Knights this powerful, you obviously needed people of comparable stature to make them from.
“No wonder.
Even their names sound like they belonged to a bunch of lowlife bastards.”
“Their names?”
“Go Gwangryung, Jeok Hwanyang, Pung Sogwi, Hwang Dokso...
No one with a normal head comes up with names like those.
Right?”
The names came out without a moment’s hesitation.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked at me in surprise.
“How strange.
How do you know their names?”
“What, weren’t they famous?
Just hearing their names puts me in a shitty mood.
I can practically tell what kind of lives they led.”
“There was a time when everyone in the Central Plains knew of them.
By their sobriquets, that is.
But...”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked between Jeok Cheongang and me before adding, “A martial artist is known by their martial arts and sobriquet, not their name.
Even back then, very few knew those men’s real names.
Even with someone who’s spent many years gaining experience at your side, you couldn’t have learned those names.”
He sounded certain.
And for good reason.
Xinjiang, once the Demonic Cult’s stronghold and now Dark Heaven’s home, had always been that kind of place.
A Land of Ruin where no one could set foot without permission.
A religious state beyond the desert, whose veil even the Hidden Shadow Pavilion had managed to lift only a little, after long and meticulous preparation.
But I was different.
I could read information no one else knew, even if it was only in fragments.
As long as the subject was in front of me.
And as long as the gap between our strength and abilities wasn’t too great.
Shaaah!
At that moment, a blue circle I couldn’t see swallowed up the space around us in a flash of light, responding to my will.
Qi Sense, now nine-tenths mastered, reached out from me and washed an area more than fifty jang in radius in blue.
Ding.
Ding-ding-ding.
Countless System windows appeared over the heads of the hundreds—no, thousands—of enemies within Qi Sense’s range.
But my gaze stayed fixed on one person.

System Lv.

His voice had dropped.
The warmth had gone from his tone.
I grinned at him.

Is it because you’re still in your prime?”

chapters.title: Chapter 1036
paragraphs: Had I failed to guess it from the start? Or had I tried to deny it because the truth was so hard to believe?
This time, I could answer that question myself.
I think it was the latter.
It was true. All of it.
The realization struck my mind, leaving it blank as a sheet of paper.
At the same time, I felt the last shred of faith I’d held on to crumble, along with everything I’d thought I knew about this world.
The strange Moving Formation, whose existence had already been revealed long ago in Henan and Sichuan.
The Water God Dragon and countless Blood Fish, corrupted by something in Hubei and driven into a frenzy.
An utterly ordinary fisherman who’d eaten those Blood Fish and gained a monster’s appearance and strength.
The cause of all those phenomena—and not just that, but the rift that had appeared once more in the jungles of Nanman.
Even the familiar beings called Black Ghosts, whom I’d faced right here today.
And.
And...
At last, it was unmistakable.
It was unfolding right before my eyes. I could hear it, feel it flowing clearly through my senses.
All the warnings that had come before—call them signs, omens, whatever you wanted.
They had finally broken through a great dam and come crashing down on me, turning the suspicion I’d only entertained in private into certainty.
In two characters:
Magic.
Shaaah.
The wind blew. A shadow moving with speed and power far beyond human limits glided toward me, trailing a long afterimage.
But I couldn’t even twitch a finger.
In a world gone slow, with my whole body feeling as if the blood in it had turned cold, all I could do was stare, dumbfounded.
What is this...?
Where a massive bomb had exploded, nothing remained but ruins and the shock wave.
My mind was wreckage now. Words and questions scattered through it, caught in the blast.
Magic. Mage. Monster. Blood-Sword Demon Lord. Buff.
A large-scale attack spell. Allies sacrificed. Countless deaths, blood spilling everywhere, broken bodies floating in it.
How was any of this possible?
How had it come to this?
And finally—
What am I supposed to do now?
Every thought scattered. Only that question remained, and I had no answer.
Grab.
A hard, rough hand—one I knew—closed around my shoulder.
No. The instant I felt it, a powerful force had already dragged me backward, sending me stumbling without strength.
Only then did time begin to move again. A streak of light was swung through the gap like lightning.
Whoooom—KABOOM!
A roar like the sky splitting apart brought my senses rushing back.
I was already airborne somewhere behind where I’d stood. As I hung weightless, an enormous shock wave struck.
KRRRACK!
The ground heaved like an earthquake had hit. Two immense forces melted and shattered everything around them.

At the center of the clash, which swallowed dozens of jang in every direction, stood Jeok Cheongang. He had shoved me aside when I froze like a statue and stepped in to stop the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
“Hah!”
How had I flown so far already?
Even at this distance, I could tell Jeok Cheongang’s shout, charged with profound internal energy, was more than a battle cry.
That was for me. He’s trying to wake me up.
It reached my ears and jolted my half-dazed mind awake. At last, I let out the breath I’d been holding.
Right. It’s not over yet.
I still couldn’t understand how any of this could be happening. But with death right in front of me, what did understanding matter?
There was no use in understanding when the water had already spilled.
All I could do on this battlefield was accept what was happening and find a way through it.
That was how I’d save everyone.
Srrk.
Still suspended in the air, I twisted smoothly around.
My muscles and internal energy, fully restored by that last Level Up, obeyed the command in my mind without the slightest delay or error.
Now.
Boom—shwaaash!
I kicked off the air with a foot charged with qi and shot toward Jeok Cheongang, who was clashing with the Blood-Sword Demon Lord more than twenty jang away.
Or I tried to.
As I cut through the wind, an immense, invisible force descended on me.
Wooooong.
The air vanished. The wind vanished.
The instant I noticed, I heard a faint voice from far away.
“Taishan.”
I knew what that quiet invocation meant. My eyes widened, but I couldn’t stop the clear voice issuing from beneath a pure-white veil on a hill fifty jang away.
“Bring him down. Crush him.”
At that very moment—
Fwooom!
A weight as immense as Taishan bore down on my whole body.
No—it sent me plummeting.
Straight toward the countless enemies who had gathered like clouds during the brief moment I’d been airborne, their spears and bows aimed at me.
Gravity magic...!
I swallowed my cry of shock.
Instead of resisting this second, unexpected spell, I let it take hold and turned it into a weapon.
KWA-BOOM!
I struck the ground under the weight of ten thousand geun. The earth split, and the enemies around me staggered off balance. At the same time, I felt the pressure pinning me down dissipate.
Of course.
Gravity acted on an area, not a single person.
While I was airborne, I’d been the first to feel the spell’s effects. Once I landed, that was no longer true.
The white-robed figures were clearly mages. If they wanted to bind me even a little, their gravity magic would have to target the Dark Heaven followers who were their allies, too.
So they meant to delay me from joining Jeok Cheongang, even if only this way...
Fine by me.
The followers staggered like soulless wooden puppets. I turned in place and swept White Flame across them.
KWA-AAAH!
The spear’s passage through the air sounded more than fierce—outright destructive.
Anyone could swing a spear sideways. But none of the enemies surrounding me could stop the wave of Force that burst from White Flame’s translucent spearhead.
Not one.
SHHK! KRRRACK!
Everything was cut apart and crushed.
Weapons. People.
In the blink of an eye, the ground within a three-jang radius had become a field of death. Yet the fear had been stripped from them. They stared at me with dark, unseeing eyes and kept charging.
They murmured the eight-character creed as if entranced.
“Heaven above, earth below.”
“All demons bow.”
“Heaven above...”
CRUNCH!
A headless body toppled. My spear flashed sideways through three more enemies closing in from the flank.
SHK!
Weapons imbued with Sword Energy and bodies hardened by the external arts alike were helpless against overwhelming force.
I drove through the scattering fragments of steel and flesh without hesitation.
I streaked like lightning between the enemies blocking my way like a wall, thinking and commanding without pause.
Open Inventory. Summon. Summon. Summon.
SHHK, THUNK, KRRRACK!
I cut, stabbed, and crushed my way forward.
Weapons stayed in my hands only briefly. Each took one life, or two or three, before it left me. Countless more blades still lay hidden in that vast subspace whose limits I couldn’t begin to guess.
For a moment, the thought crossed my mind that perhaps I could make some ridiculous idea real.
No. There’s no way.
But why?
CLANG!
I knocked aside the weapons coming at me from every direction.
THWACK!
I crushed the head of an enemy approaching from my blind spot with a single punch.
SHWEEESH—SHHK!
And the more enemies I cut down, the stronger that inexplicable certainty grew.
Could this really be nothing more than a fantasy?
SHWAAASH!
I turned and swung my spear, leaving a mist of blood along its path.
As enemies surged in from every direction to fill the gap left by the dead, I took a short breath.
I won’t know until I try.
Thinking back, it had always been like this.
Every time I needed to break through a wall, I had to go beyond it. I had to make the impossible possible, turn imagination into reality.
Just as I would now.
Open Inventory.
One breath. That was all the time I needed.

With countless enemies still blocking my path, filling every space no matter how many I killed, I quietly closed my eyes. I pictured the mountain of sharp, gleaming steel somewhere in the void called the Inventory.
Then I gave the command.
Summon.
It was madness. The sort of thing that could exist only in my imagination.
But the System answered that absurd, desperate call.
The way it always did.
Ding.
One small, clear chime.
Ding. Ding. Ding-ding.
Chimes layered over one another. Their faint ripples grew into a wave that swallowed the space around me.
Ding-ding-ding-ding-ding!
My ears grew muffled. This was the first step toward making imagination real.
I opened my eyes to a chime vaster and more majestic than any I’d ever heard.
And saw it.
Shaaah.
Something had forced its way through a gap in unseen space above my head, casting a shadow below.
I heard it, too.
Shrring.
The cold sound of hundreds of pieces of steel sliding against one another.
And finally—
I can do this.
I felt it. I understood.
What I was capable of, the limits I had been given, stretched far beyond anything I’d imagined.
I had the power to make at least part of that ridiculous idea real.
Fwoosh.
In the slowed world, immense qi surged from deep within me.
The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian flowed through every limb and bone. Blood rushed with the pounding of my heart.
Thump. Thump. Thump.
A fierce tremor. A racing pulse.
No. That’s not it.
The beat wasn’t coming from my heart alone.
The Jade Hall Acupoint.
What the people called martial artists had newly named the Middle Dantian.
Every nerve, every sense I possessed was fixed there.
Past the lower dantian, where lava surged in waves, to that lofty peak rising toward the heavens.
To a realm of Will that strength and speed could not measure.
Kiiiiing.
My vision blurred. Agony stabbed through my head as though someone were driving a needle into it.
But I spread my arms as if entranced.
A flash filled my sight, and I felt a thrill greater than the pain. My hands were empty, yet somewhere beyond the reach of touch, I felt and grasped each thing, one by one.
One, two, three.
Ten, twenty, thirty.
And at last...
One hundred.
I opened my eyes.
In that time that had felt like eternity, yet lasted no more than an instant.
Beneath a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords—a hundred blades aimed at countless enemies as if held by an invisible hand.
I parted my tightly closed lips.
“Move.”
SHWAAAAASH!
The sky filled with flashes of light.

Gravity acted on an area, not a single person.
While I was airborne, I’d been the first to feel the spell’s effects.
Once I landed, that was no longer true.
The white-robed figures were clearly mages.
If they wanted to bind me even a little, their gravity magic would have to target the Dark Heaven followers who were their allies, too.
So they meant to delay me from joining Jeok Cheongang, even if only this way...
Fine by me.
The followers staggered like soulless wooden puppets.
I turned in place and swept White Flame across them.
KWA-AAAH!
The spear’s passage through the air sounded more than fierce—outright destructive.
Anyone could swing a spear sideways.
But none of the enemies surrounding me could stop the wave of Force that burst from White Flame’s translucent spearhead.
Not one.
SHHK!
KRRRACK!
Everything was cut apart and crushed.
Weapons.
People.
In the blink of an eye, the ground within a three-jang radius had become a field of death.
Yet the fear had been stripped from them.
They stared at me with dark, unseeing eyes and kept charging.
They murmured the eight-character creed as if entranced.
“Heaven above, earth below.”
“All demons bow.”
“Heaven above...”
CRUNCH!
A headless body toppled.
My spear flashed sideways through three more enemies closing in from the flank.
SHK!
Weapons imbued with Sword Energy and bodies hardened by the external arts alike were helpless against overwhelming force.
I drove through the scattering fragments of steel and flesh without hesitation.
I streaked like lightning between the enemies blocking my way like a wall, thinking and commanding without pause.
Open Inventory.
Summon.
Summon.
Summon.
SHHK, THUNK, KRRRACK!
I cut, stabbed, and crushed my way forward.
Weapons stayed in my hands only briefly.
Each took one life, or two or three, before it left me.
Countless more blades still lay hidden in that vast subspace whose limits I couldn’t begin to guess.
For a moment, the thought crossed my mind that perhaps I could make some ridiculous idea real.
No.
There’s no way.
But why?
CLANG!
I knocked aside the weapons coming at me from every direction.
THWACK!
I crushed the head of an enemy approaching from my blind spot with a single punch.
SHWEEESH—SHHK!
And the more enemies I cut down, the stronger that inexplicable certainty grew.
Could this really be nothing more than a fantasy?
SHWAAASH!
I turned and swung my spear, leaving a mist of blood along its path.
As enemies surged in from every direction to fill the gap left by the dead, I took a short breath.
I won’t know until I try.
Thinking back, it had always been like this.
Every time I needed to break through a wall, I had to go beyond it.
I had to make the impossible possible, turn imagination into reality.
Just as I would now.
Open Inventory.
One breath.
That was all the time I needed.
With countless enemies still blocking my path, filling every space no matter how many I killed, I quietly closed my eyes.
I pictured the mountain of sharp, gleaming steel somewhere in the void called the Inventory.
Then I gave the command.
Summon.
It was madness.
The sort of thing that could exist only in my imagination.
But the System answered that absurd, desperate call.
The way it always did.
Ding.
One small, clear chime.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding-ding.
Chimes layered over one another.
Their faint ripples grew into a wave that swallowed the space around me.
Ding-ding-ding-ding-ding!
My ears grew muffled.
This was the first step toward making imagination real.
I opened my eyes to a chime vaster and more majestic than any I’d ever heard.
And saw it.
Shaaah.
Something had forced its way through a gap in unseen space above my head, casting a shadow below.
I heard it, too.
Shrring.
The cold sound of hundreds of pieces of steel sliding against one another.
And finally—
I can do this.
I felt it.
I understood.
What I was capable of, the limits I had been given, stretched far beyond anything I’d imagined.
I had the power to make at least part of that ridiculous idea real.
Fwoosh.
In the slowed world, immense qi surged from deep within me.
The fire dragon coiled in my lower dantian flowed through every limb and bone.
Blood rushed with the pounding of my heart.
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
A fierce tremor.
A racing pulse.
No.
That’s not it.
The beat wasn’t coming from my heart alone.
The Jade Hall Acupoint.
What the people called martial artists had newly named the Middle Dantian.
Every nerve, every sense I possessed was fixed there.
Past the lower dantian, where lava surged in waves, to that lofty peak rising toward the heavens.
To a realm of Will that strength and speed could not measure.
Kiiiiing.
My vision blurred.
Agony stabbed through my head as though someone were driving a needle into it.
But I spread my arms as if entranced.
A flash filled my sight, and I felt a thrill greater than the pain.
My hands were empty, yet somewhere beyond the reach of touch, I felt and grasped each thing, one by one.
One, two, three.
Ten, twenty, thirty.
And at last...
One hundred.
I opened my eyes.
In that time that had felt like eternity, yet lasted no more than an instant.
Beneath a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords—a hundred blades aimed at countless enemies as if held by an invisible hand.
I parted my tightly closed lips.
“Move.”
SHWAAAAASH!
The sky filled with flashes of light.

paragraphs: Sama Pyo suddenly wondered where he was, who he was, and what he was supposed to do against the enemies still pouring in.
Thwack!

Even as the thought crossed his mind, his saber moved on instinct and cut through an enemy’s neck. But Sama Pyo already knew: even if he cut down dozens, hundreds, tens of thousands more would remain.
His strength was far too meager to turn the tide of this disadvantageous battle.
Clang! Krrr-crack!
“Argh!”
Horrifying screams rang out from every direction.
No—more precisely, only their allies were screaming.
At the center of the front line, which was crumbling beneath an endless spray of blood, Sama Pyo could see what was coming.
At this rate... it’s all over.
His body was exhausted, but his mind was colder than ever. His judgment was clear.
When two forces of roughly equal size clashed, the quality of their troops and their momentum decided the outcome. And Dark Heaven’s army had them beaten on both counts.
Half an hour at most. No—fifteen minutes. The front line will collapse by then.
He kept to himself the thought that would have plunged any of his allies into despair and charged at another enemy.

Jin Taekyung had plunged so deep into the enemy ranks that Sama Pyo could no longer see him. Sama Pyo could barely hold the line, let alone follow. Anger at his own helplessness drove his next strike.
Slice!
One clean strike cleaved the enemy’s upper body in two.
Beneath the shower of blood, a young martial artist who had been trembling in the certainty of his own death lit up with relief.
“Th-thank you... Huh?”
His eyes widened. He sounded dazed.
He looked barely twenty. Just as he recognized Sama Pyo, Sama Pyo recognized the Black Dragon Demon Gate uniform he wore. Something about him seemed familiar, too.
Where have I seen him before?
But the question only flickered through his mind. A moment later, Sama Pyo hurriedly twisted around and swung his saber.
Whish—Kkakak!
Sword Energy tore through the air and met his blade with a violent screech.
Beyond their locked weapons, his opponent’s eyes were vacant as a corpse’s. The Sword Energy, though, shone fiercely—brighter and sharper than Sama Pyo’s own.
A master...!
One brief clash was enough to feel the gap between them down to his bones.
But there was one thing Sama Pyo had failed to notice.
Crack.
His saber had been battered and dulled in clashes with dozens of enemies. It was too weak to withstand the fierce Sword Energy of a man who stood at the threshold of the Peak realm.
KWA-CLANG!
The clash ended almost as soon as it began.
Half of Sama Pyo’s blade spun high into the air. A streak of light shot straight toward him.
Danger!
An alarm blared in his mind at the sight of that devastating flash. Instinct spoke before reason could.
Dodge. Survive, whatever it takes. No matter how disgraceful it looks.
But...
Where am I supposed to dodge?
Time seemed to slow, as though his life were flashing before his eyes. Sama Pyo was acutely aware of everything around him.
Clang-clang! Thud!
“Gaaah!”
The ceaseless clash of blades. Blood scattering through the air. Dying screams.
And his allies, still facing the enemy in a line so tightly packed their shoulders brushed.
Sama Pyo could clearly sense the tremor in their breathing. And at the same time, he knew:
There’s nowhere to dodge.
No. That wasn’t true.
He could dart to either side right now, or duck and roll to avoid as much of the enemy’s Sword Energy as possible.
Narye tagon?
Who cared? Dignity was a luxury in the face of death.
Covered in filth instead of blood, or with an ally used as his shield—it made no difference. Surviving by any means necessary was the way of the unorthodox faction.
That was what his father, the Black Night King Sima Gong, had taught him—the man who’d passed his blood down to him.
Yes. That’s what he taught me.
But things had changed.
One year.
In that short time, the son had stepped out from beneath the shadow his father had cast over his entire life. He had met people, lived through much, and changed.
That was why Sama Pyo saw no way out now.
He could dodge. He couldn’t dodge.
If he avoided the Sword Energy creeping toward him through that seemingly frozen moment, one of his allies would surely die.
What a damn mess.
The curse rested soundlessly on the tip of his tongue.
Sama Pyo didn’t notice the faint smile forming on his lips. Nor did he notice how strangely relieved he felt, even with death right before his eyes.
He launched the dagger he’d hidden under his sleeve, thinking that if the person who’d suddenly come to mind were watching, they might even praise him for this.
Not a bad end for an unorthodox bastard, don’t you think, Pavilion Master?
Sama Pyo smiled brightly.
At the same time, he felt the enemy’s Sword Energy grow even fiercer. It swallowed the dagger flying toward it and surged toward his chest.
Then he heard two sharp, unexpected whistles through the air.
Slice! Thud!
Sama Pyo stared with wide eyes.
At the last moment, someone had leaped in front of him. Blood sprayed from the man’s chest as he staggered. Over his shoulder, a blackish-blue saber blade drove through the enemy’s throat.
This is...
Sama Pyo recognized the blade at once. It was the Black Dragon Saber, his treasured weapon, which he had left behind before the meeting with the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
He recognized the owner of the Force imbued in it, too.
“You fool.”
That chilling voice was utterly familiar—and one he could never grow used to.
Thwack!
The twisted blade of the Black Dragon Saber finished severing the enemy’s neck. Black Force rose like a spreading wildfire and swept across the front.
KRRR-CRACK!
A fierce, blood-red gale engulfed dozens of enemies. The allies who witnessed that overwhelming display of martial might cried out one after another.
“S-Sect Leader!”
“The Sect Leader is here!”
The Black Night King, Sima Gong, had finally appeared on the front line. The great tree that supported the unorthodox Murim had come with the finest martial artists of the Black Dragon Demon Gate.
“Attack.”
A single word escaped his tightly pressed lips.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! KABOOM!
Dozens of Peak masters plunged into the enemy ranks.

Cheers broke out across the front. For that moment, none of the allies holding it dared ask why Sima Gong had only appeared now, or why he had stayed in the rear when he’d had plenty of time to join them.
None but one.
“You’re late.”
The son did not look at the father he had met on the battlefield.

Sama Pyo was looking at the body of the young martial artist who had just thrown himself in front of him. The boy he had saved a moment earlier had looked as though the peach fuzz had scarcely left his face.
His father followed his gaze to the body. His reply was cold.
“He died because you were weak.”
“That’s right. If I’d been stronger, he would’ve lived.”
Sama Pyo nodded calmly, then spoke without restraint.
“Then what were you doing, when you’re so strong?”
“What?”
“The monsters called Black Ghosts never came this way. If you’d brought your forces in at the right time, we could have broken through the enemy lines.”
Why hadn’t the Black Ghosts appeared here? Sima Gong commanded thirty thousand troops, a force central to this battle. Why hadn’t the enemy targeted it?
And why had his father stood by while that opportunity passed?
Sima Gong’s gaze darkened as his son voiced the questions everyone else had momentarily forgotten.
What are you trying to say?
At the sudden Sound Transmission in his ear, Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.
Why? Afraid someone might hear?
How dare you...
I’d already suspected you had other plans. But I kept telling myself it couldn’t be true. I wanted to believe in you.
His son—no, Sama Pyo—drew a deep breath.
You’re still my father, after all.
Do you still not understand why I volunteered for a position that was practically a death sentence?

Sama Pyo had known instinctively that his father was harboring other intentions. He had known that if the heir to everything Sima Gong had built over his lifetime had not been in danger, his father would not have appeared here even now.
“But please, don’t worry. However this battle ends, the Black Dragon Demon Gate will survive.”

For the first time, the son chose a path different from his father’s. He turned away without hesitation. Before charging back toward the enemy, he offered one more remark—perhaps the last he would ever make to him.
“It looks like the other one is dead already. A pity.”
The son left those cryptic words behind. The father remained.

When Sima Gong’s gaze, still frozen like a statue, finally settled on the fallen body, he suddenly remembered a middle-aged man and a young man from several days earlier, as they crossed the desert. They’d dared to speak of the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s and Sama Pyo’s hidden history.
And the command he’d given that had decided their fate in an instant.
See to it as you see fit.
The order had been carried out. Both men had been placed in the most dangerous part of the front line, and both had died.
But the Black Night King, Sima Gong, had not known.
No one could have known that a young man whom a cold-hearted father had sent to his death would save his son.
“...What a cruel twist of fate.”
Sima Gong murmured quietly, then looked down at the Black Dragon Saber in his hand.
The treasured blade he had given his son as his first and last gift now reflected an old man with a troubled look in his eyes.
At that moment, it caught a distant flash of light as well.
It was like lightning.
Bolt after bolt falling without pause, tearing and burning everything beneath them with overwhelming force.

Yet everyone staring wide-eyed at the distant scene knew what they were seeing. Their heightened senses, their instincts and common sense as martial artists, told them what those countless flashes lighting up the battlefield really were.
They were blades, like the ones in their own hands.
Fwoosh!
Dozens of brilliant streaks tore through the darkness beneath the heavy clouds.
They moved freely through the air, like living things, sweeping over beings that could no longer be called alive because they felt nothing.
KRRR-CRACK!
No screams followed—only the sickening sound of flesh being torn apart.
Weapons forged through hundreds of rounds of tempering in lands beyond the desert shattered the moment they met that wave of steel. Their wielders fared no better.
Splash. Thud-thud-thud!
Blood surged up like a wave.
Beneath that red rain, bursting from the bodies of dozens and soaking the ground, one man slowly walked forward.
Squish.
Sticky. Blood pooled up to his ankles and sloshed with each step. Its foul stench seeped into his nose.
Jin Taekyung was covered in blood from head to toe, but he kept walking.
The enormous wave of steel moved with him, subject to his Will alone.
Clack. Thud-thud-thunk!
Something clicked into place, followed by a whistle through the air. Jin Taekyung’s fingers moved ever so slightly.
Clang!

Five great sabers floating through the air spread their broad blades across his flank. The steel shield opened like petals in full bloom, catching the arrowheads that came flying at him in quick succession.
It all happened in the blink of an eye.
Kakakakclang!
A dozen arrows bounced away in showers of sparks.
Jin Taekyung did not flinch. He had already made everything within a three-jang radius his own.
And whoever had hidden among his allies to fire the repeating crossbow would not get another chance to ambush him.
Go.
There was no need to turn and find the archer. At Jin Taekyung’s command, the five great sabers that had shielded him shot away like enormous arrows.
Thud-thud-thud!
More than twenty people died in the time it took him to exhale: the one who had fired the crossbow, those who stood in the sabers’ path, and the enemies beside them.
But the five sabers didn’t return, either.
Even Jin Taekyung had limits when it came to hurling steel weighing dozens of geun apiece like bolts of lightning.
Grit.
A terrible headache struck without warning. He clenched his teeth.
Was that too ambitious?
Unlike the Lower Dantian, the Middle Dantian was the domain of Will—of mental strength.
Controlling this many weapons was nothing short of a miracle. Imbuing each one with internal energy and controlling it perfectly was another matter.
A master of a certain level could stop weapons propelled by strength and speed alone.
Just as some of them were doing now.
Thud! Kakakakclang!

The weapons shot forward again at his command, piercing flesh and bone. But over a distance of barely ten jang, the blades that had once numbered close to a hundred had dwindled by half. Some of the enemies who had reached the Peak realm were beginning to knock them aside without much trouble.
Not yet. Not yet.
Since the battle began, he had cut down hundreds of enemies on his own.
No—perhaps more than a thousand.
It was a feat worthy of the name One Against a Thousand.
But...
It’s not enough.
The deeper he pushed into the enemy ranks, the closer he came to Jeok Cheongang’s fight with the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, the stronger the enemies grew.
To bring down every enemy still surging toward him, Jin Taekyung would have to unleash everything he had.
Just one. One strike is enough.
The instant the thought arose in his mind and took shape as Will—
Slip. Clang-clang-clang!
The dozens of weapons surrounding him fell from the air.
All but one spear. It had drunk more blood than any of the other blades, yet its gleam had not faded.
Now.
Fwoosh.
In the wavering space, White Flame blazed with Force and shot forward.
At the end of its fierce passage through a human wave numbering in the hundreds stood one man.
KWA-BOOM!
A roar split the air like the sky breaking open. The immense force behind the spearhead drove a figure backward.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had been rushing at Jeok Cheongang, who was now drenched in blood. He bared his bloodstained teeth at Jin Taekyung, standing on a red path strewn with finely chopped flesh.
“So, you’ve come?”

Jin Taekyung was covered in blood from head to toe, but he kept walking.
The enormous wave of steel moved with him, subject to his Will alone.
Clack.
Thud-thud-thunk!
Something clicked into place, followed by a whistle through the air.
Jin Taekyung’s fingers moved ever so slightly.
Clang!
Five great sabers floating through the air spread their broad blades across his flank.
The steel shield opened like petals in full bloom, catching the arrowheads that came flying at him in quick succession.
It all happened in the blink of an eye.
Kakakakclang!
A dozen arrows bounced away in showers of sparks.
Jin Taekyung did not flinch.
He had already made everything within a three-jang radius his own.
And whoever had hidden among his allies to fire the repeating crossbow would not get another chance to ambush him.
Go.
There was no need to turn and find the archer.
At Jin Taekyung’s command, the five great sabers that had shielded him shot away like enormous arrows.
Thud-thud-thud!
More than twenty people died in the time it took him to exhale: the one who had fired the crossbow, those who stood in the sabers’ path, and the enemies beside them.
But the five sabers didn’t return, either.
Even Jin Taekyung had limits when it came to hurling steel weighing dozens of geun apiece like bolts of lightning.
Grit.
A terrible headache struck without warning.
He clenched his teeth.
Was that too ambitious?
Unlike the Lower Dantian, the Middle Dantian was the domain of Will—of mental strength.
Controlling this many weapons was nothing short of a miracle.
Imbuing each one with internal energy and controlling it perfectly was another matter.
A master of a certain level could stop weapons propelled by strength and speed alone.
Just as some of them were doing now.
Thud!
Kakakakclang!
The weapons shot forward again at his command, piercing flesh and bone.
But over a distance of barely ten jang, the blades that had once numbered close to a hundred had dwindled by half.
Some of the enemies who had reached the Peak realm were beginning to knock them aside without much trouble.
Not yet.
Not yet.
Since the battle began, he had cut down hundreds of enemies on his own.
No—perhaps more than a thousand.
It was a feat worthy of the name One Against a Thousand.
But...
It’s not enough.
The deeper he pushed into the enemy ranks, the closer he came to Jeok Cheongang’s fight with the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, the stronger the enemies grew.
To bring down every enemy still surging toward him, Jin Taekyung would have to unleash everything he had.
Just one.
One strike is enough.
The instant the thought arose in his mind and took shape as Will—
Slip.
Clang-clang-clang!
The dozens of weapons surrounding him fell from the air.
All but one spear.
It had drunk more blood than any of the other blades, yet its gleam had not faded.
Now.
Fwoosh.
In the wavering space, White Flame blazed with Force and shot forward.
At the end of its fierce passage through a human wave numbering in the hundreds stood one man.
KWA-BOOM!
A roar split the air like the sky breaking open.
The immense force behind the spearhead drove a figure backward.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had been rushing at Jeok Cheongang, who was now drenched in blood.
He bared his bloodstained teeth at Jin Taekyung, standing on a red path strewn with finely chopped flesh.
“So, you’ve come?”

chapters.title: Chapter 1038
paragraphs: It was probably the power of the Middle Dantian. I’d pushed it beyond its limits.
Step.
The dead and the living—everything else seemed to vanish as I stepped onto the blood-red path. At that moment, an agonizing headache unlike anything I’d ever felt before struck me.
Hup.
It felt as if a long, sharp needle were digging around inside my skull.
I held back a groan and fought to still my trembling body. If I showed the slightest weakness in front of a beast that had already bared its fangs, it would devour me on the spot.
“So, you’ve come?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
The moment I heard his utterly unruffled voice, my headache doubled.
No. Maybe the real reason was the sight of Jeok Cheongang, now drenched in blood.
Or perhaps...
System Lv. ??? Chuk Banghyeol
Lv. ??? Chuk Banghyeol
Perhaps it was the strength of the Blood-Sword Demon Lord: a true monster whose Level I could no longer measure, even now.
At least twenty Levels above me... This is going to be an even harder fight.
Swallowing a groan, I reached out. White Flame, connected to me by an invisible thread, shot back into my grasp.
Nothing stopped it. I’d been braced for interference, but none came.
“Qi-Controlled Sword. No, should I call it Qi-Controlled Spear? You must’ve been in quite a hurry to push yourself this far.”
He sounded as relaxed as he looked. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord smiled with the ease of a man who knew he was stronger.
“Still, I’ll give you credit. Good try. At least you made it back before your master died.”
He laughed and casually waved a hand. The instant he did, Jeok Cheongang spotted an opening and thrust out his palm like lightning.
“You bastard!”
KWA-AAAH!
Heat surged forward with his shout.
The force of Flame Divine Palm burned everything in its path as it bore down on the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s face. His smile never wavered.
A streak of blood-red Sword Force cut through the space between them.
SHWAK! KWA-BOOM!
The palm force split cleanly in two. Both halves flew off to either side and slammed into the ground.
A roar engulfed a dozen-jang radius. Acrid smoke billowed up, and through it the Blood-Sword Demon Lord appeared like a ghost and brought his sword down.
SHWAAASH!
Space warped under the terrible pressure.
But Jeok Cheongang threw himself aside as though he’d anticipated the strike, powerful enough to cleave a mountain.
SHK!
The ground split like tofu.
Jeok Cheongang narrowly avoided the blow and immediately found his footing. But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s blurred figure was already moving toward his flank.
Danger...!
He was so fast that even I reacted too late. There was no time to shout.
In less than a breath, the two superhumans exchanged attacks like flashes of light. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord moved faster than sound.
WHOOOM—PAM!
Compressed air burst apart.
They were too close for him to swing his sword. Instead, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord struck Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder with his palm, sending him flying backward like a cannonball.
And directly in his path—
SHWEEEE—THUD!
—I was racing toward him with all my strength.
“Old Master!”
The shout burst out before I knew it. With my help, Jeok Cheongang managed to stop himself. His reply came in a rasp.
“I’m fine. Stop making a fuss and lower your voice. You’ll burst my eardrums.”
He sounded as gruff as ever. Most people wouldn’t have heard a difference, but I knew the Fire King Jeok Cheongang better than anyone.
The greater the danger, the more he pretended to be calm. Even if it was only to reassure someone else.
“You’re doing it again. Time for your medicine.”
I sighed, placed a hand on his back, and poured internal energy into him without hesitation.
Tap. Fwoosh.
Fire joined with fire.
The Scorching Yang Qi born of the same source connected in an instant, driving out the impurities pooled deep inside his body.
“Cough.”
Drip-drip.
A mouthful of blood spilled from his lips against his will. It was black, a sign of considerable Internal Injury.
I clicked my tongue. “You’re fine, are you?”
Jeok Cheongang spat out bloody phlegm.
“It’s one mouthful of blood. What’s all the fuss?”
Honestly, I wanted to let it go. But when someone’s life was on the line, it mattered whether they were telling the truth.
THWACK!
The earlier strike had thinned the enemy forces behind us, but plenty remained. As one of them, unable to wait any longer, charged us, I kicked him in the chest and caved it in.
“You do know you’re covered head to toe in blood, right?”
“It isn’t mine. I’ve been running around so much, I got some on me.”
“That guy looks perfectly fine.”
I pointed to the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, strolling toward us through the parting waves of men. Jeok Cheongang smacked his lips.
“He must’ve been less busy.”
“Ah. Less busy. I see.”
“Anyway, I’m fine. Not a scratch on me... Well, that’s not quite true, but this much won’t stop me.”
PAM!
Jeok Cheongang sprang upright, turning three enemies to charcoal as he rose. Then he licked the blood from the corner of his mouth.
“Well?”
“Just tell me the truth. I won’t tell anyone else.”
“You insolent brat. Are you saying this old man is bluffing?”
“Aren’t you?”
“No. What’s a bastard like him to me?”
“Then I’ll go help the others.”
“Hm?”
“You can handle a bastard like him by yourself, right? Everyone else is fighting for their lives.”
Grab!
The instant I started to turn away, Jeok Cheongang snatched my wrist like lightning and replied in a stern voice.
“The wise men of old said even a sheet of paper is easier to lift when two people carry it.”
“I don’t know what trick he’s using, but every so often he gets startlingly stronger and faster. You’d think he was possessed.”
“And that’s not all. Whenever this old man tried to land a blow with all my strength, some unknown force kept stopping me. It was—”
“Old Master.”
I cut him off and added quietly, “You’re talking too much.”
“One sentence. Short and clear.”
Jeok Cheongang was silent for a moment. Then he answered exactly as I’d asked.
“That bastard’s strong as fuck.”
“Perfectly put.”

“And those pure-white things way over there are helping him with some bizarre dark arts. Every time that strange energy of theirs surges, he gets stronger. I tried to take them out before things got even worse, even if I had to overextend myself, but...”
“You failed. You got hit by those dark arts, too.”
“That’s right. What I felt then was like...”
“The sky was crushing you.”
Gravity magic. No doubt about it.
Jeok Cheongang stared at me, momentarily stunned that I’d described it so precisely. I continued calmly.
“More precisely, that’s not ordinary dark arts. It’s an ability called Magic.”
“Wait. If you mean Magic...”
“Yes. The Magic you know about. The kind you’d only see in my homeland.”
Of course Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened. I hadn’t told him every detail, but he knew something of where I came from and what kind of world it was.
Even so, he couldn’t fully understand or accept what was happening. Neither could I.
But that mattered less than defeating the enemy in front of us.
We have to target them first. Not the Blood-Sword Demon Lord—those people in white. The mages.
Even as I sent him the message through Sound Transmission, a chill ran down my spine at how unfamiliar the idea felt.
Mages. Here, of all places. Not in the modern world, but in Murim.

Then I looked past the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who was still closing the distance at a leisurely stroll. On the hill behind him stood the mages, their white robes fluttering. The reality of it sank in.
We have to take them out first, no matter what.
From the moment I’d realized they were mages, I hadn’t considered any other option.

I knew what the word Magic could mean—how many dangers and unknowns came with it. Of the tens of thousands of allies standing or falling on this battlefield, I was the only one who knew what mages could do in a battle this large.
Besides...
One of them is especially skilled. Skilled enough to hold back both me and Old Master with Magic.
Magic worked differently, but qi was still the raw material behind it. To Jeok Cheongang or me, even a fairly advanced mage wouldn’t pose much of a threat.
Unless they were among the rare few said to have reached the very edge of truth.
“...A Grand Mage.”
The title escaped my lips like a groan.
But just as I was about to conclude that one of them had to be a Grand Mage, a question occurred to me.
If they really have a Grand Mage, how has the battle stayed like this?
I didn’t mean we were winning. Everyone, myself included, was giving it their all, and the battle was still going badly for our side.
But if the Grand Mage had stepped in, we wouldn’t even have been able to keep things at this disadvantage.
I knew better than anyone what a Grand Mage could do on a battlefield. It took no thought at all to picture a wide-area attack spell unlike anything anyone in this world had ever seen.
How long could our army last against that incomprehensible power, a natural disaster with a will of its own? More than a third of our forces were an undisciplined rabble.

Yet the Grand Mage hadn’t joined the fight. He had briefly hindered Jeok Cheongang and me with gravity magic and strengthened the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s body with magic, but had done nothing beyond that.
Squish.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord crossed the blood-red path. At last, he stopped.
“What exactly... are you after?”
I was genuinely curious. And uneasy.
Were the mages holding back because they were preparing a spell powerful enough to end the battle in an instant? Or were they plotting something else?
I’d blurted the question out before I could stop myself. Three jang away, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord watched us with a smile, then furrowed his brow.
“After? From the start, I’ve only wanted two things from this battle. Victory. And you.”
“That’s a long way of saying you won’t answer.”
“I don’t know what you’re talking about, but... it doesn’t matter.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord shrugged with an expression that could have been sincere or an act, then raised the sword he’d been holding loosely and continued.
“Let’s finish this. Of course, I’d prefer an ending where one of you dies and the other is taken prisoner.”
Jeok Cheongang and I answered in one voice.
“Go fuck yourself.”
And at that moment—
PAPAT!
We charged at the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
No. Only Jeok Cheongang shot toward him.
Hold him off for half a quarter-hour. Just half a quarter-hour.
With that Sound Transmission sent through the wind, I twisted my body and charged toward the hill.
SHWEEEE!
