chapters.title: Chapter 1039
paragraphs: It happened in the blink of an eye.
Tap—SHWEEEE!
Jin Taekyung had been hurtling straight ahead. With a slight twist of his foot, he slipped sideways, his movement flowing as though he’d been waiting for this exact moment.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord could only stare in surprise.
What the...!
He hadn’t seen this coming. No one would have. With the gap between them already clear and the situation so dangerous, what Disciple would leave his injured Master behind?
But something else startled the Blood-Sword Demon Lord even more.
He’s... going after the mages!
There was no doubt. Jin Taekyung veered around his flank and shot forward again, heading straight for the twenty or so white-robed figures surveying the battlefield from the foot of a high hill.
Why in the world would he—no, how could he...?

Thoughts tangled together in his mind in that fleeting instant. But now that he’d been caught off guard, there was no time to hesitate. He pushed aside every question, twisted with all his might, and thrust out a hand.
SHWAAK!
The strike tore through the air at a terrifying speed. In that instant, as time seemed to slow, the blood-red Force coiling around his blade was about to shoot toward Jin Taekyung’s back.
No—in the very instant it was about to shoot forward—
FWOOSH!
That dreadful heat suddenly rushed in. In the disarray of his composure, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord remembered someone he’d momentarily forgotten.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
That son of a bitch...!
He didn’t even have time to shout. The horrified Blood-Sword Demon Lord barely managed to turn his sword and block the flames that had rushed right up to him.
KWA-BOOM! GRRRR!

The ground buckled as though an earthquake had struck. Acrid black smoke and steam billowed up, blanketing the area. Through them, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord saw a fist streaming blinding white light-flames.
CRUNCH.
He saw the man behind it, too, steadily driving back his sword despite the blood-red Force wrapped around it.
“You dare take your eyes off me?”
Beyond the trembling blade, barely holding back the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at Jeok Cheongang’s faint smile. His gaze sank low.
It was too late. One moment of surprise, one moment of carelessness, and Jin Taekyung had slipped away.
“You’ve still got plenty of energy, Senior. At your age, shouldn’t you be resting in a coffin?”
“Under normal circumstances, perhaps. But one day, someone high above the clouds told me something.”
FWOOSH.
The flames rose even more fiercely, belying the Internal Injury Jeok Cheongang had suffered earlier. He breathed out a scorching sigh.
“He said he’d send me a wild little brat for a Disciple—an extraordinary one—and that I should build coffins for other bastards until the boy learned to act like an adult.”
“But what use would this old man have for coffins? I can burn the whole lot of you to ashes. Wouldn’t you agree?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s sword was still being pushed back. It wasn’t simply because Jeok Cheongang had drawn on every last bit of strength he had.
It was his aura.
The history behind the name Fire King. The weight of the years borne by an old giant who had lived for more than a century.
And...
“Even if you died and came back a hundred times, you’d never understand why I’m here.”
It was the spirit only shown by those who fought with their lives on the line—not to kill someone, but to protect something precious.
“So when you die this time, don’t be reborn as a human again.”
Ghostly blue fire, like the flames of hell, flickered in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
For an instant, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord felt overwhelmed. He clenched his teeth.
“This damned old monster dares to...!”
Gone was the respectful address. His voice had turned harsh.
Jeok Cheongang’s smile broadened. His opponent was losing his composure.
“Much better. I’d rather bite down on a sword and die than keep hearing you call me ‘Senior.’”
“Shut your mouth!”
CRUNCH!

The balance of power, which had been tipping slowly in Jeok Cheongang’s favor, reversed in an instant. The fearsome power bestowed on the Blood-Sword Demon Lord by the mages—or sorcerers, as he called them—poured into his sword. A pressure as vast as Mount Taishan bore down on Jeok Cheongang.
Hup.
Jeok Cheongang caught his breath. A vein stood out on his forehead, and he felt his feet digging deep into the ground. Still, he did not retreat.
No—he couldn’t.
What? Hold him off for just half a quarter-hour?

Beyond the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s shoulder, he could see the back of a certain insolent brat disappearing into the enemy ranks. The boy had thrown aside his Master, a man he revered as the heavens, like a worn-out rag.
A faint smile touched Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
Treating this old man like a feeble geezer. The nerve of him.

He knew perfectly well that the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had the advantage. Jeok Cheongang had already spent a considerable amount of internal energy fighting the Black Ghosts. His opponent, far from tiring, had gained power beyond his own limits, just as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress once had.
But...
I’ll show you why they call me the Fire King.
A hundred and twenty years. Every one of them had been a struggle.
He had fought enemies, every manner of inner demon, and even himself. Once, loneliness had consumed him.
Not anymore.
There was someone who trusted him more than anyone else in the world. He had something worth protecting with his life.
If you want, I’ll hold out for half a year, not half a quarter-hour. I’ll wait for you as long as it takes.
That was why the Fire King Jeok Cheongang would not break.
He could not.
FWOOSH—GRRRR!
His fiercely burning light-flames wavered against the immense blood-red Force. A roar like the heavens splitting apart filled the air as overwhelming power surged toward him.
It could not wipe the smile from his face.
“Come on, then.”
KWA-BOOM!
White and red energy clashed and mingled again and again, their collisions shaking everything around them.
All of it happened far behind a man cutting through the enemy lines like the point of a sharp awl.
From some point on, I could clearly feel the constant roars and the shock waves from the immense power.
Old Master.
His face came to mind.
Half a quarter-hour. Not even enough time to leisurely finish a cup of tea.
But in a fight between superhumans trading lightning-fast blows, it was plenty of time for someone to die.
That was exactly why I had to keep moving instead of turning back to check on Jeok Cheongang.
If I kill the mages, the Magic empowering the Blood-Sword Demon Lord will break.
It was one of the reasons I’d changed direction and left Jeok Cheongang behind. As long as the Magic held, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord wouldn’t go down easily. He might even keep getting stronger.
But cut off the Magic that had made him so powerful, and we could turn the tide.
Of course, as I’d expected, things weren’t going smoothly.
SHWISH-SHWISH-SHWISH!
Weapons whistled past my ears without pause. Flashes of light skimmed dangerously close to my body.
Sabers, swords, spears, and the occasional weapon of a shape I didn’t recognize. They came in all kinds, but had two things in common.
First, every one of them had been swung at me.
Second, bright light flowed over the countless blades.
Peak masters...!
Not just a few of them. There were only about a hundred enemies stationed in the rear, but every last one had reached the level of injuring others with Sword Energy.
At their center stood someone radiating an especially powerful aura.
System Level: 170 So Gunak
A hulking man enclosed from head to toe in jet-black armor.
Naturally, I didn’t know his title. Even if I’d known who he used to be, it hardly mattered. The enemy in front of me had already lost his former self.
Black Ghost.
My heart sank, and not just because another formidable obstacle had appeared.
The last Black Ghost, who hadn’t shown up on the battlefield, was still here. That made me think of one possibility I hadn’t wanted to believe.
WHOOOM!
A heavy rush of air snapped me back to the present. My thoughts were anything but light, but my feet felt like feathers as I shot forward.
SWISH! KWA-BOOM!
The great saber missed me and tore into the ground, sending earth flying. As ice and dirt scattered in every direction, I thrust White Flame’s spearhead forward with all my strength.
SLICE!
Its flashing arc sliced across the back of his neck.
But the feel of the strike traveled up the shaft to my fingertips. It hadn’t gone deep enough to kill him.
He dodged?
I hadn’t let my guard down like a fool. Every second mattered, and I’d put everything into that first strike. The spear’s trajectory and timing had both been exact.
What I hadn’t accounted for was just how many variables Magic could introduce.
System Level: 173 So Gunak
Three levels.
That might sound like a small difference. In the realm of superhumans, it wasn’t.
WHOOOM—KWA-BOOM!
His next strike was faster and stronger than the last.
No—a strike getting faster and stronger even now.
System Level: 175 So Gunak
SHWEEEE!
The heavy rush of air sharpened to a shriek. His massive, blunt saber came crashing down like lightning, carving through the space before him.
KWA-KWA-KWA-BOOM!
The ground sank beneath the tremendous force. As I backed away to escape its shock wave, the sound of more than ten streaks of wind rang past my ears.
SLICE! SPURT!
Blood sprang from cuts across my body. I’d twisted aside the moment I sensed the danger, but it was too late.
No. They’d been too fast.
They’d grown stronger. Stronger than they were a moment ago.
I’d seen it clearly. At the last instant, the blades had gained speed and force, shooting toward me like flashes of light.
I’d felt it, too: the Black Ghost and the hundred or so Peak masters closing in from every side—and, beyond their shoulders, a distinct pulse of energy spilling down from the hilltop.
They’re trying to stop me somehow. Before I can get any closer.
I wasn’t the only one who sensed danger.
The twenty white-robed figures standing in a circle—the mages—must have felt their lives were in danger, too.
But I’m different.
Everyone fears death. Me. Them.
But what makes the difference in the face of that fear is the strength of one’s Will and desperation.
Inventory open.
I spoke the command in my mind and threw myself forward with all my strength.
Toward the more than a hundred Peak masters, who had grown even stronger.
Toward the last Black Ghost, whom I had to get past.
PAPAT!
One step.
Every distance vanished, and time slowed.
At the same time, dozens of streaks of light blazed destructively, coloring the world around me. And a single bolt of lightning, more enormous than all of them combined, came crashing down toward me.
SHWAAAK!
Yeah. I knew it. I was one man against many, and the difference in our strength was plain to see.
But what the eye could see wasn’t everything.
I have to get through. No matter what it takes.
Those trying to get past, and those standing in their way.
Those fighting to protect something, and those who had forgotten what they were meant to protect.
They had no Will. They had forgotten desperation. They couldn’t even remember the word duty.
But I wasn’t like them.
I knew what all of those things meant. That was why I could risk my life to keep going. Why I could throw myself into the oncoming attacks and strike with everything I had, down to my soul.
Just like now.
SHWAK!
White Flame’s spearhead tore through the air.
At the same time, I whispered the command I’d held back.
Summon Fire Dragon Armor.
Ding.
KWA-BOOOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 1040
paragraphs: KWA-BOOOOM!
A deafening explosion shook the earth.
The shock wave burst out without warning, rattling everything around it. It reached beyond a radius of several dozen jang, all the way up the steep hill.
Rumble.
“May I say something?”
The old man’s voice cut through the rumbling. Beneath a silver-white veil, red lips stirred.
“No. You may not.”
There was no trace of the woman who’d been rattled by the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s fury just fifteen minutes ago.
At his superior’s calm, almost icy reply, the old mage flinched.
“...Grand Sorceress.”
His voice was full of concern.
But the woman called the Grand Sorceress, standing at the center of the white-robed figures, paid him no mind as she spoke.
“Put your worries aside. What you’re afraid of won’t happen.”
“B-but...”
“But what?”
Ordinarily, the old mage would have fallen silent by now.
Dark Heaven’s hierarchy was mercilessly strict, and the woman before him could crush him like an ant with a flick of her hand.
But he had seen it clearly.
At the last moment, countless flashes of light had swallowed one man.
A young man who’d thrown himself toward certain death, so far beyond recklessness that it was as if he’d already given up on living.
The old mage knew his role. Swallowing hard, he forced himself to continue.
“But if this goes on, he may be in danger. As you know, if ‘he’ dies here, how are we to bear that person’s wrath?”
He was right.
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
If a man who had drawn such keen interest from the absolute one met such a futile end, they too would die for failing their mission.
No—they would die. Without a doubt.
The old mage believed there would be no exception, not even for the woman before him: his superior, and one of the absolute one’s closest confidantes.
Of course, that was only what he thought.
Danger? Die?
The woman repeated his words, then gave a quiet laugh.
Beyond the finely woven veil, her black eyes remained fixed on the hill below.
Who, exactly?
“Pardon? Why, of course...”
The old mage was about to answer when—
FWOOSH.
The hazy cloud of dust at the foot of the hill split apart.
And, as if an invisible, razor-sharp blade had passed through it, the veil parted cleanly to reveal the scene hidden within.
The old mage—and everyone else on the hill—stared wide-eyed.
Amid ground devastated as if a meteor had struck it stood a towering figure.
“Th-that’s...”
One mage pointed before he knew what he was doing. The gesture was pointless. Everyone was already looking.
No one could miss that nine-foot frame, with arms and legs as thick as pillars. Or the familiar black armor enclosing it from head to toe.
“Black Ghost...!”
A trembling groan escaped the old mage.
His brief shock gave way to despair as his gaze fell on the bloodied man lying at the Black Ghost’s feet.
The man who must not die here.
Jin Taekyung.
It’s over. All of it.
The old mage’s vision blurred.
He’d taken a sliver of hope from the Grand Sorceress’s composure a moment ago. That only made the shock worse.
Half the hundred elite fighters they’d kept back as guards had vanished, but that meant nothing beside Jin Taekyung’s death.
All twenty mages thought the same.
At least, until the Grand Sorceress’s quiet voice rang out the very next moment.
“As expected...”
The mages’ eyes widened at the murmur, its meaning beyond them but its note of admiration unmistakable.
Then, all at once, they saw.
Rustle. THUD.
Far below, the Black Ghost crumpled like a rotten log.
Only now, with his enormous body falling away, could they see the silver spearhead lodged between his brows.
They could see it. But they could not hear—
Ding.
The clear chime meant for only one person.
It rang in the ears of the man everyone believed dead, but who still lived: the sound of his return to life.
System You defeated Lv. 175 So Gunak! - Level Up!
Warm light welled up from deep within his cooling body.

It stopped the blood seeping through the gaps in his red armor, shattered by countless strikes of Sword Energy and Force. It mended torn flesh and broken bones, rekindling the flame of life once more.
Huff.
His breath was hot as fire.
As if waking from a long dream, Jin Taekyung slowly opened his eyes. He looked up at the dark sky before him once again and muttered,
“Fuck, it’s good to see you.”
The moment the old mage saw it, he understood.
Danger? Die?
He understood what the Grand Sorceress had meant.
Who, exactly?
The Grand Sorceress had been right.
Jin Taekyung wasn’t the one who now had to risk dying.
They were.
WHIP—GRAB.
The spear lodged deep between the Black Ghost’s brows flew into its owner’s grasp as if drawn by an invisible force.
No sooner had it reached his hand than it shot out in a flash.
SHWAAAAK—SPLAT!
Blue-black flames swept through the surviving enemies in a savage arc like a giant dragon’s tail.
“Grand Sorceress!”
“We have to stop him, whatever it takes! If this goes on, he’ll—he’ll...”
Urgent shouts rose all around her, beginning with the old mage.
But the Grand Sorceress watched the horrifying, wondrous sight in silence, an inscrutable light in her eyes.
At last.
The quiet exclamation hovered on her tongue.
Even when the mages could wait no longer for her command and stepped forward with clenched teeth, she alone stood there, smiling quietly.
From the moment I first opened my eyes in Murim, I’d faced the same reality again and again. Put simply:
High risk, high return.
It had always been that way.
An adventure with no set ending always came with enormous danger. But the greater the risk, the more certain the reward.
Just like now.
Ding. Ding. Ding. BEEP-BEEP.
Chimes and warning beeps rang out in rapid succession, tangling together in my ears.
A message confirming I’d defeated the Black Ghost, the last obstacle. A Level Up. A holographic window telling me I’d recovered as a result.
And that final warning beep...

System Fire Dragon Armor has suffered severe damage from powerful energy! - Fire Dragon Armor has been automatically recalled to Inventory! It cannot be resummoned until the damaged sections are repaired to a certain degree! - Time until Fire Dragon Armor is automatically repaired: 3 days
It told me the divine weapon that had made this gamble possible had taken the hit. Despite the crazy stunt I’d pulled, it had kept death at bay, if only for a little while.
I actually survived.
Maybe it was because I’d come so close to death, but it still didn’t feel real.
I’d made the gamble hoping I would survive, of course.
I just hadn’t been a hundred percent sure.
If that damned Black Ghost had taken even a little longer to die, the best I could’ve hoped for was taking him down with me.
But...
SHK!
I was alive. I’d survived.
And just as I had from the beginning, I was still here, cutting down enemies without stopping.
My body was brimming with life—the reward I’d won for risking my life.
PUK! BOOM!
I drove my spear through three enemies in a single powerful thrust, then swept out a palm strike at those rushing in from my blind spot.
KWA-AAAA!
Flesh and bone melted in the terrible heat.
Of the fifty or so enemies who’d survived my clash with the Black Ghost, fewer remained by the moment.
Faster. Faster.
I gritted my teeth and pushed harder.
I had to end this fight as quickly as I could.
My mental strength had already been pushed to its limit. I was running on empty.
If the Level Up hadn’t restored my body—if I hadn’t been thinking of everyone still behind me—I might have collapsed already.
They won’t fall until I bring them down.
I swung White Flame as if possessed.

I’d pushed the Middle Dantian’s ability to its limit, and my mind had slowed noticeably. My hands and feet, guided by instinct and movements ingrained through endless training, swept through the enemy faster than I could think.
I was relying on instinct more than reason.
Even so, there was one last thread of reason I clung to: the reason I couldn’t fall, and the greatest variable my enemies had.
Magic.
Maybe that was why my instincts, keener than ever as they raced ahead of my thoughts, picked up another change. I’d been wary of Magic all along.
WHOOOOOM.
Space trembled. The air trembled.
At the same time, desperate voices rang out in the distance.
“The power of the Wind Ghost!”
“The might to uproot mountains!”
FWOOSH!
Energy boiled up from the hilltop and hurtled toward me.
An invocation, followed by its manifestation.
But I knew this kind of body-strengthening Magic could only take effect if its target was still alive.
SHWAK!
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in blue-black fire, tore through the air.
The terrifying ring of fire swept through a dozen or so enemies within the spell’s range.
SHK! PUK!
Ten heads flew into the air.
At that very instant, pain shot through my side.
I’d been ready for it. Without slowing down, I turned and drove my elbow back.
CRACK! KWA-BOOM!
The enemy’s face caved in, and he went flying. I pulled the dagger lodged deep in my side free and whipped my arm out in a flash.
SWISH—PUK!
With a dull thud, another enemy’s head snapped back. Only about twenty remained.
“What is this...!”
“No! Stop him!”
Listening to the shouts of the white-robed figures—or rather, the mages—now tinged with fear, I could roughly guess what was happening.
There was a limit to the Magic they could use.
That was what set them apart from the mages I knew in the modern world.
And in the next moment, that realization lent force to my feet.
CRUNCH—BOOM!
The ground buckled, then melted.
Flamefire Path.
I shot forward in a single explosive burst. No one nearby could stop me now.
No matter how strong you made a hunting dog, it couldn’t stand against a wolf. Even a thousand-year-old imugi couldn’t ascend to the heavens without a dragon pearl.
Not even something inhuman could stop me.
“Taishan.”
WHOOOOOM.
“Fall and crush him.”
A voice I remembered rang out, and immense pressure descended on me as I shot forward like a streak of flame.
But unlike last time, I was ready.
I can see it.
I could feel it, too.

sentences.text: KWA-BOOOOM!
A deafening explosion shook the earth.
The shock wave burst out without warning, rattling everything around it.
It reached beyond a radius of several dozen jang, all the way up the steep hill.
Rumble.
“May I say something?”
The old man’s voice cut through the rumbling.
Beneath a silver-white veil, red lips stirred.
“No.
You may not.”
There was no trace of the woman who’d been rattled by the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s fury just fifteen minutes ago.
At his superior’s calm, almost icy reply, the old mage flinched.
“...Grand Sorceress.”
His voice was full of concern.
But the woman called the Grand Sorceress, standing at the center of the white-robed figures, paid him no mind as she spoke.
“Put your worries aside.
What you’re afraid of won’t happen.”
“B-but...”
“But what?”
Ordinarily, the old mage would have fallen silent by now.
Dark Heaven’s hierarchy was mercilessly strict, and the woman before him could crush him like an ant with a flick of her hand.
But he had seen it clearly.
At the last moment, countless flashes of light had swallowed one man.
A young man who’d thrown himself toward certain death, so far beyond recklessness that it was as if he’d already given up on living.
The old mage knew his role.
Swallowing hard, he forced himself to continue.
“But if this goes on, he may be in danger.
As you know, if ‘he’ dies here, how are we to bear that person’s wrath?”
He was right.
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
If a man who had drawn such keen interest from the absolute one met such a futile end, they too would die for failing their mission.
No—they would die.
Without a doubt.
The old mage believed there would be no exception, not even for the woman before him: his superior, and one of the absolute one’s closest confidantes.
Of course, that was only what he thought.
Danger?
Die?
The woman repeated his words, then gave a quiet laugh.
Beyond the finely woven veil, her black eyes remained fixed on the hill below.
Who, exactly?
“Pardon?
Why, of course...”
The old mage was about to answer when—
FWOOSH.
The hazy cloud of dust at the foot of the hill split apart.
And, as if an invisible, razor-sharp blade had passed through it, the veil parted cleanly to reveal the scene hidden within.
The old mage—and everyone else on the hill—stared wide-eyed.
Amid ground devastated as if a meteor had struck it stood a towering figure.
“Th-that’s...”
One mage pointed before he knew what he was doing.
The gesture was pointless.
Everyone was already looking.
No one could miss that nine-foot frame, with arms and legs as thick as pillars.
Or the familiar black armor enclosing it from head to toe.
“Black Ghost...!”
A trembling groan escaped the old mage.
His brief shock gave way to despair as his gaze fell on the bloodied man lying at the Black Ghost’s feet.
The man who must not die here.
Jin Taekyung.
It’s over.
All of it.
The old mage’s vision blurred.
He’d taken a sliver of hope from the Grand Sorceress’s composure a moment ago.
That only made the shock worse.
Half the hundred elite fighters they’d kept back as guards had vanished, but that meant nothing beside Jin Taekyung’s death.
All twenty mages thought the same.
At least, until the Grand Sorceress’s quiet voice rang out the very next moment.
“As expected...”
The mages’ eyes widened at the murmur, its meaning beyond them but its note of admiration unmistakable.
Then, all at once, they saw.
Rustle.
THUD.
Far below, the Black Ghost crumpled like a rotten log.
Only now, with his enormous body falling away, could they see the silver spearhead lodged between his brows.
They could see it.
But they could not hear—
Ding.
The clear chime meant for only one person.
It rang in the ears of the man everyone believed dead, but who still lived: the sound of his return to life.
System You defeated Lv.
175 So Gunak! - Level Up!
Warm light welled up from deep within his cooling body.
It stopped the blood seeping through the gaps in his red armor, shattered by countless strikes of Sword Energy and Force.
It mended torn flesh and broken bones, rekindling the flame of life once more.
Huff.
His breath was hot as fire.
As if waking from a long dream, Jin Taekyung slowly opened his eyes.
He looked up at the dark sky before him once again and muttered,
“Fuck, it’s good to see you.”
The moment the old mage saw it, he understood.
Danger?
Die?
He understood what the Grand Sorceress had meant.
Who, exactly?
The Grand Sorceress had been right.
Jin Taekyung wasn’t the one who now had to risk dying.
They were.
WHIP—GRAB.
The spear lodged deep between the Black Ghost’s brows flew into its owner’s grasp as if drawn by an invisible force.
No sooner had it reached his hand than it shot out in a flash.
SHWAAAAK—SPLAT!
Blue-black flames swept through the surviving enemies in a savage arc like a giant dragon’s tail.
“Grand Sorceress!”
“We have to stop him, whatever it takes!
If this goes on, he’ll—he’ll...”
Urgent shouts rose all around her, beginning with the old mage.
But the Grand Sorceress watched the horrifying, wondrous sight in silence, an inscrutable light in her eyes.
At last.
The quiet exclamation hovered on her tongue.
Even when the mages could wait no longer for her command and stepped forward with clenched teeth, she alone stood there, smiling quietly.
From the moment I first opened my eyes in Murim, I’d faced the same reality again and again.
Put simply:
High risk, high return.
It had always been that way.
An adventure with no set ending always came with enormous danger.
But the greater the risk, the more certain the reward.
Just like now.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
BEEP-BEEP.
Chimes and warning beeps rang out in rapid succession, tangling together in my ears.
A message confirming I’d defeated the Black Ghost, the last obstacle.
A Level Up.
A holographic window telling me I’d recovered as a result.
And that final warning beep...
System Fire Dragon Armor has suffered severe damage from powerful energy! - Fire Dragon Armor has been automatically recalled to Inventory!
It cannot be resummoned until the damaged sections are repaired to a certain degree! - Time until Fire Dragon Armor is automatically repaired: 3 days
It told me the divine weapon that had made this gamble possible had taken the hit.
Despite the crazy stunt I’d pulled, it had kept death at bay, if only for a little while.
I actually survived.
Maybe it was because I’d come so close to death, but it still didn’t feel real.
I’d made the gamble hoping I would survive, of course.
I just hadn’t been a hundred percent sure.
If that damned Black Ghost had taken even a little longer to die, the best I could’ve hoped for was taking him down with me.
But...
SHK!
I was alive.
I’d survived.
And just as I had from the beginning, I was still here, cutting down enemies without stopping.
My body was brimming with life—the reward I’d won for risking my life.
PUK!
BOOM!
I drove my spear through three enemies in a single powerful thrust, then swept out a palm strike at those rushing in from my blind spot.
KWA-AAAA!
Flesh and bone melted in the terrible heat.
Of the fifty or so enemies who’d survived my clash with the Black Ghost, fewer remained by the moment.
Faster.
Faster.
I gritted my teeth and pushed harder.
I had to end this fight as quickly as I could.
My mental strength had already been pushed to its limit.
I was running on empty.
If the Level Up hadn’t restored my body—if I hadn’t been thinking of everyone still behind me—I might have collapsed already.
They won’t fall until I bring them down.
I swung White Flame as if possessed.
I’d pushed the Middle Dantian’s ability to its limit, and my mind had slowed noticeably.
My hands and feet, guided by instinct and movements ingrained through endless training, swept through the enemy faster than I could think.
I was relying on instinct more than reason.
Even so, there was one last thread of reason I clung to: the reason I couldn’t fall, and the greatest variable my enemies had.
Magic.
Maybe that was why my instincts, keener than ever as they raced ahead of my thoughts, picked up another change.
I’d been wary of Magic all along.
WHOOOOOM.
Space trembled.
The air trembled.
At the same time, desperate voices rang out in the distance.
“The power of the Wind Ghost!”
“The might to uproot mountains!”
FWOOSH!
Energy boiled up from the hilltop and hurtled toward me.
An invocation, followed by its manifestation.
But I knew this kind of body-strengthening Magic could only take effect if its target was still alive.
SHWAK!
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in blue-black fire, tore through the air.
The terrifying ring of fire swept through a dozen or so enemies within the spell’s range.
SHK!
PUK!
Ten heads flew into the air.
At that very instant, pain shot through my side.
I’d been ready for it.
Without slowing down, I turned and drove my elbow back.
CRACK!
KWA-BOOM!
The enemy’s face caved in, and he went flying.
I pulled the dagger lodged deep in my side free and whipped my arm out in a flash.
SWISH—PUK!
With a dull thud, another enemy’s head snapped back.
Only about twenty remained.
“What is this...!”
“No!
Stop him!”
Listening to the shouts of the white-robed figures—or rather, the mages—now tinged with fear, I could roughly guess what was happening.
There was a limit to the Magic they could use.
That was what set them apart from the mages I knew in the modern world.
And in the next moment, that realization lent force to my feet.
CRUNCH—BOOM!
The ground buckled, then melted.
Flamefire Path.
I shot forward in a single explosive burst.
No one nearby could stop me now.
No matter how strong you made a hunting dog, it couldn’t stand against a wolf.
Even a thousand-year-old imugi couldn’t ascend to the heavens without a dragon pearl.
Not even something inhuman could stop me.
“Taishan.”
WHOOOOOM.
“Fall and crush him.”
A voice I remembered rang out, and immense pressure descended on me as I shot forward like a streak of flame.
But unlike last time, I was ready.
I can see it.
I could feel it, too.
The flow of qi.
A single line hidden beneath that immense power.
And...
Now.
SHK!
My spearhead crossed the space without a sound.
It cut through Taishan.

chapters.title: Chapter 1041
paragraphs: Magic was an unpredictable and powerful force.
It could strengthen allies, weaken enemies, and change the course of a battle in countless ways, from wide-area attacks to defensive barriers.
That was why mages were so highly valued even in the modern world, where the insane profession known as Hunter had taken root.
But if someone asked me whether mages were the most powerful among Hunters of the same rank, I’d answer without hesitation.
No.
Under the right circumstances, they could wield more power than anyone else on the battlefield. But they needed a few things in place first.
The first was allies who could protect them while keeping approaching enemies at bay.
SHING!
I cut through it.
There was no sensation of slicing through flesh and bone, no hot blood spurting like a fountain. And yet I felt it clearly.
I’d cut straight through something intangible and odorless that people called qi. The System knew it, too.
Ding.
System You successfully dispelled Gravity Magic! Qi Sense has improved slightly! - You can now control qi a little more freely!
A translucent holographic window appeared as the System notification rang in my ears.
I paid it no mind.
I drew up every bit of qi sleeping deep within my body and kept moving forward.
SHWEEEE!
The several dozen jang between us vanished fast. As I closed in, the immense energy covering the hill surged more violently.
“F-Fire Ghost, answer our call!”
“Strange rocks and crags, block our master’s enemies!”
The incantations came out in a rush.
Dozens of massive fireballs filled the air. Ahead of me, the ground turned over and a wall of stone rose high.
FWOOSH! GRRRR!
If anyone else had seen it—or even a seasoned master of the martial world—they would have stared in awe, calling it the work of supernatural powers.
But in all the vast world, I was the one exception.
Fire Ball. And Stone Wall, too?
The moment I recognized the newly manifested Magic, my face stiffened.
Was it because these spells were too much for even me to dispel easily?
Wrong.
Judging by their size, range, and power, even B-rank or upper C-rank mages could cast them.
The problem was that I’d just realized my earlier theory was wrong.
They weren’t limited in the kinds of Magic they could use. They just hadn’t used them.
Magic was valued not only for its power, but for its variety and all the ways it could change a battle.
Yet despite having both the ability and the opportunity, all they’d shown so far was body-enhancement Magic and Gravity Magic.
Why the hell?
The question filled my mind.
But the Magic reached me before I could find an answer.
KWA-AAAA!
The dozens of fireballs had been tiny when they were first launched from afar. Now, as huge as boulders weighing a thousand geun, they sailed over the stone wall and fell toward me.
The heat alone would have taken anyone else’s breath away.
But the heat in White Flame’s spearhead as I brought it down on them was deeper and fiercer beyond comparison.
SHING—KWA-BOOOOM!
I dodged half and cut through the rest.
The fireballs exploded in midair, scattering brilliant flame in every direction. I burst through the acrid smoke and drove my fist toward the enormous stone wall blocking my way.
WHOOOM!
My fist cut through the wind—no, burned through it.
The art had none of the ever-changing forms or profound principles boasted by the other great sects. But for sheer explosive force and destructive power, it had no equal.
Long ago, the third Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan had been obsessed with fist-and-foot martial arts, unlike his spear-loving master. He’d named the martial art he created:
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
CRUNCH—KRRR!
True to its name, the wall of strange rocks and crags gave way, breaking into hundreds, then thousands of pieces.
No—it melted and burst apart at the same time.
GRRRR!
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck.
I passed beneath the boulders raining down overhead and shot toward the hill again.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System You successfully dispelled Fire Ball! - You successfully dispelled Stone Wall! Qi Sense has improved slightly! - You can now control qi a little more freely!
“He’s—he’s coming!”
“Arrows of Radiance, answer our call!”
As their shouts rose almost to screams, I stared straight at the hilltop.
Twenty people in white robes.
Some were vomiting blood from the backlash of having their Magic dispelled. Others were casting another spell. Still others trembled, their faces as white as their robes.
One person stood out because none of that applied to him.
So it’s you.
The Grand Mage.
A great mage who had reached the very edge of truth—and an enemy I absolutely had to defeat. He was a man.
His voluminous robes couldn’t entirely hide his slender figure. Red lips showed beneath his silver-white veil.
He was another formidable foe, one whose presence had been overshadowed by the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
He might also be the only person who could answer my question.
SHWISH-SHWISH-SHWISH!
Magic Arrow.
I swung my spearhead up toward the countless streaks of brilliant light shooting at me.
FWOOSH!
Blue-black Force surged like wildfire and swallowed the light.
No—as soon as I thought it had, everything there burned to ash, and new spells came rushing in.
POW-POW-POW! SHWEEEE!
The air and the ground below it were blanketed in lights of every color.
A spear of ice. A rain of fire. Blades of lightning and wind.
All of it came crashing down on one person.
Me.
The countless streaks of light merged and followed one another, each as powerful as a Peak Master’s Sword Energy.
But that was all they were. They could never wound me.
SHING.
I cut through the ice spear with my own.
SHWISH-SHWISH! KWA-BOOOOM!
Moving as swiftly as Shifting Form and Position, I dodged the rain of fire falling all around me.
BA-BOOM!
The heat of Flame Divine Palm swallowed the lightning and blades of wind waiting for me.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
Clear chimes rang in succession, announcing that I’d dispelled the Magic.
The pinnacle of mastery.
The high, densely wooded peak I’d built by surviving the brink of death again and again—none of their spells had come close to threatening it.
Here on the hill overlooking the blood-soaked battlefield, nothing could stop me now.
Not people. Not Magic.
“Plants sleeping beneath this earth, rise up and bind our master’s enemies!”
RUSTLE!
I felt it before the incantation was even complete. I knew what it was.
The pulse of energy beneath my feet. The nature of this Magic.
But there was no reason to dodge, and no need to cut it apart.
Thick roots burst from deep underground and coiled around my whole body, binding me tight. I simply stepped forward in silence. That was enough.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
The stems, hardened like steel by Magic, trembled.
They were wrapped tight around my limbs, my waist, even my neck. I felt their pressure, reached out, and tore them apart.
KRRRUNCH!
Ordinarily, I shouldn’t have been able to reach out at all. I certainly shouldn’t have been able to take a step.
But...
That’s what you think.
That was only what they thought, staring at me in disbelief.
To me, this was perfectly natural.
A Reward earned through one life-threatening adventure after another.
Pure physical strength that a simple binding spell couldn’t restrain.
That strength, far beyond human limits—and the several jiazi of internal energy still surging endlessly from my lower dantian—made it possible.
CRACK! BOOM!
The stems binding my body burst apart in an instant.
They kept coming, persistent as living creatures. I trampled them again and again, then ripped them out by the roots.
So they could never rise again. And so whoever had cast the spell would collapse, spitting blood.
Ding.
Another chime announced that I’d dispelled the binding spell.
“Ugh—bleeegh!”
Another white-robed figure fell to his knees, vomiting dark red blood.
He looked like the oldest of the twenty mages. He was also the nineteenth to fall.
What that meant was clear.
One person remained.
While the mages under his command kept collapsing from the backlash of their energy, the Grand Mage stood alone on the hill without the slightest sign of being shaken.
No—more precisely, it was just him and me, now almost face-to-face.
“I’d only heard about you until now... I’m glad to see you in person.”
His red lips moved beneath the closely woven silver-white veil.
His voice was calm, with what sounded almost like a hint of excitement.
“Crazy bastard.”
At my heartfelt insult, a breeze accompanied by a low laugh stirred his veil.
“What an ill-mannered man. Cursing someone whose face and name you don’t even know.”
He was right.
I didn’t know this man’s name or face.
I already knew that even the supernatural ability granted to me by the System couldn’t reveal any information about him.
Otherwise, he wouldn’t dare speak to me like that with less than a jang between us.
WHOOOOOM.
I couldn’t see it, but I could feel it.
The immense, deep energy blocking the space between us.
Though we occupied the same space, it separated us as if we existed in different worlds. It was an extraordinarily solid defensive barrier.
“So you’ve been sitting up on that hill, scheming away, and this is all you’ve got?”
“Ah, I knew you’d be able to feel it.”
The Grand Mage nodded happily, then added,
“And I knew you wouldn’t try anything lightly in a situation like this.”
“Oh, did I hit a nerve?”
I silently clenched my teeth.
He was right.
I had one attempt.
If I failed to break the barrier and take his life with that one strike, the Grand Mage would escape the narrow distance I’d managed to close.
That was why I couldn’t act rashly, even with every second counting.
But the quiet voice that slipped into my ears next was enough to shake me far more than anything he’d said before.
“Still, I’m a little disappointed. This isn’t all I prepared.”
“...What?”
“Shall I show you? I was getting a little bored anyway.”
At that very moment—
GROOOOOM.
In stark contrast to his bright, laughter-filled voice, an utterly dreadful amount of energy surged up around his slender body.

I couldn’t see it, but I could feel it.
The immense, deep energy blocking the space between us.
Though we occupied the same space, it separated us as if we existed in different worlds.
It was an extraordinarily solid defensive barrier.
“So you’ve been sitting up on that hill, scheming away, and this is all you’ve got?”
“Ah, I knew you’d be able to feel it.”
The Grand Mage nodded happily, then added,
“And I knew you wouldn’t try anything lightly in a situation like this.”
“Oh, did I hit a nerve?”
I silently clenched my teeth.
He was right.
I had one attempt.
If I failed to break the barrier and take his life with that one strike, the Grand Mage would escape the narrow distance I’d managed to close.
That was why I couldn’t act rashly, even with every second counting.
But the quiet voice that slipped into my ears next was enough to shake me far more than anything he’d said before.
“Still, I’m a little disappointed.
This isn’t all I prepared.”
“...What?”
“Shall I show you?
I was getting a little bored anyway.”
At that very moment—
GROOOOOM.
In stark contrast to his bright, laughter-filled voice, an utterly dreadful amount of energy surged up around his slender body.

chapters.title: Chapter 1042
paragraphs: Gooooom.
The instant Jin Taekyung felt the enormous energy surging around the Grand Mage, two words shot through his mind like bullets, wiping it blank.
The first was wide-area Magic.
And the second...
One Annihilation.
He knew it by instinct.
To stop the insane thing the man before him was about to do, he would have to make an insane choice of his own.
Only a desperate strike he’d thought he could never use again—a strike he had even less chance of surviving this time—could stop the wide-area Magic from activating.
He realized he’d already made his decision and laughed bitterly to himself.
Damn it.
He didn’t want to die yet.
He wanted to live somehow, even if he had to struggle pathetically for it.
But there was no way.
No—there was only one way.
To break through the powerful barrier surrounding the Grand Mage and take his life with a single strike, he would have to burn up his own life.
Was he certain it would work?
No.
There was only a chance.
Would he survive, or die?
Death was far more likely.
But even so, that was enough.
It was the only way to protect the tens of thousands of allies still fighting on the battlefield—and the people precious to him among them.
All right.
That was enough.
A noble sacrifice or a pointless death.
He didn’t know which it would be. But in this moment, these chaotic times demanded that Jin Taekyung become a hero, and he was ready.
Perhaps he had been for a very long time.
Fwoosh.
The wind stopped. The air trembled.
Time seemed to stand still. Hundreds of acupoints awakened, and he felt every muscle in his body, down to the last strand.
And then...
Qi flowed into the white spearhead.
Dark as the deep sea, flashing like lightning, burning like flame.
At last, those forces merged and swelled larger than ever before. Powerful enough to devour its wielder’s life, the energy surged along the spearhead he held drawn back like a bowstring.
In that moment, it blazed with such dazzling light that it seemed to color the Grand Mage’s eyes, hidden behind his finely woven veil.
This is...
The barrier couldn’t fully conceal that destructive radiance. Fear seized the Grand Mage, along with awe for the young man before him and the unbelievable choice he had made.
At this rate, I’ll die. Without a doubt.
He was certain. Once that terrifying strike was complete and launched, he and his barrier would vanish without a trace.
Jin Taekyung’s life would scatter like ash as well.
But neither the Grand Mage nor the master he served wanted that.
We’re both lucky, you and I.
A money pouch forced to bear more weight than it could hold would tear. Tie it shut before the full weight settled, though, and it would remain intact.
The difference was that narrow.
The Grand Mage’s Magic was already a step ahead. Jin Taekyung’s strike was a step behind.
That sliver of time—no more than an instant—changed both their fates.
Pour forth, flames of hell.
Fwoosh!
An immense energy exploded around the Grand Mage.
It began spreading far faster than Jin Taekyung had expected. He had only one choice left.
Shwoosh!
The spearhead tore through space.
At the same time, a One Annihilation larger than ever before, and therefore not even half-formed, finally met the barrier between them.
Gooooom.
A deafening roar made his ears ring, and white light washed over the hill.
Amid the faint pain coming from all over his body, the old Daoist steadied his ragged breathing.
Hoo.
His sweetish-smelling breath slowly dispersed.
Blood running from the wound on his forehead had stained his vision red. Through it, he saw two men standing tall as iron towers.
No—the instant he thought he saw them, they vanished.
Whish.
A whistle so faint it made his skin crawl reached his ears.
An alarm sounded in his mind. His thoughts raced ahead, ordering his body to dodge.
Move. Get out of their way, now.
But already badly wounded, his body could no longer move as it normally would.
Shhk!
Excruciating pain shot through him.
Two blades he hadn’t quite avoided slashed his side and shoulder, and the tremendous energy within the steel tore deep into his body.
Hng...!
His vision blurred.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord steadied himself and swept his treasured sword out. Brilliant Sword Force flared along the blade, now only half its former length.
Bang! Bang! Baaang!
Three clashes, swift as lightning. Then a figure shot through the cloud of dust like a cannonball.
“Sect Leader!”
The Zhongnan Sect Disciples fighting amid the Dark Heaven cultists cried out.
At that moment, two figures appeared from nowhere and caught the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord as he flew backward.
Grind.
Only after sliding back about ten feet did they finally stop.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord coughed up dark blood. He moved his lips, looking toward the two men whose faces he could barely make out.
“Senior Brothers...”
“Damn it, don’t say a word.”
His eldest Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman, snapped at him. Then his second Senior Brother, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, spoke with a grave expression.
“This is enough. Junior Brother, Sect Leader.”
This is enough.
It was a short sentence, but the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord understood at once what it meant.
That was precisely why he couldn’t believe it.
“Enough? What in the world are you...”
“We’re out of time. The longer this goes on, the greater our sect’s losses will be.”
“Senior Brother!”
His cry rang with shock.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword pressed his lips together. Beside him, the Roaring Fury Swordsman gritted his teeth as he watched the two Black Ghosts slowly approach.
“He’s right. We’ve already secured a way out. Give the order! Now!”
It sounded less like an appeal than a command.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord stared blankly at his two Senior Brothers.
“Are you... serious?”
Neither answered.
Unable to meet their Junior Brother’s wide eyes, they kept their fearful gazes fixed on the Black Ghosts.
They knew how far what they were proposing strayed from the righteous path.
Seeing them like that, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord finally understood that this was real.
“...You were serious. Both of you.”
What was he supposed to call this feeling?
It was strange.
They had spent their lives together, studying under the same Master. Yet they seemed unfamiliar now, as though he were seeing them for the first time.
Retreat. Retreat.
The word echoed through his hollow heart, and memories came to him, beginning with the day he first joined the Zhongnan Sect.
Even in that distant past, now buried in dust, the three of them had always been together.
He had been glad of it.
They were closer to martial artists than Daoists and sometimes caused trouble with their harsh words and actions, but they were his Senior Brothers.
When he was appointed Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect, they had been angry that they weren’t chosen. In the end, they had accepted it and followed him.
When trouble arose with the Nanman Beast Palace during the Great Faction War.
When, only a year ago, their own mistakes had led to their humiliation at the hands of Jeok Cheongang and then Jin Taekyung.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had stood up for them, stopping their critics and speaking in their defense.
And when both Senior Brothers recovered from their Internal Injuries at a speed that astonished everyone, no one had been happier than he was.
But...
“How did you come to this?”
He let out a quiet sigh.
He shrugged off the support of his two Senior Brothers, who stared at him with wide eyes, and gripped the hilt—all that remained of his beloved sword—so tightly it seemed ready to break.
“Do you remember? When Master gave me this sword, he said, ‘You need not strive to become a Daoist. Just live rightly. If you uphold your duty as a human being, that makes you a Daoist.’”
“If you want so badly to live, then go, Senior Brothers. I’ll stay. That is the only way not to disgrace the name of the Great Zhongnan Sect we inherited from our Master.”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord knew. So did the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
Everyone on the battlefield knew.
If the Zhongnan Sect, one of the forces holding the battlefront together at this point, withdrew, this battle would be a certain defeat.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord could not retreat.
Not him.
Grnk.
He bit his tongue. The sharp pain cleared his vision.
He stepped toward the two Black Ghosts approaching through billowing clouds of black smoke.
Squish.
His feet were heavy. So was his heart.
Perhaps he wanted to flee this place too.
But he didn’t stop.
He couldn’t run away.
That was the duty his Master had taught him to uphold as a human being.
Looking back, I wasn’t much of a Daoist either.
He had always envied Huashan for forging ahead and pursued only the Zhongnan Sect’s interests.
He’d grown the sect’s influence through wealth exchanged in collusion with those in power, and accepted Disciples for their talent rather than their character.
He had believed it was the right way to serve the Zhongnan Sect.
Yet through it all, he had never forgotten affection and loyalty.
Countless allies were still fighting for their lives here.
And in the most dangerous place of all, a young man faced a greater threat than anyone else.
Shame.
That was why he couldn’t retreat.
“Come. No—this time, I’ll come to you.”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s voice was thick with blood.
With eyes clearer than ever, he watched the two monsters approach and poured every last bit of his energy into the remains of his beloved sword.
Tsssss!
Brilliant Sword Force blazed.
It was the last flame he could kindle as Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect and as a martial artist.
“For the Great Zhongnan Sect.”
The words barely left his lips before he hurled himself forward with all his strength.
“No!”
“Junior Brother, Sect Leader!”
He left his Senior Brothers’ cries behind and flew toward the Black Ghosts like a moth to a flame. Two streaks of light waited for him.
Whish! Sshhh!
A massive battle-ax shattered the wind. A white sword blade sliced through space.
As he charged into that wave of destructive power, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord knew with sudden calm:
This is the end.
Even with every ounce of strength he had, this strike would not kill them.
But then something happened that neither he, having accepted his death, nor anyone else on the battlefield could have foreseen.
Whoom—KWA-BOOOOM!
A blinding flash erupted in the distance, and an enormous shock wave slammed across the battlefield.
An explosion. A calamity.
He didn’t know what to call it, but one thing was clear.
Grind!

The unexpected shock wave threw the two Black Ghosts off balance where they stood, while the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s strike, already hurtling through the air, slipped between their two streaks of light.
Shhk!
The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, wrought from dazzling light, cleaved through space.
Fwoosh.
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord swept past the two Black Ghosts like the wind. Then he—and everyone else on the battlefield—looked up on instinct.
At last, they saw it.
Flicker.
A sphere of flame so enormous it seemed not to belong to this world.
Hellfire dragged up from the depths of hell—Hell Fire.

chapters.title: Chapter 1043
paragraphs: For one instant, everyone on the battlefield stared at the sky, their eyes vacant.
Not a single person was an exception.
Not even the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, who had brought down two Black Ghosts thanks to what could only be called a stroke of heaven-sent luck.
Not even his two pathetic Senior Brothers, who had somehow gone somber and were now rushing to support their Junior Brother as he staggered, utterly spent.
Not even the Disciples of the Zhongnan Sect and the Gansu Murim Alliance, still fighting their separate battles on the blood-soaked snow.

Not even a father standing like a stone monument where his son had disappeared, or the Fire Dragon Pavilion members pouring every last bit of strength into chasing after their friend and leader, who had already raced far ahead.
Not even the Dark Heaven cultists, whose eyes were empty as they continued their mindless fighting.
Every living being looked at it.
A vast sphere of fire, unlike anything they had ever seen or heard of.
Grrrrrrr-BOOM.
Would this be the sound of an ancient giant roaring?
If the brimstone fires of hell recorded in old scriptures really existed, would they look like this?
A deafening roar poured down over everyone’s heads, leaving their ears ringing.
As the sphere fell from a dizzying height like a meteor, its terrible heat scorched the sky.
“A-aah...”
Groans rose from here and there.
Everyone froze where they stood. It was all they could do.
They were seeing it with their own eyes, and still they couldn’t believe it. Something beyond comprehension.
No—a calamity.
That was why no one knew its exact name.
No one except the person who had desperately tried to stop it, but failed in the end.
Hell Fire...!
In a world that seemed frozen in time, Jin Taekyung bit back the scream rising between his lips.
Hellfire, just as its name suggested.
One of the most powerful wide-area spells a human could wield—a calamity in its own right, capable of taking thousands of lives with a single cast.
No.
He knew its power better than anyone. That was why he’d tried to stop it.
He hadn’t cared if he lost his life in the process.
If he could bring someone down in exchange—if he could stop the calamity—he could have told himself it was a decent end.
But in the end, he hadn’t stopped it.
Right now, all Jin Taekyung could do was feel the weakness constricting his entire body and stare blankly as the calamity unfolded.
Even now... I have to do something. Somehow.
His vision wavered, no matter how desperately he wished otherwise.
And that wasn’t all.
Every bone and muscle in his body screamed in pain, as if squeezed in a giant’s fist. His dantian was already empty; he couldn’t find even a trace of internal energy.
The One Annihilation he’d launched before it was complete.
That had been both misfortune and good luck.
Because it was incomplete, it hadn’t shattered every defensive barrier. Because of that, Jin Taekyung had survived.
But for someone who had been prepared to give up everything, this was misfortune.
Shit.
The horrible aftereffects tore deeper and deeper through his body. Jin Taekyung shuddered without meaning to.
But he couldn’t give up. He didn’t want to give up on everything here.
Crack.
He clenched his teeth and moved his twitching arms and legs.
Gripping the spear shaft before it could slip from his hand, he used it as a cane and hauled his unsteady body upright.
“—Get out of the way! All of you!”
“Aaah! Aaaaaah!”
He heard the screams of those who had finally realized that the calamity falling from the sky, painting it red, was real.
He heard, too, the terrible confusion and fear covering the battlefield below the hill—and, somehow out of place amid it all, a calm voice.
“Why don’t you just lie down? If you push yourself any harder, you really will be in trouble.”
At the Grand Mage’s composed voice, blood trickled from between Jin Taekyung’s clenched lips.
“Shut your damn mouth, you bitch.”
“That’s a little harsh. When you think about it, I’m the one who saved your life.”
Pop.
He appeared beside him as if he’d teleported—or, rather, he had used Blink, which was teleportation itself—and stopped less than a jang away.
More precisely, he stopped before the invisible magic barrier still standing between them.
“Honestly, you really surprised me just now. It gave me goose bumps.”
His fingers, so thin and translucent that every vein showed through, gently traced the barrier.
The powerful barrier he’d personally layered dozens of times was down to a single layer, barely holding its shape. But he showed no sign of tension.
He knew Jin Taekyung could barely get to his feet under his own power, let alone attack.
“I’m only saying this out of concern, but don’t waste your effort. You know, don’t you? Killing me now won’t undo what’s already happened.”
“Yeah. I know.”
Jin Taekyung answered between ragged breaths.
But unlike his voice, his eyes weren’t on the Grand Mage.
He watched the hellfire cross the blackened sky, moving slowly for all its enormous size, and continued.
“I also know you—and the rest of your lot—can never kill me.”
He knew that better than anyone. Without hesitation, Jin Taekyung turned and gripped White Flame in a reverse hold.
He hadn’t risked his life just to kill the Grand Mage.
He’d fought to protect one ally rather than bring down one formidable enemy—to protect tens of thousands of lives.
Please. Just once. One last time.
With a desperate prayer, Jin Taekyung wrung every last thread of energy from his body.
He made his body, ready to break at any moment, into a bow and set White Flame against its string.
Crrrk.
Excruciating pain filled his vision.
His already-weakened body screamed.
The acupoints damaged by his earlier, excessive release of power burned even under the tiny amount of Scorching Yang Qi he could muster.
Grind.
But Jin Taekyung clenched his teeth and endured pain no ordinary person could even imagine.
He swallowed the blood pooled in his mouth along with the pieces of a molar that had cracked and finally broken apart.
Even now, the blazing sphere was drawing closer to the ground. He aimed his spearhead at it.
Only a faint shimmer of energy clung to the spearhead, like a heat haze. It could no longer be called Force.
“You really are a fool.”
The Grand Mage’s voice came with a sigh, but Jin Taekyung didn’t hear it.
He focused every sense and every ounce of strength on seizing his last chance.
Can I do this?
The question surfaced in his mind.
But Jin Taekyung already knew the answer.
No—or rather, anyone who saw this situation would give the same answer.
He couldn’t.
It was nothing but a foolish dream.
Nothing more than the desperate struggle and wish of a man who wanted to do everything he could right up to the end.
But...
If I couldn’t even dream a foolish dream like this, I never would’ve made it this far.
For one young man, life had been a long dream.
He’d been enraged by cruel reality, resigned himself to it, and even despaired for a time. But the young man had kept dreaming.
Then, one day, the dream became reality.
In that dream, he discovered an unexpected new goal and longing, great power—and an even heavier responsibility.
That was the one reason.
The reason he could never give up, even if he was a moth flying toward a blazing flame, even if he was a firefly destined to vanish in the heat of the burning sun.
Step. Scrape.
His trembling legs finally steadied and planted themselves in the ground like iron pillars.
His shoulder drew all the way back. Then, with a powerful step forward, he sent the spearhead aimed at the distant sky flying.
Go.
Whoom!
Every bit of strength one man possessed condensed, then burst forth.
Compressed air exploded with it.
Shwoooosh!
White Flame’s spearhead tore through the wind. It split open space.
A streak of light crossed the sky, dyed in ominous darkness, and shot toward a sphere whose size and power dwarfed it.
It covered more than a hundred jang of distance, shrinking until it became a single point. Jin Taekyung watched it with eyes growing dim.
The spearhead hadn’t reached its target yet.
But some things could be known without seeing them.
Like this.
It’s no use.
An empty murmur echoed in Jin Taekyung’s heart.
Failure.
He had nowhere near enough strength, speed, or internal energy to stop the Hell Fire the Grand Mage had prepared.
That was all. That was all there was to it.
Now that he’d poured out everything, Jin Taekyung had nothing left.
If anything remained, it was exhaustion weighing even more heavily on his body, and a helplessness greater than that.
And the enemy’s sneer—the one who’d brought all of this upon him.
“Oh, don’t be too disappointed. From where I was standing, it was a very impressive attempt.”
The Grand Mage spoke with a mix of sympathy and amusement as he watched the spearhead, carrying the faintest trace of energy, finally touch the Magic he’d cast.
And at the same time, he heard it clearly.
The deafening boom that rang out all around them, as if the sky had split apart.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Jin Taekyung and the Grand Mage both stared wide-eyed.
Grrrrrrr-BOOM!
Hell Fire.
The horrifying hellfire, the enormous sphere of flame, was shaking.
“What is this...!”
The Grand Mage was astonished.
The outcome had seemed as certain as a life-and-death duel between a child and a Supreme Peak master.
Jin Taekyung was exhausted, and the force behind White Flame’s spearhead had been pitifully weak.
That was why he’d simply watched without even trying to stop him.
He’d known from the start that he couldn’t do it.
To the Grand Mage, it was nothing more than a foolish dream.
And yet that single spear had changed the course of a sphere of fire hundreds of times its size.
It had bent part of the blazing flames and opened a rift in them.
“How...? How could this possibly happen?”
In the midst of a reality he couldn’t begin to understand, the Grand Mage suddenly turned his head.
At last, he saw Jin Taekyung struggling to hold his unsteady body upright as he watched the unbelievable sight.
He saw the faint smile on Jin Taekyung’s face, and his lips, caked with dried blood, moving.
“Yeah. Nobody wants to give up.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice came out with difficulty, but it rang clearly in the Grand Mage’s ears.
“Me, too. And them.”
Just a few words.
But the Grand Mage felt something and whipped his head around. At the same time, he found the answer to the question he’d asked himself moments earlier.
Shwoooosh—KWA-BOOM!
Dazzling streaks of light shot up from the ground and rained down on the sphere of fire covering everyone’s heads.
There were others who shared that young man’s dream.

sentences.text: For one instant, everyone on the battlefield stared at the sky, their eyes vacant.
Not a single person was an exception.
Not even the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, who had brought down two Black Ghosts thanks to what could only be called a stroke of heaven-sent luck.
Not even his two pathetic Senior Brothers, who had somehow gone somber and were now rushing to support their Junior Brother as he staggered, utterly spent.
Not even the Disciples of the Zhongnan Sect and the Gansu Murim Alliance, still fighting their separate battles on the blood-soaked snow.

Not even a father standing like a stone monument where his son had disappeared, or the Fire Dragon Pavilion members pouring every last bit of strength into chasing after their friend and leader, who had already raced far ahead.
Not even the Dark Heaven cultists, whose eyes were empty as they continued their mindless fighting.
Every living being looked at it.
A vast sphere of fire, unlike anything they had ever seen or heard of.
Grrrrrrr-BOOM.
Would this be the sound of an ancient giant roaring?
If the brimstone fires of hell recorded in old scriptures really existed, would they look like this?
A deafening roar poured down over everyone’s heads, leaving their ears ringing.
As the sphere fell from a dizzying height like a meteor, its terrible heat scorched the sky.
“A-aah...”
Groans rose from here and there.
Everyone froze where they stood.
It was all they could do.
They were seeing it with their own eyes, and still they couldn’t believe it.
Something beyond comprehension.
No—a calamity.
That was why no one knew its exact name.
No one except the person who had desperately tried to stop it, but failed in the end.
Hell Fire...!
In a world that seemed frozen in time, Jin Taekyung bit back the scream rising between his lips.
Hellfire, just as its name suggested.
One of the most powerful wide-area spells a human could wield—a calamity in its own right, capable of taking thousands of lives with a single cast.
No.
He knew its power better than anyone.
That was why he’d tried to stop it.
He hadn’t cared if he lost his life in the process.
If he could bring someone down in exchange—if he could stop the calamity—he could have told himself it was a decent end.
But in the end, he hadn’t stopped it.
Right now, all Jin Taekyung could do was feel the weakness constricting his entire body and stare blankly as the calamity unfolded.
Even now...
I have to do something.
Somehow.
His vision wavered, no matter how desperately he wished otherwise.
And that wasn’t all.
Every bone and muscle in his body screamed in pain, as if squeezed in a giant’s fist.
His dantian was already empty; he couldn’t find even a trace of internal energy.
The One Annihilation he’d launched before it was complete.
That had been both misfortune and good luck.
Because it was incomplete, it hadn’t shattered every defensive barrier.
Because of that, Jin Taekyung had survived.
But for someone who had been prepared to give up everything, this was misfortune.
Shit.
The horrible aftereffects tore deeper and deeper through his body.
Jin Taekyung shuddered without meaning to.
But he couldn’t give up.
He didn’t want to give up on everything here.
Crack.
He clenched his teeth and moved his twitching arms and legs.
Gripping the spear shaft before it could slip from his hand, he used it as a cane and hauled his unsteady body upright.
“—Get out of the way!
All of you!”
“Aaah!
Aaaaaah!”
He heard the screams of those who had finally realized that the calamity falling from the sky, painting it red, was real.
He heard, too, the terrible confusion and fear covering the battlefield below the hill—and, somehow out of place amid it all, a calm voice.
“Why don’t you just lie down?
If you push yourself any harder, you really will be in trouble.”
At the Grand Mage’s composed voice, blood trickled from between Jin Taekyung’s clenched lips.
“Shut your damn mouth, you bitch.”
“That’s a little harsh.
When you think about it, I’m the one who saved your life.”
Pop.
He appeared beside him as if he’d teleported—or, rather, he had used Blink, which was teleportation itself—and stopped less than a jang away.
More precisely, he stopped before the invisible magic barrier still standing between them.
“Honestly, you really surprised me just now.
It gave me goose bumps.”
His fingers, so thin and translucent that every vein showed through, gently traced the barrier.
The powerful barrier he’d personally layered dozens of times was down to a single layer, barely holding its shape.
But he showed no sign of tension.
He knew Jin Taekyung could barely get to his feet under his own power, let alone attack.
“I’m only saying this out of concern, but don’t waste your effort.
You know, don’t you?
Killing me now won’t undo what’s already happened.”
“Yeah.
I know.”
Jin Taekyung answered between ragged breaths.
But unlike his voice, his eyes weren’t on the Grand Mage.
He watched the hellfire cross the blackened sky, moving slowly for all its enormous size, and continued.
“I also know you—and the rest of your lot—can never kill me.”
He knew that better than anyone.
Without hesitation, Jin Taekyung turned and gripped White Flame in a reverse hold.
He hadn’t risked his life just to kill the Grand Mage.
He’d fought to protect one ally rather than bring down one formidable enemy—to protect tens of thousands of lives.
Please.
Just once.
One last time.
With a desperate prayer, Jin Taekyung wrung every last thread of energy from his body.
He made his body, ready to break at any moment, into a bow and set White Flame against its string.
Crrrk.
Excruciating pain filled his vision.
His already-weakened body screamed.
The acupoints damaged by his earlier, excessive release of power burned even under the tiny amount of Scorching Yang Qi he could muster.
Grind.
But Jin Taekyung clenched his teeth and endured pain no ordinary person could even imagine.
He swallowed the blood pooled in his mouth along with the pieces of a molar that had cracked and finally broken apart.
Even now, the blazing sphere was drawing closer to the ground.

Only a faint shimmer of energy clung to the spearhead, like a heat haze.
