chapters.title: Chapter 1044
paragraphs: The Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, suddenly wondered what he was doing.
There was barely enough time to escape this hopeless battlefield. Why was he still swinging his sword with all his might?
Shwoooosh!
Streams of Force raced along his blade and tore through the air.
The dazzling streak of light, aimed neither ahead nor behind but into empty space, crossed a distance of more than twenty jang and struck the enormous ball of fire in the blink of an eye.
KWA-BOOM!
The sphere shuddered with a deafening roar.
But it faltered for only a moment. Then the calamity resumed its descent as though nothing had happened, and despair filled the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes.
It’s no use. I can’t stop it.
He knew by instinct. He’d already given it everything he had several times.
He was worthy of being called a superhuman, yet his strength was nowhere near enough to stop that enormous fireball—a thing that might as well have been wrought by supernatural powers.
What the hell is this...
He could barely breathe.

The sphere was slowly covering part of the battlefield, its heat unbearable even from this distance. And the helplessness gripping his whole body was something he’d felt only a handful of times in his life.
But at that very moment—
Pop, sh-sh-sh-shk!
The Roaring Fury Swordsman sensed someone appear beside him. At the same time, he saw dazzling streaks of light surge forward.
Fwoosh!
This is...
His eyes widened.
Dazzling light spread. Even from more than twenty jang away, the heat that had warmed his skin vanished in an instant.
Dozens of streams of Force shot forward, woven as tightly as a net. He knew them at once.
“Junior Brother!”
KWA-BOOOOM!
His reflexive shout mingled with another deafening roar. Beneath the fiery fragments raining down from the collision, a familiar figure appeared.
“We meet again so soon, Senior Brother.”

His expression and voice were so cold that anyone else might have found them chilling. The Roaring Fury Swordsman murmured, almost groaning, at the sight of his Junior Brother, known to the world by that very demeanor as the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
“How did you get here...!”
His surprise held more confusion than joy, and even a trace of worry and anger. The Taeeul Merciless Sword answered calmly.
“What, did you think this Hwangbo Eom would obey you so readily?”
“You fool! What kind of nonsense is that? What happened to Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, and the other Disciples?”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman bellowed, living up to his fiery sobriquet.
Only moments ago, he’d left Hwangbo Eom to look after the Sect Leader—who had finally collapsed from exhaustion and injuries—and the surviving Disciples of their sect.
Hwangbo Eom should have been leading them in a swift retreat. Instead, he was here.
For a moment, the Roaring Fury Swordsman forgot everything around him and shouted at the top of his lungs.
“You idiot! If you’re gone too, who in the world is going to lead our sect...!”
“They say old habits die hard. You certainly live up to your sobriquet. Come to think of it, you’ve always been like that, Senior Brother—even as a child.”
“What?”
No answer came. Ignoring his Senior Brother’s incredulous stare, Hwangbo Eom swung his sword.
His face was as impassive as ever, but the veins standing out on his skin showed how much strength he was pouring into every strike.
Shwaak! KWA-BOOOOM!
Force shot from his blade and collided with the flames.
The fireball faltered again. Fragments broke away and fell toward the ground amid a drizzle of sparks.
“As I thought, this won’t be enough. Not on my own.”
“Are you ready for the Moon-Shattering Sword Formation?”
This time, Song Il was the one who gave no answer.
He glared furiously at Hwangbo Eom, gathered all his strength, and swung his sword upward.
Shhk, shwoooosh!
Their sword strikes, as different as their temperaments, flew side by side through the air as though competing.
No. They seemed about to collide, but instead they mingled, growing more powerful together.
As if to prove they had grown from the same root.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The roar was louder, the shock wave stronger than ever before.
The fireball’s course shifted, if only slightly. Taking what encouragement they could from the sight, the two martial brothers poured out Force with everything they had.
Shhk, whoooosh!
They slashed, struck upward, and thrust.
Amid the ceaseless explosions, the two old Daoists could still hear each other speak.
“Don’t worry about Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, and the other Disciples. So Pyeong will do his duty well.”
“So Pyeong... I see. So that’s how it ended up.”
It was too late to change anything now.
Only then did the Roaring Fury Swordsman realize who was leading the Zhongnan Sect’s survivors. His face darkened.
The Zhongnan Sect’s thousand finest.
In less than half a shichen, a third of them had been killed or wounded. Among those still able to move, few Disciples were ready to bear the sect’s future.
Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.
The Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy, and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—the finest young martial artists of the Central Plains.

He had once been so lost in wine and women that he couldn’t come to his senses. But since the dispute between the Taeeul Merciless Sword and the Yongbong Escort Bureau, he had grown remarkably, both as a person and as a martial artist.
Even so, the Roaring Fury Swordsman could not set aside his concern.
“He’s still too young. You should have stayed behind.”

“By that reasoning, you’re the problem, Senior Brother, and we could go on forever. Besides, I was even younger than him during the Great Faction War. Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, was younger still.”
“That was different.”
“I’d like to ask how, but I’ll let it go this time.”
Shwaak!
His blade tore through the air.
Spreading a net of Force with all his might, the Taeeul Merciless Sword added in a low voice, “At least back then, supernatural powers like this weren’t running rampant.”
KWA-BOOOOM!
A roar like the sky splitting open. Heat fierce enough to burn them at any moment.
At the center of it all was a fireball much larger than it had been only moments ago.
It might shudder, and pieces might break away, but the calamity kept falling, as inexorable as a mountain.
Closer now, it loomed larger still: hellfire that would devour thousands of lives.
“Can we... stop that?”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman was breathing hard. The Taeeul Merciless Sword, just as visibly exhausted, answered with a question of his own.
“What do I look like to you, Senior Brother?”
A silence passed, brief and yet seemingly endless.
But the Roaring Fury Swordsman had a good idea what his Junior Brother meant.
Right. They couldn’t stop it.
They were only human, and that was a power beyond their understanding, a force of supernatural powers.
If anyone could hold this mad calamity back even a little, it would be true superhumans—those who, in human bodies, had reached a realm comparable to monsters or gods.
“I must be going senile. I never thought I’d want to see that mad old monster, the Fire King.”
“For once, I had a similar thought. A moment ago, I saw some reckless brat flash before my eyes. It made me wonder if I’d really lost my mind.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
And the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
The two martial brothers would never forget them for as long as they lived.
Not for any good reason, of course.
“They can’t come, can they?”
“Why ask when you already know?”

The senses of Supreme Peak masters surpassed anything ordinary people could imagine. Reading the events unfolding across the battlefield, the two men already suspected that neither the old monster nor the young one from the Fire Gate Clan could come to their aid.
And at the same time, they held the contradictory wish that they didn’t want help from either of them, whatever the circumstances.
Even now, they hadn’t been able to let go of their grudge against the Fire Gate Clan’s Master and Disciple.
And that grudge had led them to commit an irreversible wrong.
KWA! KWA! KWA-BOOOOM!
Explosions followed one another.
But the Force Song Il and Hwangbo Eom unleashed had grown noticeably weaker. The fireball was now less than ten jang away, its heat fierce enough to burn away the last of their will to fight.
Grrrrrrr.
It was hot.
A crimson-black shadow, unlike anything they’d ever seen and something they’d never experience again, covered part of the battlefield.
“Do you... regret it?”
The Taeeul Merciless Sword’s quiet question slipped between parched lips.
Staring hollow-eyed at the sky, the Roaring Fury Swordsman answered.
“Yes.”
Seeing his Senior Brother like that, the Junior Brother did not ask what he regretted.
Nor did Song Il ask whether Hwangbo Eom regretted it too.
They had exchanged only a few words, but everything had been said. Each was left with his own silent thoughts.
We should never have done it.
The two men had temperaments as different as their sobriquets, but they’d lived similar lives. In this moment, the same thoughts came to them.
Their peaceful childhood, spent honing their martial arts rather than learning to act with humanity and righteousness.
Their youth, steeped in blood and death, when they’d chased achievements instead of living by a martial artist’s code.
The years of regained peace, when their black hair turned white and they swiftly gave themselves over to self-interest and desire.
And then—
“I hear you two went through quite an ordeal.”
One day, after paying the price for their greed, they had been left with severe Internal Injuries and inner demons. Consumed by hatred, they had received a tempting offer.
“This is a rare elixir I managed to acquire. Its effects rival Shaolin’s Great Restoration Pill. It will be more than enough to heal your Internal Injuries.”

They had said they would not meet him, but the uninvited guest had managed to see them anyway. When the two martial brothers doubted such unbelievable generosity, he offered them something they could not refuse.
“This isn’t generosity. It’s a transaction. If you accept, you can settle an old grudge and help safeguard the Zhongnan Sect as well.”
They had hesitated. In the end, they accepted.

They’d spent their lives as the direct disciples of the Zhongnan Sect Leader, heroes of the Great Faction War and respected masters of the martial world. They couldn’t go on living with this indelible humiliation weighing on them.
They had to take revenge.
Even if they did not kill anyone, they had to inflict on the Fire Gate Clan the same humiliation they had suffered.
And the transaction would safeguard the Zhongnan Sect too.
They could not refuse such a sweet offer.
They had willingly taken the hand extended by the uninvited guest. No—by Sima Gong, the Black Night King.
Only months later did they come to regret that decision.
Now they watched the blazing flames slowly closing over their heads.
“How did you come to this?”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.
Their youngest Junior Brother had spoken those words in a hollow voice. Hearing the regret in it, they had understood what choice remained to them.
What they had to do.
“Run. There’s still time.”
“I refuse. You go, Senior Brother.”
“I refuse, too.”
Three jang.
The enormous sphere of fire filled their vision. The two martial brothers stared at it, dazed.
“We never had a chance of stopping it.”
“That’s right.”
“Then why did you come?”
“For the same reason you did, Senior Brother. I felt I had to do something. Even if it was only this. And...”
Two jang.
The heat and light pouring from the flames were so blinding that the Taeeul Merciless Sword closed his eyes.
Or perhaps he was too ashamed to face the world openly as he died.
“...I was ashamed. And I was sorry.”
To the Master who had taught them humanity and righteousness.
To their youngest Junior Brother and the sect’s Disciples, who had treated them as Senior Brothers despite how unworthy they were.
To everyone else.
And to a certain Master and Disciple who, unlike them—who’d strayed from the path long ago—still walked the righteous path.
“What a damned mess.”
Whether the words slipped from the Taeeul Merciless Sword’s lips or the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s, the voice sounded more hollow than ever.
Fwoooooosh!
The heat and light pouring from the enormous fireball, extending across a radius of hundreds of jang, were more magnificent than ever.

Force shot from his blade and collided with the flames.
The fireball faltered again.
Fragments broke away and fell toward the ground amid a drizzle of sparks.
“As I thought, this won’t be enough.
Not on my own.”
“Are you ready for the Moon-Shattering Sword Formation?”
This time, Song Il was the one who gave no answer.
He glared furiously at Hwangbo Eom, gathered all his strength, and swung his sword upward.
Shhk, shwoooosh!
Their sword strikes, as different as their temperaments, flew side by side through the air as though competing.
No.
They seemed about to collide, but instead they mingled, growing more powerful together.
As if to prove they had grown from the same root.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The roar was louder, the shock wave stronger than ever before.
The fireball’s course shifted, if only slightly.
Taking what encouragement they could from the sight, the two martial brothers poured out Force with everything they had.
Shhk, whoooosh!
They slashed, struck upward, and thrust.
Amid the ceaseless explosions, the two old Daoists could still hear each other speak.
“Don’t worry about Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, and the other Disciples.
So Pyeong will do his duty well.”
“So Pyeong...
I see.
So that’s how it ended up.”
It was too late to change anything now.
Only then did the Roaring Fury Swordsman realize who was leading the Zhongnan Sect’s survivors.
His face darkened.
The Zhongnan Sect’s thousand finest.
In less than half a shichen, a third of them had been killed or wounded.
Among those still able to move, few Disciples were ready to bear the sect’s future.
Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.
The Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy, and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—the finest young martial artists of the Central Plains.
He had once been so lost in wine and women that he couldn’t come to his senses.
But since the dispute between the Taeeul Merciless Sword and the Yongbong Escort Bureau, he had grown remarkably, both as a person and as a martial artist.
Even so, the Roaring Fury Swordsman could not set aside his concern.
“He’s still too young.
You should have stayed behind.”
“By that reasoning, you’re the problem, Senior Brother, and we could go on forever.
Besides, I was even younger than him during the Great Faction War.
Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, was younger still.”
“That was different.”
“I’d like to ask how, but I’ll let it go this time.”
Shwaak!
His blade tore through the air.
Spreading a net of Force with all his might, the Taeeul Merciless Sword added in a low voice, “At least back then, supernatural powers like this weren’t running rampant.”
KWA-BOOOOM!
A roar like the sky splitting open.
Heat fierce enough to burn them at any moment.
At the center of it all was a fireball much larger than it had been only moments ago.
It might shudder, and pieces might break away, but the calamity kept falling, as inexorable as a mountain.
Closer now, it loomed larger still: hellfire that would devour thousands of lives.
“Can we... stop that?”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman was breathing hard.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword, just as visibly exhausted, answered with a question of his own.
“What do I look like to you, Senior Brother?”
A silence passed, brief and yet seemingly endless.
But the Roaring Fury Swordsman had a good idea what his Junior Brother meant.
Right.
They couldn’t stop it.
They were only human, and that was a power beyond their understanding, a force of supernatural powers.
If anyone could hold this mad calamity back even a little, it would be true superhumans—those who, in human bodies, had reached a realm comparable to monsters or gods.
“I must be going senile.
I never thought I’d want to see that mad old monster, the Fire King.”
“For once, I had a similar thought.
A moment ago, I saw some reckless brat flash before my eyes.
It made me wonder if I’d really lost my mind.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
And the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
The two martial brothers would never forget them for as long as they lived.
Not for any good reason, of course.
“They can’t come, can they?”
“Why ask when you already know?”
The senses of Supreme Peak masters surpassed anything ordinary people could imagine.
Reading the events unfolding across the battlefield, the two men already suspected that neither the old monster nor the young one from the Fire Gate Clan could come to their aid.
And at the same time, they held the contradictory wish that they didn’t want help from either of them, whatever the circumstances.
Even now, they hadn’t been able to let go of their grudge against the Fire Gate Clan’s Master and Disciple.
And that grudge had led them to commit an irreversible wrong.
KWA!
KWA!
KWA-BOOOOM!
Explosions followed one another.
But the Force Song Il and Hwangbo Eom unleashed had grown noticeably weaker.
The fireball was now less than ten jang away, its heat fierce enough to burn away the last of their will to fight.
Grrrrrrr.
It was hot.
A crimson-black shadow, unlike anything they’d ever seen and something they’d never experience again, covered part of the battlefield.
“Do you... regret it?”
The Taeeul Merciless Sword’s quiet question slipped between parched lips.
Staring hollow-eyed at the sky, the Roaring Fury Swordsman answered.
“Yes.”
Seeing his Senior Brother like that, the Junior Brother did not ask what he regretted.
Nor did Song Il ask whether Hwangbo Eom regretted it too.
They had exchanged only a few words, but everything had been said.
Each was left with his own silent thoughts.
We should never have done it.
The two men had temperaments as different as their sobriquets, but they’d lived similar lives.
In this moment, the same thoughts came to them.
Their peaceful childhood, spent honing their martial arts rather than learning to act with humanity and righteousness.
Their youth, steeped in blood and death, when they’d chased achievements instead of living by a martial artist’s code.
The years of regained peace, when their black hair turned white and they swiftly gave themselves over to self-interest and desire.
And then—
“I hear you two went through quite an ordeal.”
One day, after paying the price for their greed, they had been left with severe Internal Injuries and inner demons.
Consumed by hatred, they had received a tempting offer.
“This is a rare elixir I managed to acquire.
Its effects rival Shaolin’s Great Restoration Pill.
It will be more than enough to heal your Internal Injuries.”
They had said they would not meet him, but the uninvited guest had managed to see them anyway.
When the two martial brothers doubted such unbelievable generosity, he offered them something they could not refuse.
“This isn’t generosity.
It’s a transaction.
If you accept, you can settle an old grudge and help safeguard the Zhongnan Sect as well.”
They had hesitated.
In the end, they accepted.
They’d spent their lives as the direct disciples of the Zhongnan Sect Leader, heroes of the Great Faction War and respected masters of the martial world.
They couldn’t go on living with this indelible humiliation weighing on them.
They had to take revenge.
Even if they did not kill anyone, they had to inflict on the Fire Gate Clan the same humiliation they had suffered.
And the transaction would safeguard the Zhongnan Sect too.
They could not refuse such a sweet offer.
They had willingly taken the hand extended by the uninvited guest.
No—by Sima Gong, the Black Night King.
Only months later did they come to regret that decision.
Now they watched the blazing flames slowly closing over their heads.
“How did you come to this?”
The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.
Their youngest Junior Brother had spoken those words in a hollow voice.
Hearing the regret in it, they had understood what choice remained to them.
What they had to do.
“Run.
There’s still time.”
“I refuse.
You go, Senior Brother.”
“I refuse, too.”
Three jang.
The enormous sphere of fire filled their vision.
The two martial brothers stared at it, dazed.
“We never had a chance of stopping it.”
“That’s right.”
“Then why did you come?”
“For the same reason you did, Senior Brother.
I felt I had to do something.
Even if it was only this.
And...”
Two jang.
The heat and light pouring from the flames were so blinding that the Taeeul Merciless Sword closed his eyes.
Or perhaps he was too ashamed to face the world openly as he died.
“...I was ashamed.
And I was sorry.”
To the Master who had taught them humanity and righteousness.
To their youngest Junior Brother and the sect’s Disciples, who had treated them as Senior Brothers despite how unworthy they were.
To everyone else.
And to a certain Master and Disciple who, unlike them—who’d strayed from the path long ago—still walked the righteous path.
“What a damned mess.”
Whether the words slipped from the Taeeul Merciless Sword’s lips or the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s, the voice sounded more hollow than ever.
Fwoooooosh!
The heat and light pouring from the enormous fireball, extending across a radius of hundreds of jang, were more magnificent than ever.

chapters.title: Chapter 1045
paragraphs: Whatever its type or purpose, two things could bring a spell’s power to its limit.
First, the caster’s immense mana.
Second, a Magic Formation that could gather and release that mana as efficiently as possible.
The magic wielded by the woman known as the Grand Mage had both. It could hardly have been more perfect.
Just as a masterwork sword was born after countless rounds of hammering and quenching, magic, too, could reach its greatest power when enough time and effort were devoted to it.

The Magic Formation had been completed while the hillside below turned red with blood. Once it activated, no one could stop it. And Jin Taekyung wasn’t the only one who had some idea how powerful that enormous sphere of flame would be.
Fwoooooosh!
The world slowed.
Light and flame spread, slowly.
The fireball was still two jang from the ground, but the heat pouring from it was already horrifyingly intense.
It swallowed the wind and moisture around it, and the shadow of its flames spread over part of the battlefield. Fire King Jeok Cheongang watched it descend, stunned.
So this is... Magic.
The words dark arts had long since vanished from his mind.
Yes. This was Magic.
A spell wielded not by a human, but by a demon. Jeok Cheongang knew there could be no more fitting description.
He also knew that, at this moment, he was the only one left who could stop that terrible power from exploding.
Boom!
Flames burst from beneath his toes, and he shot forward like a flash of light.
But as Jeok Cheongang raced toward the fireball along the Flamefire Path, a chilling whistle sounded behind him. He ducked.
Shwoooosh! Slice!
The back of his head suddenly grew hot.
Like a skilled butcher slicing meat, a streak of dark-red Force skimmed past Jeok Cheongang’s head, slicing off a thin layer of hair and skin before cutting through the air.
“Where are you in such a hurry to go?”
His footing had wavered for the instant it took to dodge. By then, that butcher of a man had appeared in front of him at a speed surpassing Shifting Form and Position. Jeok Cheongang bit his lip.
“Blood-Sword Demon Lord, how dare you...!”
“How dare I? Even in that state, you still haven’t figured it out?”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord smiled and gave the sword in his hand a shake.
Unlike Jeok Cheongang, who was covered in blood after their fierce battle, he had suffered only a few minor wounds. Now he was certain of the difference in their strength.
Certain of his advantage.
“You can’t stop anything.”
Shwaaak!
His sword blurred like a heat shimmer and came at Jeok Cheongang, tearing through the wind.
Bang! Bang! KWA-BOOOOM!
Its speed and destructive power defied imagination.
Enormous surges of Force lashed out and exploded in every direction.
Jeok Cheongang barely dodged the attacks pouring down on him, forgetting even to breathe. His gaze grew still.
I can’t stop anything, huh? Yes, I suppose that’s true.
If all he’d had was a fiery temper, the title of Fire King might have vanished from the world long ago.
But Jeok Cheongang had survived this long in Murim’s mountain of sabers and forest of swords. Even now, with his life hanging in the balance, he faced reality with a cool head.
And he could see the one way past the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, the one way to stop the terrible calamity before it reached the ground.
Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
Yes. That was his only choice.
The final dance of a fire demon prepared to die.
The beginning and end of the Fire Gate Clan. Its fiercest blaze and its final ashes.
No flame burned forever. When the dance ended, its heat would fade and his body would burn away.
The stronger the spark within him, the greater the power of the blaze. And to sustain that growing fire, he would have to feed it more of his own life.
This will be the last time.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang knew it by instinct.
The dance about to begin would be his third—and his last.
His body held more Scorching Yang Qi than ever before. This time, it would not survive.
But he had no regrets.
Even if his body turned to ash and scattered, the spark he left behind would remain.
Even if Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s flames died out, the spark called Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, would burn brighter somewhere in the world.
So...
That’s enough.
Jeok Cheongang murmured the words to himself and twisted his body. Slipping through the dense net of Force surrounding him, he drew up every last bit of energy he possessed.
The Scorching Yang Qi he had accumulated over countless years—several jiazi’ worth.
And at last, he awoke the innate qi sleeping deep inside his body, a forbidden realm for martial artists.
No—more precisely, he tried to awaken it.
At that very moment, a massive surge of ink-black Force came flying from somewhere and blocked the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Whooom—KWA-BOOOOM!
Power clashed with power, Force with Force.
A thunderous crash shook the surrounding air.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord emerged through the dust before it could billow up, recognized the intruder, and frowned.
“...Why are you here?”
“Go, Fire King.”
The dry words slipped between firmly closed lips.
The intruder—no, Black Night King Sima Gong—kept his eyes on the Blood-Sword Demon Lord as he spoke calmly to Jeok Cheongang behind him.
“Before I change my mind.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened at this unexpected appearance.
Sima Gong was the man he’d thought a traitor.
No, he’d been certain of it.
There was much he wanted to ask him, and much he wanted to say.
But he had almost no time. Jeok Cheongang put it all aside and sprang forward again, leaving only a brief Sound Transmission behind.
Stay alive, you filthy unorthodox bastard.
There was no answer.
Only the wind tearing across his body as he followed the Flamefire Path, and the terrifying crashes and shouts that rang through it.
“How dare a bastard like you—!”
KWA-BOOOOM!
The air shook. That was all.
Jeok Cheongang realized that Sima Gong had barely blocked the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s Force from behind him. Gritting his teeth, he pushed himself to go faster.
Moments.
That was all Sima Gong could hold out against the Blood-Sword Demon Lord as he was now.
He might die within a few dozen exchanges.
But...
That’s enough.
A single finger’s breadth could decide life and death, and a gap of a split second—divided and divided again—could change one’s fate.
That was Murim. The world of superhumans.
Crack!
The ground sank beneath Jeok Cheongang’s toes as he pushed off with all his strength. The world slowed, and pure-white flames surged up.
BANG!
No flame could move faster than light.
But in that instant, Jeok Cheongang crossed dozens of jang in a single bound. Nothing could hold him back.
If one chain bound him, it was time alone.
Damn it!
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the groan threatening to break from his lips.
His body shot forward faster than ever, hurtling toward the enormous sphere of flame.
It hung less than one jang above the ground now, its terrible blaze spreading over everyone’s heads.
Just a little farther...!
But no matter how desperately he wished otherwise, events followed their cruel course.
Fwoooooosh.
Hot.
Even from more than twenty jang away, he could barely breathe.
Watching the flames swell at last before they touched the ground, Jeok Cheongang suddenly thought:
If only he’d had a few more seconds.
If only he’d been a dozen jang closer.
And...
If only someone other than him or Jin Taekyung were here. Someone who could stop this calamity.
Damn it.
Jeok Cheongang clenched his teeth and drove himself forward with the last of his strength.
He knew.
It was already too late to stop the enormous explosion.
But he had to keep going.
He belonged to neither the righteous path, the unorthodox faction, nor the Demonic Path. This was the path he had chosen.
If he didn’t at least try, he felt he’d never be able to look that reckless brat of a Disciple in the face again.
“Come on!”
Jeok Cheongang unleashed an azure dragon’s roar that shook the air around him and threw a punch with all his might at the calamity twenty jang away.
Then, in the next instant, he saw it clearly.
He heard it, too.
Shwoooooosh!
Just as the white light-flames of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist shot out in an explosion, a dazzling streak of light shone across the dark sky ahead of it, cutting through space.
Brilliant bolts plunged into the enormous, swelling sphere of flame.
Gooooooong.
In a world that seemed to have stopped, light and fire mingled in a distant flash that turned everyone’s vision white.
The sky and the earth split apart.
The world everyone knew gave way to a new world made of light.
At least in that moment, everyone on the battlefield—not just Jin Taekyung—must have felt that way.
Could this be...?
Fwoosh.
Before Jin Taekyung could fully recall the unbelievable sight he’d seen at the last moment, he felt his vision, which had been washed in blinding light, slowly return.
The white flash that had blinded everyone faded. In its place came a tremendous roar, arriving late, and flames surging up across the battlefield.
BANG! KWA-BOOOOM!
KOOOOROOM!
Was this what it would look like if the sun rained down from the sky?
Hundreds of fireballs, great and small, fell across a radius of more than a hundred jang.
They crushed frail human flesh and bone, melted the ground, and evaporated snow mixed with blood.
Like flames of death—true to the name Hell Fire.
But death did not fall equally on everyone on the battlefield.
“Ah.”
The groan that escaped someone’s lips did not belong to Jin Taekyung.
The Grand Mage gazed silently at the inferno below the hill.
More precisely, at the Dark Heaven cultists collapsing into charred lumps without even a chance to scream.
Why?
She felt no sorrow at the sight of her allies dying so horribly.
Only bewilderment.
Why had the fireball that should have exploded in the midst of the enemy broken apart and swept through her own forces instead?
Among the roughly thousands of casualties, why did the enemy number fewer than a hundred?
Those questions filled her mind. She had watched only Jeok Cheongang in the final moments, but someone else had seen it all—and already knew the answer.
“Took you damn long enough.”
“What?”
The Grand Mage turned at the voice behind her and saw Jin Taekyung smiling, weakly but unmistakably.
He was looking somewhere far beyond her shoulder. Something golden glimmered faintly in his eyes.
“Damn old hag.”
At that instant, the Grand Mage understood something and spun around in a hurry.
At the same time, she saw the answer to her question with her own eyes.
Shwoooosh!
The streak of light that had torn the fireball apart—the Force arrows.
“Bow Saint...!”

“What?”
The Grand Mage turned at the voice behind her and saw Jin Taekyung smiling, weakly but unmistakably.
He was looking somewhere far beyond her shoulder.
Something golden glimmered faintly in his eyes.
“Damn old hag.”
At that instant, the Grand Mage understood something and spun around in a hurry.
At the same time, she saw the answer to her question with her own eyes.
Shwoooosh!
The streak of light that had torn the fireball apart—the Force arrows.
“Bow Saint...!”

chapters.title: Chapter 1046
paragraphs: Among the tens of thousands of allies and enemies locked in a brutal fight across the vast battlefield, killing and dying, no one noticed at first.
Not the dazzling white flash that had flown in and shattered the enormous ball of fire.
Nor the Force arrows still raining down over the slopes of the Great Snow Mountain.
Shwip, shwip, shwip!
One, two, three. Then ten.
Ten streaks of light burst forth one after another, tearing through the air as one.
Though each had been loosed a fraction of a moment after the last, the dazzling streaks flew side by side across more than two hundred jang and struck the battlefield.
More precisely, they struck the great and small fireballs falling where they had no right to fall.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Overlapping explosions roared across the battlefield, and the heat from the collisions swept over the ground.
Fwoosh, sizzle!
Collars blackened. Hair melted away.
But to those who had already seen death coming in the spheres of flame hurtling toward them, such pain was nothing.
No—their shock was so great that, for a moment, they forgot the pain altogether.
“H-How...? Cough.”
The old Daoist, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, coughed up a mouthful of blood. He couldn’t finish his sentence; the corners of his eyes trembled.
At the last moment, he had given up everything and closed his eyes. He couldn’t believe he was still among the living.
Beside him, though, someone who had watched death bear down on them reacted differently.
“Heh. Heh...”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman let out a weak laugh, not even noticing that one of his arms had been burned black.
He had wanted to die like this. He deserved to die.
And yet he had survived.
Thanks to help he had never expected.
Today, he had seen that destructive, dazzling flash again—the one he’d witnessed in his distant youth, when his now-melted white hair had still been black.
Bow Saint. Is it really you?
An incredible coincidence? Or Heaven’s grace?
With those words echoing in his heart, the Roaring Fury Swordsman squeezed out what strength remained and rose to his feet.
He didn’t know whether this was mere good fortune or fate decreed by Heaven.
But one thing was certain.
If there was a reason they were still alive, it was to pay for the sins they had yet to atone for.
“...Primordial Heavenly Venerable.”
At last, the Roaring Fury Swordsman planted both feet on the ground. For the first time in ages, he invoked the Primordial Heavenly Venerable and looked up at the sky.
Shaa.
As if answering his call, a ray of light slipped through the black clouds blanketing the sky.
Beneath that light, the Zhongnan Sect Disciples—whom he’d thought had already left—were sweeping through their enemies.
Shing! Slice!
Swords flashed, scattering blood.
Beneath fireballs raining down only on their enemies, a desperate yet powerful battle cry rang out.
“Disciples of the Zhongnan Sect! Don’t you dare retreat!”
“Yaaah!”
KWA-BOOM!
Rrrrmmble!
Flames surged endlessly, and the earth heaved.
Even as they were charred black, the Dark Heaven forces advanced as if possessed, chanting words of praise for the Lord of Heaven.
Yet the Zhongnan Sect Disciples, now fewer than five hundred, did not stop for a single moment.
“Our path is here!”
Zhongnan One Dragon, Hyuk Sopyung.
His cry, ragged as if he were coughing up blood, roused everyone from their exhaustion.
The sight of the Disciples fighting with death already accepted, together with the Force arrows raining down one after another, halted the Gansu Coalition Army’s retreat as defeat loomed.
“Damn it! Attack!”
“Now! Push them all back!”
“Yaaah! You fucking bastards!”
Unorthodox factions, orthodox factions, dark-path figures. Even the imperial army.
They were jumbled together as chaotically as the battle itself. They still couldn’t make sense of what was happening, but all of them knew it instinctively:
If they didn’t seize this chance now, they’d never get another.

And at the front of the group charging at the enemy again with screams that sounded like cries of anguish was a band of fighters who hadn’t retreated for even an instant—not from the beginning, not now.
“Uoooooh!”
Whoom!
The sound of the weapon cutting through the air alone sent a chill down the spine.
With a battle cry like a beast’s roar, the massive two-section staff swept through the enemies blocking the way.
KRAK-KOOM!
Blood and flesh flew in every direction.
Perched on the shoulder of the giant who stood out even on this battlefield, a small, foreign old man spat out a piece of flesh that had landed in his mouth and screamed.
“Hey! To the side! Look to the side!”
But before Taishan could make sense of Namho’s shout, seven enemies rushed in from the flank, swinging Sword Energy.
Shing! Slice!
Three weapons cut through the space first, cleaving their necks and chests.
Splaash!
Amid the spray of blood, Soul-Chasing Guest Song Ilseom shook the sticky blood from his willow-leaf saber and spoke.
“Is everyone all right?”
Namho had had his mouth open and swallowed a mouthful of blood. He answered, “No. My stomach’s churning.”
Thwack!
With a horrifying impact, Taishan felled another enemy—or rather, smashed him halfway to pieces. His voice was unusually subdued.
“Namho. Don’t throw up. Not until we find the Lord.”
“Look at this little shit. Is that how you talk to an old man suffering at his age?”
“Then why’d you come? Did someone threaten you with a knife?”
Namho was at a loss for words. Ju Hwaran, cutting down enemies with movements as graceful as a dance, spoke up.
“We’re all right, too. I’m just worried about the Pavilion Master.”
Hyuk Mujin clutched his side, where a long gash had opened during the fight, and muttered, “I’m hurt, though...”
“Everyone’s fine. So stop hesitating and let’s get to the Pavilion Master.”
“No, why didn’t you even ask—”
“Pavilion Master. Danger. Urgent.”

Hyuk Mujin immediately shut his mouth. Ma Junggeol, the leader of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang, who had somehow ended up here with them, looked sadly from the dagger stuck in his thigh to Ju Hwaran and back.
“Do you have something to say?”
“Young Lady, well. It’s just...”
“You don’t.”
“...Right. Let’s say that.”
At the sight of Ju Hwaran, whose eyes had begun to gleam, Ma Junggeol lowered his head gloomily.
They were crazy.
There was no doubt about it. These people were completely insane.
Why did I come all the way here?
He didn’t know.
He’d blinked a few times, and somehow he was running with them. Before he knew it, he was fighting on the front line.
How could anyone come through a battle like this unscathed unless they were a Supreme Peak master?
He’d been slashed by a sword and stabbed with a dagger in the thick of the fighting.
But he had to keep fighting.
No—he was being told to keep fighting.
Shit...
More than ever, Ma Junggeol wished his sworn brothers were here.
Even the face of Great Sir, who did nothing but talk nonsense, floated before his eyes.
You said you’d bring him here in time. You damn bastards.
Swallowing back tears, Ma Junggeol glanced behind him for no particular reason.
The Great Snow Mountain—perhaps the last sight he’d ever see—still stood magnificent and radiant, as it always had, even after tens of thousands of unwelcome visitors had left it behind...
“Hm?”
For a moment, Ma Junggeol doubted his eyes.
It wasn’t because of the streaks of light pouring down the slopes of the Great Snow Mountain and into the battlefield one after another.
He already knew from these unsettling companions that the legendary Bow Saint had appeared.
But...
What’s that?
What caught Ma Junggeol’s eye was a golden wave flowing down the Great Snow Mountain.
The Great Snow Mountain was always white, blanketed in snow that never melted.
In spring, summer, fall, and winter.
It had been that way for a thousand years, and it would remain so a thousand years from now.
But today, at this very moment, was an exception.
Whoooosh!
The wind howled.
Snow scattered from the ground in the wake of figures that had appeared out of nowhere in the mountain range and were racing forward like streaks of light.
They ran down the steep mountainside as if it were flat ground, moving like a single wave.
A golden wave, its dazzling radiance undimmed wherever it went.
“The Embroidered Uniform Guard...!”
As someone’s cry, thick with emotion, swept across the battlefield, a thousand Embroidered Uniform Guards in golden armor raced down the mountainside like a wave, gathering speed.
All the while, one word echoed in their minds: victory.
And their commander’s voice rang clearly in their ears.
“Do you see them?”
No one answered the question from Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
Only their aura, simmering like water in a cauldron, steadily grew stronger.
“Our enemies are there. Evil men who defy the natural order and seek to plunge the world into misery.”
More than a hundred years had passed since the age of warring heroes ended and a new dynasty took its place.

The hero of the Zhu clan ascended the throne and at last became the father of all his people. His descendants, the dragon-blooded heirs, called themselves the Sons of Heaven and firmly established their authority.
From among the countless people, those with the greatest martial skill and loyalty were selected and dressed in golden robes and armor. Thus was the Embroidered Uniform Guard born.
“They have thrown the imperial court into turmoil and sought to bring down the nation ruled by His Majesty the Emperor!”
As Jeong Hogun’s voice grew stronger, a thousand pairs of eyes glinted beneath their low-set helmets.
From Zhejiang Province, where the Imperial Capital stood, all the way to Shanxi.
Then through Liaoning and Hebei—and, as though that were not enough, across half the continent to Gansu.
It had been a grueling journey.
It would be a lie to say they weren’t tired. Even the Great Nation’s finest guards of the Imperial Family did not have bodies made of steel.
But the resolve and loyalty they carried in their hearts were harder than steel and shone as brightly as gold.
Go. You are my sharpest sword and my shield. Protect the Marquis of Shangshan, benefactor of the Imperial Family, and put his enemies to the sword.
The thousand Embroidered Uniform Guards still remembered it vividly.
No—they would never forget it for as long as they lived.
The Son of Heaven they had met the day before leaving the Imperial Capital.
The smile he had worn despite his sickly complexion as he spoke of Jin Taekyung, the Marquis of Shangshan. And his final command.
Remember. His enemies are my enemies.
As the Emperor’s commanding voice echoed in their ears, Jeong Hogun cried out,
“Do you all remember the imperial command from that day?”
At their commander’s question, they answered.
In their own way.
Clang, clang, clang!
Countless weapons finally emerged into the open, glinting in the light. Beneath their helmets, their eyes shone toward the enemies drawing rapidly closer.
A thousand weapons shimmering with tangible qi.
A thousand pairs of eyes radiating suffocating fighting spirit.
And a thousand masters, each possessing both.
The enormous golden wave covered the mountainside and poured toward the battlefield.
No—it became a wave that swept away everything in its path.
Shing! KWA-BOOM!
The instant the Force arrows fired by the Bow Saint vaporized the enemy ranks—
KRAK-KOOM!
The thousand Embroidered Uniform Guards drove through the opening like awls and changed the course of the battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1047
paragraphs: If you asked what mattered most in deciding the outcome of a battle, every single person would give the same answer.
The quality of the troops—or their numbers.
But ask a general commanding an army, and he would answer differently.
He would name the two words that flashed through the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s mind at that very moment.
Momentum.
There was no doubt about it.
The enemy’s momentum—the tide of battle—had changed.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord suddenly felt the air grow hot.
Their fighting spirit, which had been fading little by little like a campfire soaked by drizzle, was flaring up again. The shouts they raised with all their strength grew louder and fiercer.
An emotion close to desperation. A resolve to face death.
Weapons swung with their final spark of life, as if their wielders had never once considered giving up.
And then—
Shwaaa!
A dazzling streak of light cut through the air ahead of them.
KWA-BOOOOM!
A flash packed with terrible destructive force swallowed dozens of Dark Heaven cultists in an instant.
The explosions of fireballs, large and small, had already opened gaps in the cultists’ ranks. Now another powerful streak of light shook their once-solid formation.
All the enemy needed was a spear to slip through that opening and pierce their heart.
Something like...
A golden spear called the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
KRAK-KOOM!
Deafening shouts mingled with thunderous booms.
The two sides collided. Blades swung like lightning, lives were lost and spared, and a thick mist of blood blanketed the area.
It took only an instant for the golden wave that had swept down the steep slopes of the Great Snow Mountain and charged onto the battlefield to turn red.
Slice! Thud-thud!
A flashing blade severed a neck in one stroke. A sharp spearhead pierced a chest.

Each guard had reached at least Supreme First Rate, and some had attained the Peak realm. That was how they had earned the honor of protecting the Imperial Family. The Great Nation’s most powerful fighting force cut and stabbed through everything in its path.
Their fierce shouts proclaimed why they had come to this battlefield.
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor! May His Highness the Imperial Younger Brother live a thousand years!”
“For the Marquis of Shangshan!”
“Attack!”
Shwish-shwish-shwish!
With the fanatically loyal guards at their head, more than twenty thousand surviving Coalition Army soldiers charged forward.
Some sought revenge for their comrades. Others fought for a greater cause.
Their reasons and aims differed, but they all wanted the same thing.
Victory.
And the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who felt the scales of battle tipping rapidly in the face of this unexpected turn, wanted a glorious victory here today just as much as they did.
“You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!”
A groan escaped through his clenched lips.
The battle was unfolding in a direction he had never expected.
The Bow Saint—and now the Embroidered Uniform Guard?
The Bow Saint was one of the Three Saints; nothing more needed to be said about her. The Embroidered Uniform Guard, directly under the Imperial Family, was the Great Nation’s sharpest sword.
His side still held the advantage in numbers, but he could no longer be sure they were stronger overall.

And now that this powerful reinforcement had restored the momentum of the more than twenty thousand enemy soldiers, they were charging wildly. Unease began to take root in one corner of the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s mind.
No... No, that can’t be.
He tried desperately to reject the word that had appeared in his mind without warning.
Defeat.
Even now, when he had become more powerful than ever, he could feel himself shrinking from the thought.
The sorcerers are still here. The Grand Sorceress is, too. If that bitch can do what she did before, we won’t be outmatched.
But why?
The enormous ball of fire that had stunned even him, though he was on her side, had not appeared again.
He sensed neither another spell nor a surge of qi heralding one.
...Why?
Could something have happened to the Grand Sorceress in that brief time?
His heart lurched, and he turned to check what was happening on the hill.
Or rather, he tried to.
Someone who had been watching him calmly spoke up.
“Things aren’t going your way, are they?”
Black Night King Sima Gong.
At the words that passed between his bloodied lips, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s face twisted like a fiend’s.
“What?”
“I understand. Sometimes things turn out that way.”
Sima Gong continued calmly, though his voice was weary. He looked at his arm—or rather, the shoulder where the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had brutally torn it away.
“Half an hour ago, I never imagined I’d end up like this either.”
He wasn’t saying that merely because he had lost an arm.
Sima Gong was half-submerged in a pool of blood. Thick blood that belonged to him alone.
Yet the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who had struck down the traitor in his path in moments, trembled with rage, not the joy of punishment.
“If it weren’t for you—if it weren’t for you...!”
Everything had gone badly wrong.
Under the original plan, Sima Gong was supposed to order the Gansu Coalition Army to retreat at the right moment, leaving the Blood-Sword Demon Lord an easy victory.
That had been their bargain.
If Sima Gong helped Dark Heaven win in Gansu, they would use the province as a foothold to seize the Central Plains. In return, they would recognize his ownership of Gansu and Shaanxi.
A secret bargain, struck on terms both sides found reasonable.
And part of it had already been carried out successfully.
Not here at the Great Snow Mountain, but in Dunhuang, at the western edge of Gansu Province.
“Was this your plan from the beginning? Did you use the Kongtong Sect—of all people—as a mere decoy, just to win today and convince us you were still our spy?”
Questions poured out of him in a rush.
There was no time to waste. He ought to have killed this traitor, whom he could have torn apart without feeling satisfied, and begun salvaging the situation at once.
But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord still could not believe his judgment had been wrong. He had to hear the answer.
The Black Night King Sima Gong he knew was an unorthodox man to the bone. To survive, he would join hands with the devil himself, let alone Dark Heaven. He was a pest worse than a bat.
That was why the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had chosen him for the bargain. Even so, he had held on to his last doubts right up until he set foot in Gansu.
Only after he won a resounding victory over the Kongtong Sect guarding Dunhuang, using the information Sima Gong had given him, had he finally let those doubts go.
“Answer me! Now!”
Anyone else would have reacted the same way.

The Kongtong Sect had resisted fiercely in Dunhuang and suffered terrible losses. No one, however willing to sacrifice the few for the many, would have dreamed of using a member of the Nine Sects and One Gang as bait for a temporary ruse.
At last, under the overwhelming aura radiating from the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, Sima Gong’s tightly closed lips parted.
“I’m not a madman. I’m too rational to commit the lunacy of betraying someone a second time. That’s why I joined hands with you.”
His words confirmed what the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had thought.
But the answer he wanted only left him with a bigger question.
“Then why the hell—”
“Why? Why did I do this? Well...”
Sima Gong cut him off. He blinked weakly and asked himself the same thing.
Why had he made such a foolish choice?
When everything had been going smoothly, why had he crossed a river he could never return from?
Then he found himself thinking of someone who was not here—and should not be—and smiled bitterly.
“Maybe I lost my mind for a little while.”
“What... did you say?”
“But it’s a damn good thing I did. It worked, didn’t it?”

That was enough for Sima Gong.
Even if he died, the Black Dragon Demon Gate would have at least some measure of absolution, enough to survive.
His heir, who wasn’t here, would live and make everything Sima Gong had passed down even stronger.
“I’m tired. Time to rest.”
The old unorthodox sect leader spoke calmly to the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who stood frozen with his eyes wide.
Then he added the one thing he had long wanted to say to the fanatic before him, the man who had betrayed the Heavenly Demon to serve a new master.
“Go ahead and kill me, you bat-like Demonic Cult bastard.”
Grind.
A chilling scrape came from between the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s clenched teeth.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord clenched his molars as if to crush them, then raised his sword, pouring his rage into its tip.
He aimed it at the traitor who had ruined a plan that should have succeeded—who had dared to throw filth across the path of the mighty Lord of Heaven.
Shwaaa!
But just as the blade, wrapped in dark-red Force, was about to fall like lightning—
Shing! KRAK-KOOM!
A streak of light flew in from somewhere and struck the flat of the blade dead on.
Slice!

Shwish-shwish-shwing!
Five streaks of light illuminated the surroundings. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gritted his teeth, and his figure blurred.
Bang! Bang! KWA-BOOOOM!

Considerable force traveled through the trembling blade into his hand, but that was all.

sentences.text: If you asked what mattered most in deciding the outcome of a battle, every single person would give the same answer.
The quality of the troops—or their numbers.
But ask a general commanding an army, and he would answer differently.
He would name the two words that flashed through the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s mind at that very moment.
Momentum.
There was no doubt about it.
The enemy’s momentum—the tide of battle—had changed.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord suddenly felt the air grow hot.
Their fighting spirit, which had been fading little by little like a campfire soaked by drizzle, was flaring up again.
The shouts they raised with all their strength grew louder and fiercer.
An emotion close to desperation.
A resolve to face death.
Weapons swung with their final spark of life, as if their wielders had never once considered giving up.
And then—
Shwaaa!
A dazzling streak of light cut through the air ahead of them.
KWA-BOOOOM!
A flash packed with terrible destructive force swallowed dozens of Dark Heaven cultists in an instant.
The explosions of fireballs, large and small, had already opened gaps in the cultists’ ranks.
Now another powerful streak of light shook their once-solid formation.
All the enemy needed was a spear to slip through that opening and pierce their heart.
Something like...
A golden spear called the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
KRAK-KOOM!
Deafening shouts mingled with thunderous booms.
The two sides collided.
Blades swung like lightning, lives were lost and spared, and a thick mist of blood blanketed the area.
It took only an instant for the golden wave that had swept down the steep slopes of the Great Snow Mountain and charged onto the battlefield to turn red.
Slice!
Thud-thud!
A flashing blade severed a neck in one stroke.
A sharp spearhead pierced a chest.
Each guard had reached at least Supreme First Rate, and some had attained the Peak realm.
That was how they had earned the honor of protecting the Imperial Family.
The Great Nation’s most powerful fighting force cut and stabbed through everything in its path.
Their fierce shouts proclaimed why they had come to this battlefield.
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!
May His Highness the Imperial Younger Brother live a thousand years!”
“For the Marquis of Shangshan!”
“Attack!”
Shwish-shwish-shwish!
With the fanatically loyal guards at their head, more than twenty thousand surviving Coalition Army soldiers charged forward.
Some sought revenge for their comrades.
Others fought for a greater cause.
Their reasons and aims differed, but they all wanted the same thing.
Victory.
And the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who felt the scales of battle tipping rapidly in the face of this unexpected turn, wanted a glorious victory here today just as much as they did.
“You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!”
A groan escaped through his clenched lips.
The battle was unfolding in a direction he had never expected.
The Bow Saint—and now the Embroidered Uniform Guard?
The Bow Saint was one of the Three Saints; nothing more needed to be said about her.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard, directly under the Imperial Family, was the Great Nation’s sharpest sword.
His side still held the advantage in numbers, but he could no longer be sure they were stronger overall.
And now that this powerful reinforcement had restored the momentum of the more than twenty thousand enemy soldiers, they were charging wildly.
Unease began to take root in one corner of the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s mind.
No...
No, that can’t be.
He tried desperately to reject the word that had appeared in his mind without warning.
Defeat.
Even now, when he had become more powerful than ever, he could feel himself shrinking from the thought.
The sorcerers are still here.
The Grand Sorceress is, too.
If that bitch can do what she did before, we won’t be outmatched.
But why?
The enormous ball of fire that had stunned even him, though he was on her side, had not appeared again.
He sensed neither another spell nor a surge of qi heralding one.
...Why?
Could something have happened to the Grand Sorceress in that brief time?
His heart lurched, and he turned to check what was happening on the hill.
Or rather, he tried to.
Someone who had been watching him calmly spoke up.
“Things aren’t going your way, are they?”
Black Night King Sima Gong.
At the words that passed between his bloodied lips, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s face twisted like a fiend’s.
“What?”
“I understand.
Sometimes things turn out that way.”
Sima Gong continued calmly, though his voice was weary.
He looked at his arm—or rather, the shoulder where the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had brutally torn it away.
“Half an hour ago, I never imagined I’d end up like this either.”
He wasn’t saying that merely because he had lost an arm.
Sima Gong was half-submerged in a pool of blood.
Thick blood that belonged to him alone.
Yet the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who had struck down the traitor in his path in moments, trembled with rage, not the joy of punishment.
“If it weren’t for you—if it weren’t for you...!”
Everything had gone badly wrong.
Under the original plan, Sima Gong was supposed to order the Gansu Coalition Army to retreat at the right moment, leaving the Blood-Sword Demon Lord an easy victory.
That had been their bargain.
If Sima Gong helped Dark Heaven win in Gansu, they would use the province as a foothold to seize the Central Plains.
In return, they would recognize his ownership of Gansu and Shaanxi.
A secret bargain, struck on terms both sides found reasonable.
And part of it had already been carried out successfully.
Not here at the Great Snow Mountain, but in Dunhuang, at the western edge of Gansu Province.
“Was this your plan from the beginning?
Did you use the Kongtong Sect—of all people—as a mere decoy, just to win today and convince us you were still our spy?”
Questions poured out of him in a rush.
There was no time to waste.

But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord still could not believe his judgment had been wrong.

The Black Night King Sima Gong he knew was an unorthodox man to the bone.

chapters.title: Chapter 1048
paragraphs: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at the two figures before him, his gaze wavering.
It was a strange sensation—one even he, a fiend who had made his mark on an entire age, had experienced only a handful of times.
Beneath a sky buried in storm clouds, countless enemies and allies were locked in a desperate battle. And yet it seemed as though those two alone filled his field of vision.
That was how much weight and meaning their titles carried: Fire King and Bow Saint.
All the more so when two living legends appeared in one place.
I can’t see an opening...
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord swallowed without realizing it.
Not a hundred enemies. Not a thousand. There were only two people before him.
And yet those two made him feel as if he were surrounded on all sides by an army of more than ten thousand.
No—the pressure was greater than that.
Step.
For an instant, three footsteps sounded together.
Jeok Cheongang and the Bow Saint slowly closed in from either side. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord instinctively stepped back, then belatedly realized what he’d done and flushed.
He’d been pushed back.
By their aura. By their fighting spirit.
And Fire King Jeok Cheongang was not the sort of man to politely overlook it.
“What happened? A moment ago, you said you’d take us all on. Changed your mind already?”
“...You damn old monster.”
“That sounds good today. Go on, say some more.”
“What?”
“Are your ears already failing you, you little brat? I said keep running your mouth.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned and continued.
He was visibly wounded, but a fierce heat still burned in his voice and on his face.
“Come to think of it, every bastard who’s talked to this old man like that has ended up dead. Every last one.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyelids quivered.
It was an obvious taunt, but he could feel that Jeok Cheongang wasn’t just putting on a show.
No matter how far he’d surpassed his former limits, it was hard to imagine him gaining the upper hand against both the Fire King and the Bow Saint at once.
Shwaak!
And then, at that very moment, a streak of light cut through the air. For all its dazzling brilliance, it was more than enough to deepen the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s unease.
Rrrr, KWA-BOOM!
A Force arrow came flying without warning.

The Blood-Sword Demon Lord reacted at once, batting away the terrifying streak of light. As he tightened his grip on the sword hilt trembling from the impact, a graceful figure emerged through the cloud of dust.
Swish.
Her steps were so light they seemed weightless.
Her dust-covered clothes fluttered, proof of the punishing journey she’d made across half the land without a moment to catch her breath.
But the woman’s face, visible above them, was flawless, and her eyes shone cold and bright as she watched her enemy beyond the dust cloud.
Three jang ahead. Three chi to the left.
So Gyo—no, the great martial artist known as the Bow Saint—shot forward and gripped her beloved weapon.
At the same time, three streaks of Force gathered along her white fingers as they flashed into motion.
Pa-pa-pat!
The dust cloud split apart. Force arrows, carrying power greater than lightning, cut through everything in their path.
Before the Blood-Sword Demon Lord could even see past them, he felt a surge of power on the other side. He swept his sword through the air with all his strength.
Whoooom!
A horizontal slash that seemed capable of cutting through even Mount Tai.
Dark-red Force swelled around the blade, then swept aside the Force arrows with speed and strength far beyond human limits.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The air burst in every direction. The Force that had swallowed the streaks of light shot straight ahead.
Rrrrmmble!
It didn’t merely shake the earth. The strike laid waste to everything in its path.
But the destructive trail of that blood-red flash held no sign of the enemies the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was looking for.
Only two different whistles tore in from a blind spot.
Fwoosh! Shing!
In a world that seemed to slow, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
One attack was as fierce as could be. The other was so stealthy it raised goose bumps.
Their energies were opposites—he could tell that from the sound alone. But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord knew better than anyone what they had in common.
If I let even one strike through, it’s over.
How many martial artists in this vast land could withstand the attacks coming at him now, even if the whole world were turned upside down?
The Fire King and the Bow Saint.
The Bow Saint and the Fire King.
They weren’t merely relics of a distant past.
They had written their own legends then, and carried those legends into the present. In the distant future, countless storytellers would sing of their deeds and praise them.
That was how legends lasted. How giants were remembered forever.
And perhaps, here today, a new verse would be written in that legend.
Two great martial artists had felled the fiend known as the Blood-Sword Demon Lord on the open plain of the Great Snow Mountain, amid blood and snow.
But...
That will never happen.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord clenched his teeth. As the flow of time slowly returned, he pushed every ounce of strength and every sense he possessed to its limit and twisted his body.
He moved with an agility he doubted he could ever summon again in his life.
Slice!
A sudden, burning pain ran along his arm and the side of his neck.
The Bow Saint.
She had separated her beloved weapon, which had been shaped like a bow, into two curved swords. She had already passed him by.
With two flashes of those blades, swung stealthily yet swiftly as lightning, she had torn away part of his nape and the shoulder of his left arm.
But an attack that should have taken his life outright had done surprisingly little. Before the pain could fully register, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord felt an appalling heat rush at him from the side.
Fwoosh! Poom!
Hng...!
It all happened almost at once.
Jeok Cheongang’s Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist swept fiercely past his flank.
That glancing blow alone melted away a fistful of flesh.
And the unbearable pain made the Blood-Sword Demon Lord suck in a breath and stop moving without realizing it.
But that was all.
At that moment, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was cheering deep down because he had survived.
Even though the Bow Saint had taken one of his arms, and the heat from Jeok Cheongang’s fist had melted part of his flank and reached his innards as well.
That’s enough.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had something to fall back on. Injuries like these were bearable.

What mattered more than anything was that he hadn’t fallen to the combined attack of the Fire King and the Bow Saint—and that, unlike them, who had already missed their perfect chance, he still had one move left.
I’ll kill them. I swear it!
A decisive strike always left an opening.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord suppressed the pain surging through him and brought his sword down at Jeok Cheongang, who watched him with eyes wide.
No—more precisely, he tried to.
Before he could, someone moved with a desperate resolve equal to—or perhaps greater than—his own moments earlier.
Thuk!
A fierce, unexpected pain shot through him. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord staggered, then stared in disbelief at the dark blade buried deep in his ankle—and at the face of the man holding it.
Black Night King Sima Gong.
“You son of a—”
The moment he managed to force out a groan—
“I told you. Every last one of them died.”
Poom! Krrrcrack!
At Jeok Cheongang’s cold voice, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s vision flipped over.
The dark sky. The ground covered in blood and snow. The countless people fighting and killing one another across it.
Everything turned blindingly white, then red.
Flame Divine Palm.
Unlike Jeok Cheongang’s cold voice, the dreadful heat melted flesh and broke bones as it sank deep into his body. Trapped by the excruciating pain, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord could do nothing.
But an unexpected stroke of luck awaited him—one even he hadn’t foreseen.
KWA-BOOM! KWA-BOOM! Krrrcrack!
His body shot away like a cannonball, unable to withstand the tremendous force. It rolled and crashed along the ground before finally slamming into something.
“Well.”
As the Blood-Sword Demon Lord spat blood mixed with bits of his innards, a voice drifted faintly into his ear.
“You’ve been badly hurt, Demon Lord.”
Was he hearing things?
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord blinked weakly as he wondered. Then he realized the slope beneath his battered body was a hillside, and that the voice he’d just heard sounded uncannily familiar.
“Guh, hahahaha!”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord burst out laughing without meaning to.
Bloody phlegm bubbled in his throat, and every time his body shook with laughter, tremendous jolts of pain shot through his broken limbs. He didn’t care in the least.
He laughed like a madman.
Like the happiest person in the world. Like someone who had been rescued at the very edge of death.
Trembling with joy, he stretched a bloodied hand toward his savior.
No—he gave his subordinate an order.
“Heal me. Right now.”
The savior, the Grand Sorceress, gazed silently at the Blood-Sword Demon Lord. She slowly parted her lips to speak—
Shwaak!
A streak of light whistled through the air. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
Beyond the Grand Sorceress’s shoulder, he saw a young man hauling himself up from where he had fallen. His eyes blazing, the young man brought his spearhead down.
There was not even a thread of internal energy in it. No trace of his usual strength or speed.
Jin Taekyung was squeezing out every last bit of strength he had left for a strike with all his might.
That crazy bastard...!
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord screamed soundlessly.
Clang!
An invisible barrier around the Grand Sorceress knocked away the silver-white spearhead.
It did so with astonishing ease, as if mocking the desperate hope behind the blow.
And then—
That was all.
Thud.
The spear shaft rolled from its owner’s powerless hand.
In the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes, still wide with shock, a figure slowly began to topple.
Thump.
The body finally crumpled.
Jin Taekyung lay in a wretched heap, glaring weakly at him. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord sucked in a breath without realizing it.
You stubborn bastard.
He’d already reached his limit, and still he’d waited for a chance to strike.
His persistence was so terrifying it inspired awe—or rather, sent a chill down the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s spine.
But...
That desperate struggle ends here.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord bared his bloodied teeth in a grin.
If he were his former self—or even just a flesh-and-blood human—those injuries would have killed him several times over.
But his body, strengthened to an extreme degree, had granted him a brief handful of moments. Those moments would change everyone’s fate.
The Fire King and the Bow Saint, both rushing here with all their strength even now.
The tens of thousands of enemies and allies swinging their weapons amid the sea of corpses and blood.
And, most important of all, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s own life and death.
“It’s time... to put an end to this damned battle.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord forced out the words, his breathing noticeably more labored. The Grand Sorceress nodded calmly.
“Of course.”
At that moment—
Fwoosh.
A brilliant light spread from the Grand Sorceress’s fingertips.
A healing light, warm as the midday sun and clear as a pond deep in the mountains.
Ah.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s eyes closed without his meaning to.
For a moment, he let himself sink into the peace the light brought.
Then, after a moment that felt both brief and eternal, he opened his eyes.
He stared, unable to believe what he saw.
“What... is this?”
His body was still horribly mangled, not healed in the slightest.
And someone else, wrapped in the fading glow, was breathing more steadily than before.
No.
Jin Taekyung.
